# Required

Load the `here` package and source the project-wide library and utility script.

```{r}
# Install R package from CRAN
install.packages("here")
library(here)
source(here("scripts_notebooks", "required.R"))
```


# Preprocessing

#===================

# 1. Fluad + MF59, Vaccine

## Mouse
### Download dataset

Download the Fluad/MF59 mouse dataset (GSE120661) from GEO. Extract metadata from the ExpressionSet, save it as a CSV, then extract and save the raw expression matrix.

```{r eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, cache = TRUE}
# Download the GEO ExpressionSet
filename = "GSE120661"
GSE120661 <- getGEO("GSE120661", GSEMatrix = TRUE) 
eset <- GSE120661[[1]]

# Clean and save metadata
GSE120661_metadata = eset %>% 
  pData() %>% 
# Reorder columns
  dplyr::select( 
    geo_sample = "geo_accession", 
    subject_id = "title",
    sex = "gender:ch1", 
    treatment = "treatment:ch1", 
    tissue = "tissue:ch1",
    timepoint = "timepoint:ch1",
    animal_replicate = "animal replicate:ch1",
    strain = "strain/background:ch1") %>% 
# Relevel treatment factor: set saline/control as the reference level for proper contrast encoding
  mutate(treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "saline"),
         timepoint = fct_relevel(timepoint, "0"),
         condition = paste(treatment, timepoint, tissue, sep = "_"))

#Save
write_csv(GSE120661_metadata, file = here("tables", "influenza_hepatitisb_GSE120661_metadata.csv"))

# Extract and save expression matrix
eset <- exprs(eset)

#Save
eset %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  saveRDS(here("tables", "influenza_hepatitisb_GSE120661_exprs.rds"))

```


Inspect the distribution of expression values for one representative sample (GSM3407136) to confirm the data are on the log2 scale.

```{r eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, cache = TRUE}
# Load the expression matrix
GSE120661_exprs = readRDS(here("tables", "influenza_hepatitisb_GSE120661_exprs.rds"))
GSE120661_counts_not_normalized_log2 = readRDS(here("tables","influenza_hepatitisb_GSE120661_exprs.rds"))

# Pivot to long format
GSE120661_exprs_distribution = GSE120661_exprs %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probes") %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = -probes,
               names_to = "sample_id",
               values_to = "value") 

# Plot expression histogram for the first sample
GSE120661_exprs_distribution %>% 
  filter(sample_id == "GSM3407136") %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = value) +
  geom_histogram()
```


Get metadata
Reload and clean the metadata for the current condition.

Reload the metadata, clean factor levels (timepoint as integer, treatment releveled with saline as reference), and create a unified condition column.

```{r}
# Load raw metadata
GSE120661_metadata = read_csv(here("tables", "influenza_hepatitisb_GSE120661_metadata.csv")) 

# Clean factor levels
GSE120661_metadata = GSE120661_metadata %>% 
  mutate(timepoint = as.integer(timepoint) %>% 
           as.character() %>% 
           as.factor() %>% 
           fct_relevel(., "0"),
         treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "saline"),
         condition = paste(treatment, timepoint, tissue, sep = "_"))

#Save
GSE120661_metadata %>% saveRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_metadata.rds"))
```

Import
Load the required data objects from disk.

Filter the mouse metadata to Fluad-treated PBMC samples only, recode timepoints from hours to days, select the corresponding expression columns, and save both the filtered metadata and expression matrix.

```{r}
# Load metadata and expression
GSE120661_metadata = readRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_metadata.rds"))
GSE120661_exprs = read_rds(here("tables", "influenza_hepatitisb_GSE120661_exprs.rds"))

# Check probe count
GSE120661_exprs %>% rownames() %>% length()

# Filter to Fluad PBMC samples, recode timepoint (hours to days)
mouse_fluad_metadata = GSE120661_metadata %>% 
# Filter to the treatment of interest: removes control/saline samples from this branch
  filter(treatment == "Fluad",
         tissue == "PBMC") %>% 
  mutate(timepoint = as.character(timepoint) %>% as.numeric(),
         timepoint = (timepoint / 24) %>% round(1),
         participant_id = paste0("TriFLU-MF59_BL", animal_replicate)) %>% 
# Keep only the specified timepoints of interest: removes irrelevant intermediate timepoints
  filter(timepoint %in% c(0, 1, 3, 7))

#Save
mouse_fluad_metadata %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_metadata.rds"))

# Subset expression matrix to selected samples
GSE120661_exprs = GSE120661_exprs %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  select(c(mouse_fluad_metadata$geo_sample)) %>% 
  as.matrix()

#Save
GSE120661_exprs %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_exprs.rds"))
```

### Annotate genes

Map Agilent probe IDs to human gene symbols using Ensembl BioMart and the FIT.mouse2man orthology lookup table.

```{r}
# Set up Ensembl BioMart for mouse
ensembl_mart <- useMart("ensembl")
# Select the mouse genome (mmusculus_gene_ensembl) as the annotation dataset in BioMart
ensembl_mart <- useDataset("mmusculus_gene_ensembl", mart = ensembl_mart)

# Get probe IDs from the expression matrix
gene_id <- GSE120661_counts_not_normalized_log2 %>% rownames()

# List available attributes
listAttributes(ensembl_mart)

# Retrieve annotations for all probes
# Query BioMart for gene annotations (Ensembl → HGNC/MGI symbols)
annot <- getBM(
  attributes = c("agilent_sureprint_g3_ge_8x60k", #Agilent microarray data (design ID 028005, retrieved from GEO)
                 "ensembl_gene_id",
                 "entrezgene_id",
                 "mgi_symbol",
                 "description"),
  filters = "agilent_sureprint_g3_ge_8x60k",
  values = gene_id,
  mart = ensembl_mart)

# Load mouse-to-human orthology lookup table
library(FIT.mouse2man)
HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez = FIT.mouse2man::HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(mouse_entrez = mouse_ortholog)

# Summarise expression per probe, collapse to one row per gene
### Filter probes with highest median expression
mouse_fluad_log2summary = GSE120661_exprs %>% #20,845 probes
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe") %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -probe,
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "expression") %>% 
# Group by probe ID to collapse multiple probe-to-gene mappings later
  group_by(probe) %>% 
# Compute per-probe summary statistics (mean, median) across all samples to select the most representative probe
  summarise(mean = mean(expression,na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(expression, na.rm = T)) %>%  
  # Join BioMart annotation to expression data
inner_join(annot %>% 
              rename(probe = agilent_sureprint_g3_ge_8x60k), 
            by = "probe") %>%  #24.009 rows
  # Collapse multiple probes per Ensembl ID (keep highest median)
  group_by(ensembl_gene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-ensembl_gene_id) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  group_by(entrezgene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%  #21.863 probes/entrez_ids
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(mouse_entrez = entrezgene_id) %>% 
  
  # Join human orthologs, collapse to one row per HGNC symbol
  inner_join(HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez, by = c("mouse_entrez", "mgi_symbol")) %>% 
  group_by(hgnc_symbol) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1)  %>% #14.396
  ungroup()

# Remove HGNC symbols that map to multiple MGI symbols
hgnc_symbol_dupes = mouse_fluad_log2summary %>% 
# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
  get_dupes(hgnc_symbol)

mouse_fluad_log2summary = mouse_fluad_log2summary %>% 
# Remove genes with ambiguous human symbol mappings: retains only one-to-one mouse-to-human orthologs
  filter(!hgnc_symbol %in% c(hgnc_symbol_dupes$hgnc_symbol %>% unique())) 

# Build filtered expression matrix with human gene symbols
mouse_fluad_log2_filtered_probes = GSE120661_exprs %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe") %>% 
# Join expression data with annotation by probe ID: adds gene symbols to raw probe-level measurements
  inner_join(mouse_fluad_log2summary, by = "probe") %>%   #214,396
  select(human_symbol = hgnc_symbol,
         human_entrez,
         mouse_entrez,
         c(mouse_fluad_metadata$geo_sample))
#14395
mouse_fluad_log2_filtered_probes %>% dim()

mouse_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol = mouse_fluad_log2_filtered_probes 

# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
mouse_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% get_dupes(human_symbol)

#Save 
mouse_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
```
Create expression set
Build an ExpressionSet with the expression matrix and phenotype data.

Reshape the annotated expression matrix to long format, compute log2 fold-change relative to day 0 for each participant and gene, and save in both long and wide formats.

```{r}
# Load annotation and metadata
mouse_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
mouse_fluad_metadata = readRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_metadata.rds")) 

# Pivot to long, add metadata, compute log2 fold-change vs day 0
mouse_fluad_log2fc_filtered_sample_long = mouse_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol %>%
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -human_symbol,
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "log2") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(mouse_fluad_metadata %>% 
               select(geo_sample, participant_id, timepoint),
             by = "geo_sample") %>% 
  select(participant_id, human_symbol,  timepoint, value = log2) %>%
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
    distinct() %>% 
  # Reshape to wide format with one column per timepoint
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value, names_prefix = "day_") %>%
# Reshape columns from wide to long using a common prefix pattern: separates metric type from timepoint via names_pattern
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("day_"),
               names_to = "timepoint",
               names_prefix = "day_",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(participant_id, human_symbol) %>% 
# Extract baseline (day 0) expression value for each participant × gene pair: reference for fold-change calculation
  mutate(day0 = value[timepoint == "0"]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Compute log2 fold-change relative to baseline
mutate(log2fc = value - day0) %>%
# Remove baseline rows: only post-vaccination/infection timepoints are relevant for differential expression analysis
  filter(timepoint != "0")

#Save
mouse_fluad_log2fc_filtered_sample_long %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))

# Pivot to wide format (participants as columns)
mouse_fluad_log2fc_filtered_sample_wide = mouse_fluad_log2fc_filtered_sample_long %>% 
  select(-c(value:day0)) %>% 
# Widen data: reshape so that each timepoint becomes a separate column (required format for t-test input)
  pivot_wider(names_from = "participant_id",
              values_from = "log2fc")

# Play notification sound: alerts that a long-running chunk has finished execution
beep()

```

### Differential gene expression

Build an ExpressionSet from the filtered gene-symbol expression matrix with quantile normalization.

```{r}
# Create ExpressionSet
# Load data
mouse_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
mouse_fluad_metadata = readRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_metadata.rds")) 

# Build expression matrix
GSE120661_exprs_matrix_fluad = mouse_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  select(human_symbol, c(mouse_fluad_metadata$geo_sample)) %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
  column_to_rownames("human_symbol") %>% 
  as.matrix()

# Quantile normalization
GSE120661_exprs_matrix_fluad_normalized <- normalizeBetweenArrays(GSE120661_exprs_matrix_fluad, 
                                                                    method = "quantile")

# Diagnostics
dim(GSE120661_exprs_matrix_fluad_normalized) #14357   20

# Convert metadata to AnnotatedDataFrame: formal phenotype data structure required by ExpressionSet
dim(AnnotatedDataFrame(mouse_fluad_metadata %>% column_to_rownames("geo_sample"))) #35

# Create new ExpressionSet with normalized data
eset_filtered <- ExpressionSet(
  assayData = GSE120661_exprs_matrix_fluad_normalized,
# Convert metadata to AnnotatedDataFrame: formal phenotype data structure required by ExpressionSet
  phenoData = AnnotatedDataFrame(mouse_fluad_metadata %>%
                                   mutate(timepoint = as.character(timepoint) %>% as.factor()) %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
                                   column_to_rownames("geo_sample")))
```


#### Limma

Fit a linear model with array weights, duplicate correlation, and empirical Bayes moderation to identify differentially expressed genes at each timepoint vs day 0.

```{r}
# Create design matrix
eset_mouse_fluad = readRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_eset.rds"))

# Filter low-expressed genes (log2 > 6 in at least 5 samples)
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_mouse_fluad) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>% 
  rowSums() %>% 
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_mouse_fluad[genes_to_keep, ]

# Build design matrix for Limma with condition and covariates
design <- model.matrix(~ timepoint + 0, eset_filtered)
# Ensure syntactically valid column names: replaces spaces/special characters with dots for model.matrix compatibility
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))

# Estimate correlation between samples from the same individual
corfit <- duplicateCorrelation(eset_filtered, 
                               design = design, 
                               block = eset_filtered$participant_id)
corfit$consensus #0.024

# Array weights
# Calculate sample quality weights
aw <- arrayWeights(eset_filtered, design)

# Barplot of array weights
barplot(aw, 
        names.arg = eset_filtered$condition,
        main = "Sample Weights Diagnostic", 
        ylab = "Weight", 
        las = 2,
        cex.names = 0.7,
        col = "skyblue")

# Fit linear model
# Fit linear model with array weights and duplicate correlation
fit <- lmFit(eset_filtered, 
             design, 
             weights = aw,
             block = eset_filtered$participant_id, 
             correlation = corfit$consensus
             ) 

# Define contrasts
colnames(design) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  arrange(.)

# Define contrasts of interest (each timepoint vs baseline)
cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(timepoint1  - timepoint0 ,
                             timepoint3  - timepoint0 ,
                             timepoint7  - timepoint0 ,
                             levels=design)

# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont.matrix)

# Empirical Bayes moderation
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink variances
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2, trend = T, robust = T)

# Diagnostic plot: scatterplot of log2 residual variance vs average expression (should show no strong trend after moderation)
plotSA(fit2, main = "Sigma vs Abundance (Weights Applied)")

# Extract DEGs for every contrast
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2), function(i) {
  
# Extract differentially expressed genes using the treat method (tests whether log2FC exceeds a minimum threshold, not just non-zero)
  topTreat(fit2, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(comparison = colnames(fit2)[i]) %>% 
    rownames_to_column("symbol")
    
})

# Combine all results
all_contrasts_degs <- bind_rows(results_list)

# Clean and organise DEG table
all_degs_mouse = all_contrasts_degs %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  select(comparison, everything()) %>% 
  mutate(comparison = stringr::str_replace(comparison, "\\.\\.\\.", "_") %>% 
           str_replace(., "timepoint", "Time") %>% 
           str_replace(., "treatment", "")) %>% 
# Split contrast name into comparison and reference columns (e.g. 'Time1 - Time0' → comparisonA / comparisonRef)
  separate(comparison, sep = " - ", into = c("comparisonA", "comparisonRef")) %>% 
  mutate(comparisonRef = str_replace(comparisonRef, "treatment", "Time0")) %>% 
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  mutate(condition = case_when(comparisonA == "Time1"	~ "Fluad_1_PBMC",
                                comparisonA == "Time3"	~ "Fluad_3_PBMC",
                                comparisonA == "Time7"	~ "Fluad_7_PBMC",
                                T~comparisonA),
         timepoint = str_remove(comparisonA, "Time"),
         organism = "Mouse") %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(condition, everything()) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(condition, human_symbol = symbol, mean_l2fc = log_fc, ci_lower = ci_l, ci_upper = ci_r, ave_expr,  everything())

all_degs_mouse %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
# Count the number of differentially expressed genes (adj.p ≤ 0.05) per comparison
  summarise(n_degs = n())
	
#Save
all_degs_mouse %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))


```



#### Simple t-Test

Perform paired and unpaired t-tests comparing each post-vaccination timepoint to day 0 for every gene, then combine and save the results.

```{r}
# Load log2 fold-change and expression data
mouse_fluad_log2fc_filtered_sample_long = 
# Load dataset from disk or GEO: reads pre-saved expression matrix / metadata into the R environment
  readRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))
mouse_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds")) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct()

# Pivot to wide format (one column per timepoint)
mouse_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol_wide = mouse_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol %>%
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -human_symbol,
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "log2") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(mouse_fluad_metadata %>% 
               select(geo_sample, participant_id, timepoint),
             by = "geo_sample") %>% 
  select(human_symbol, participant_id, timepoint, log2) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  select(participant_id, human_symbol, timepoint, value = log2) %>%
  # Reshape to wide format with one column per timepoint
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value, names_prefix = "day_") 

# Paired t-test per gene
mouse_fluad_log2fc_paired_ttest <- mouse_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_day1 = tryCatch(t.test(day_1, day_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_day3 = tryCatch(t.test(day_3, day_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_day7 = tryCatch(t.test(day_7, day_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_day1 = p.adjust(pval_day1, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day3 = p.adjust(pval_day3, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day7 = p.adjust(pval_day7, method = "fdr")
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(day\d+)"
  ) %>% 
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  mutate(condition = case_when(timepoint == "day1"	~ "Fluad_24_PBMC",
                                timepoint == "day3"	~ "Fluad_72_PBMC",
                                timepoint == "day7"	~ "Fluad_168_PBMC",
                                T~timepoint),
         timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "day"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Paired")

# Unpaired t-test per gene
mouse_fluad_log2fc_unpaired_ttest <- mouse_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_day1 = tryCatch(t.test(day_1, day_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_day3 = tryCatch(t.test(day_3, day_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_day7 = tryCatch(t.test(day_7, day_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_day1 = p.adjust(pval_day1, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day3 = p.adjust(pval_day3, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day7 = p.adjust(pval_day7, method = "fdr")
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(day\d+)"
  ) %>% 
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  mutate(condition = case_when(timepoint == "day1"	~ "Fluad_24_PBMC",
                                timepoint == "day3"	~ "Fluad_72_PBMC",
                                timepoint == "day7"	~ "Fluad_168_PBMC",
                                T~timepoint),
         timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "day"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Unpaired")

# Combine paired and unpaired results
mouse_fluad_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest = mouse_fluad_log2fc_paired_ttest %>% 
  bind_rows(mouse_fluad_log2fc_unpaired_ttest) 

#Save
mouse_fluad_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds"))

```

## Human

### Download dataset

Data was quantile normalized signal intensity using limma 3.38.3, read.maimages source = agilent.median, backgroundCorrect method = normexp, normalizeBetweenArrays method = quantile (Ref: GEO).

```{r eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, cache = TRUE}
# Download GSE124689 from GEO
GSE124689 <- getGEO("GSE124689", GSEMatrix = TRUE) 
# Extract ExpressionSet
eset <- GSE124689[[1]]
# Expression matrix
GSE124689_exprs <- eset %>% exprs()
# Metadata
GSE124689_metadata = eset %>% pData()
#Save
GSE124689_exprs %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "influenza_human_GSE124689_exprs.rds"))
```

### Annotate features

Map Agilent probe IDs to Entrez IDs and gene symbols via the platform annotation file, collapse multiple probes per gene by highest median expression, and save both Entrez-ID-based and symbol-based expression matrices.

```{r eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, cache = TRUE}
# Load platform annotation
probes_annotation <- read.delim(here("tables", "GPL21272-58809.txt"), skip = 19, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", quote = "") %>% 
  select(gene_id = ID, entrez_id = ENTREZ_GENE_ID, ensembl_id = ENSEMBL_ID, gene_symbol = GENE_SYMBOL) %>% 
  mutate(gene_id = as.character(gene_id))

# Join expression with annotation
GSE124689_counts <- GSE124689_exprs %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>% 
# Join BioMart gene annotation to expression data by probe ID: adds gene symbol, Entrez ID, and description
  inner_join(probes_annotation, by = "gene_id") %>% 
  select(gene_id, entrez_id, ensembl_id, gene_symbol, c(human_samples_pbmc_fluad$biosample_accession)) %>% 
  mutate(entrez_id = as.character(entrez_id)) 

# Collapse multiple probes per Entrez ID (keep highest median)
GSE124689_counts_genes_selected = GSE124689_counts %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long format, keeping gene identifiers as keys
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(gene_id, entrez_id, ensembl_id, gene_symbol),
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "expression") %>% 
# Group by Entrez gene ID: collapse multiple Ensembl IDs per Entrez ID after orthology mapping
  group_by(entrez_id, gene_id) %>% 
  drop_na(entrez_id) %>% 
  summarise(median = median(expression),
            median = round(median, 10)) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>% 
  ungroup()

# Merge back with full data
GSE124689_counts_raw = GSE124689_counts %>% 
  inner_join(GSE124689_counts_genes_selected %>% 
               select(gene_id, entrez_id),
             by = join_by("gene_id", "entrez_id"))

# Remove duplicate Entrez IDs by random sampling
dupes_entrez = GSE124689_counts_genes_selected %>% 
# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
  get_dupes(entrez_id) %>% 
# Group by Entrez gene ID: collapse multiple Ensembl IDs per Entrez ID after orthology mapping
  group_by(entrez_id) %>% 
# Randomly select one representative entry from each group of duplicates (last resort for ambiguous mappings)
  slice_sample(n = 1)

# Build Entrez-ID-based expression matrix
human_fluadd_not_normalized = GSE124689_counts_raw %>%
  select(-gene_symbol) %>% 
  filter(!gene_id %in% c(dupes_entrez$gene_id)) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  select(c(entrez_id, human_samples_pbmc_fluad$uid)) %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
  column_to_rownames("entrez_id") 

#Save
human_fluadd_not_normalized %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_GSE124689_exprs.rds"))

# Repeat collapse by gene symbol
GSE124689_counts_genes_selected_symbol = GSE124689_counts %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long format, keeping gene identifiers as keys
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(gene_id, entrez_id, ensembl_id, gene_symbol),
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "expression") %>% 
  group_by(gene_symbol, gene_id) %>% 
  filter(gene_symbol != "") %>% 
  drop_na(gene_symbol) %>% 
  summarise(median = median(expression),
            median = round(median, 10)) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>% 
  ungroup()

GSE124689_counts_raw_symbol = GSE124689_counts %>% 
  inner_join(GSE124689_counts_genes_selected_symbol %>% 
               select(gene_id, gene_symbol),
             by = join_by("gene_id", "gene_symbol"))

# Remove duplicate gene symbols
dupes_symbols = GSE124689_counts_genes_selected_symbol %>% 
# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
  get_dupes(gene_symbol) %>% 
  group_by(gene_symbol) %>% 
# Randomly select one representative entry from each group of duplicates (last resort for ambiguous mappings)
  slice_sample(n = 1)

# Build symbol-based expression matrix
human_fluadd_not_normalized_symbol = GSE124689_counts_raw_symbol %>%
  filter(!gene_symbol %in% c(dupes_symbols$gene_symbol)) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  select(c(gene_symbol, human_samples_pbmc_fluad$uid)) %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
  column_to_rownames("gene_symbol")

# Save symbol-to-Entrez lookup
human_fluadd_symbol_entrez = GSE124689_counts_raw_symbol %>%
  filter(!gene_symbol %in% c(dupes_symbols$gene_symbol)) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  select(symbol = gene_symbol, entrez_id)

#Save
human_fluadd_not_normalized_symbol %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_GSE124689_exprs_not_normalized.rds"))

# Inspect results
human_fluadd_not_normalized_symbol %>% 
  rownames_to_column("human_symbol") %>% 
  pivot_longer(columns_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "log2fc")

human_fluadd_not_normalized_symbol
```

### Unite and normalize with human

Combine the human and mouse expression matrices by shared gene symbols, apply quantile normalization across species, and save the joint ExpressionSet.

```{r}
# Filter out duplicated MGI symbols
filter_out_mgi = GSE120661_counts_not_normalized_log2_annotations %>% 
  select(mgi_symbol) %>% 
# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
  get_dupes()

# Clean mouse symbol table
GSE120661_counts_not_normalized_log2_symbol = GSE120661_counts_not_normalized_log2_annotations %>% 
  select(-probe, -entrezgene_id) %>% #21,856 rows
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>%  #21,666 rows
  filter(mgi_symbol != c(filter_out_mgi$mgi_symbol)) %>% #21,557 rows
  mutate(mgi_symbol = str_to_upper(mgi_symbol)) %>% 
  rename(symbol = mgi_symbol)

# Join human and mouse matrices by symbol, quantile normalize
human_mouse_fluad_matrix = GSE124689_expression_not_normalized_log2_raw_symbol %>%

  column_to_rownames("symbol") %>% 
  select(human_mouse_fluad_metadata %>% 
           pull(sample_id)) %>% 
  as.matrix() %>% 
# Apply quantile normalisation between arrays: makes expression distributions identical across all samples, reducing technical variation
  normalizeBetweenArrays(method = "quantile")

human_mouse_fluad_df = human_mouse_fluad_matrix %>%
```

#### Limma

##### All samples

Fit a Limma model with array weights, duplicate correlation, and empirical Bayes moderation to identify DEGs in human Fluad response at days 1, 3, and 7 vs day 0.

```{r All samples}
# Load ExpressionSet
eset_human = readRDS(file = here("tables", "fluad_eset_human.rds"))

# Filter low-expressed genes (log2 > 6 in at least 5 samples)
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_human) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>% 
  rowSums() %>% 
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_human[genes_to_keep, ]

# Create design matrix with covariates
design <- model.matrix(~ condition + sex + age + race + 0, eset_filtered) 
# Ensure syntactically valid column names: replaces spaces/special characters with dots for model.matrix compatibility
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))

# Estimate intra-individual correlation
corfit <- duplicateCorrelation(eset_filtered, 
                               design = design, 
                               block = eset_filtered$participant_id)
corfit$consensus #0.11

# Array weights
aw <- arrayWeights(eset_filtered, design)
# Barplot of array weights: visual diagnostic to identify low-quality arrays (bars near zero indicate problematic samples)
barplot(aw, 
        names.arg = eset_filtered$condition,
        main = "Sample Weights Diagnostic", 
        ylab = "Weight", 
        las = 2,           
        cex.names = 0.7,   
        col = "skyblue")

# Fit linear model
fluad_human_limma_fit <- lmFit(eset_filtered, 
             design, 
             weights = aw,
                             block = eset_filtered$participant_id, 
                             correlation = corfit$consensus)

# Define contrasts
colnames(design) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  arrange(.)

# Define contrasts of interest: specify which group means to subtract (e.g. Treatment − Control) to test specific hypotheses
cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(conditionFLUADD.Day.1 - conditionFLUADD.Day.0,
                             conditionFLUADD.Day.3 - conditionFLUADD.Day.0,
                             conditionFLUADD.Day.7 - conditionFLUADD.Day.0,
                             levels=design)

# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fluad_human_limma_fit, cont.matrix)

# Empirical Bayes moderation
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2, 
               robust = T, 
               trend = T)

# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
fit2 %>% saveRDS(here("tables","fluad_human_limma_fit.rds"))

# Diagnostic plot: scatterplot of log2 residual variance vs average expression (should show no strong trend after moderation)
plotSA(fit2, main = "Sigma vs Abundance (Weights Applied)")

# Load results (re-run if needed)
fit2 = readRDS(here("tables","fluad_human_limma_fit.rds"))

# Extract DEGs for every contrast
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2), function(i) {
# Extract differentially expressed genes using the treat method (tests whether log2FC exceeds a minimum threshold, not just non-zero)
  topTreat(fit2, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(comparison = colnames(fit2)[i]) %>% 
    rownames_to_column("symbol")
  })

# Combine all results
all_contrasts_degs <- bind_rows(results_list)

# Clean and organise DEG table
fluad_human_degs = all_contrasts_degs %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  select(comparison, everything()) %>% 
  mutate(comparison = str_replace_all(comparison, "\.", " "),
        comparison = str_replace_all(comparison, "condition", "")) %>% 
# Split contrast name into comparison and reference columns (e.g. 'Time1 - Time0' → comparisonA / comparisonRef)
  separate(comparison, sep = " - ", into = c("comparisonA", "comparisonRef")) %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(condition = comparisonA, everything()) %>% 
  select(-comparisonRef) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(condition, symbol, mean = log_fc, lower = ci_l, upper = ci_r, ave_expr,
         everything()) %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(human_mouse_fluad_metadata_pData %>% 
               select(condition, timepoint, vaccine, sample_type) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
               distinct(), by = "condition") %>% 
# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human") 

#Save
fluad_human_degs %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_human_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

# Summarise number of DEGs per condition
fluad_human_degs %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
# Count the number of differentially expressed genes (adj.p ≤ 0.05) per comparison
  summarise(n_degs = n())
```

##### Subsampling

Demonstrate a single subsampling iteration: randomly select 5 human participants while ensuring all 4 timepoints are present and demographic covariates remain non-uniform, then run Limma and extract DEGs.

```{r Subsampling example}
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(tidyverse)
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(limma)
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(here)
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(janitor)

# Load ExpressionSet
eset_human <- readRDS(file = here("tables", "fluad_eset_human.rds"))
human_mouse_fluad_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_human_mouse_metadata.rds"))

# Filter low-expressed genes
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_human) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>% 
  rowSums() %>% 
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_human[genes_to_keep, ]
meta_df <- as_tibble(pData(eset_filtered), rownames = "sample_id")
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
expr_matrix <- exprs(eset_filtered)
unique_participants <- meta_df %>% dplyr::pull(participant_id) %>% unique()

# Defensive subsampling function supporting missing data
draw_flexible_subset <- function(participants_list, metadata, target_n = 5) {
  valid_draw <- FALSE
  attempts <- 0
  
  while(!valid_draw) {
    attempts <- attempts + 1
    if(attempts > 500) stop("Could not find a balanced subset. Please check metadata variance.")
    
    selected_ids <- sample(participants_list, size = target_n, replace = FALSE)
    
    sub_meta <- metadata %>% 
      filter(participant_id %in% selected_ids) %>%
      mutate(condition = as.factor(condition),
             sex = as.factor(sex),
             race = as.factor(race))
    
    has_all_timepoints <- (length(unique(sub_meta$condition)) == 4)
    diverse_sex  <- (length(unique(sub_meta$sex)) > 1)
    diverse_race <- (length(unique(sub_meta$race)) > 1)
    
    if(has_all_timepoints && diverse_sex && diverse_race) {
      valid_draw = TRUE
    }
  }
  return(sub_meta)
}

# Execute the controlled test iteration
set.seed(42)

sub_meta <- draw_flexible_subset(unique_participants, meta_df, target_n = 5)
sub_expr <- expr_matrix[, sub_meta$sample_id]

# Resilient linear modeling via Limma
design_sub <- model.matrix(~ condition + sex + age + race + 0, data = sub_meta)
colnames(design_sub) <- make.names(colnames(design_sub))

# Estimate within-subject correlation for repeated measures: samples from the same individual are more similar than samples across individuals
corfit_sub <- duplicateCorrelation(sub_expr, design = design_sub, block = sub_meta$participant_id)
cat("Consensus intra-individual correlation for this specific round:", corfit_sub$consensus, "
")

# Estimate sample-specific quality weights using arrayWeights: down-weights arrays with excessive noise to improve statistical power
aw_sub <- arrayWeights(sub_expr, design_sub)

# Fit linear model with array weights and duplicate correlation
fit_sub <- lmFit(sub_expr, 
                 design = design_sub, 
                 weights = aw_sub,
                 block = sub_meta$participant_id, 
                 correlation = corfit_sub$consensus)

# Define contrasts of interest: specify which group means to subtract (e.g. Treatment − Control) to test specific hypotheses
cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(conditionFLUADD.Day.1 - conditionFLUADD.Day.0,
                             conditionFLUADD.Day.3 - conditionFLUADD.Day.0,
                             conditionFLUADD.Day.7 - conditionFLUADD.Day.0,
                             levels = design_sub)

# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2_sub <- contrasts.fit(fit_sub, cont.matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink variances
fit2_sub <- eBayes(fit2_sub, robust = TRUE, trend = TRUE)

# Extract and format results
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2_sub), function(i) {
  # Extract DEGs for this contrast using topTreat
  df_res <- topTreat(fit2_sub, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE)
  df_res$symbol <- rownames(df_res)
  df_res$comparison <- colnames(fit2_sub)[i]
  rownames(df_res) <- NULL
  return(df_res)
})

# Row-bind all contrast results into a single data frame: combines list of per-contrast results into a tidy DEG table
single_iteration_output <- do.call(rbind, results_list) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names()

print(head(single_iteration_output))
```


##### Subsampling loop

Run 200 subsampling iterations, each drawing 5 random participants and fitting Limma, then aggregate results via median to obtain robust DEG estimates across iterations.

```{r Subsampling loop}
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(tidyverse)
library(limma)
library(here)
library(janitor)

# Load and pre-filter ExpressionSet
eset_human <- readRDS(file = here("tables", "fluad_eset_human.rds"))

# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_human) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>% 
  rowSums() %>% 
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_human[genes_to_keep, ]
meta_df <- as_tibble(pData(eset_filtered), rownames = "sample_id")
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
expr_matrix <- exprs(eset_filtered)
unique_participants <- meta_df %>% pull(participant_id) %>% unique()

# Defensive longitudinal subsampling function
draw_flexible_subset <- function(participants_list, metadata, target_n = 5) {
  valid_draw <- FALSE
  attempts <- 0
  
  while(!valid_draw) {
    attempts <- attempts + 1
    if(attempts > 2000) stop("Could not find a mathematically stable sub-cohort. Check metadata variance.")
    
    selected_ids <- sample(participants_list, size = target_n, replace = FALSE)
    
    sub_meta <- metadata %>% 
      filter(participant_id %in% selected_ids) %>%
      mutate(condition = as.factor(condition))
    
    has_all_timepoints <- (length(unique(sub_meta$condition)) == 4)
    
    if(has_all_timepoints) {
# Build design matrix for linear modelling: encodes group membership and covariates (sex, age, race) for Limma
      test_design <- model.matrix(~ condition + age + 0, data = sub_meta)
      colnames(test_design) <- make.names(colnames(test_design))
      bad_coefs <- limma::nonEstimable(test_design)
      
      if(is.null(bad_coefs)) {
        valid_draw <- TRUE
      }
    }
  }
  return(sub_meta)
}

# Run multi-iteration simulation loop
n_iterations <- 200 
mouse_n <- 5       

# Set random seed for reproducibility: ensures that subsampling draws the same iterations across runs
set.seed(123)

df_global_runs <- tibble(iteration = 1:n_iterations) %>%
  mutate(
# Apply the sampling function to each iteration: generates a list-column of sampled metadata sets
    sampled_metadata = map(iteration, ~ draw_flexible_subset(unique_participants, meta_df, target_n = mouse_n)),
# Apply Limma to each subsample: fits a linear model per iteration to assess DEG stability
    limma_results = map(sampled_metadata, ~ {
      sub_meta <- .x
      sub_expr <- expr_matrix[, sub_meta$sample_id]
      
# Build design matrix without intercept: each column directly encodes a group mean (facilitates explicit contrasts between groups)
      design_sub <- model.matrix(~ condition + 0, data = sub_meta)
      colnames(design_sub) <- make.names(colnames(design_sub))
      
# Estimate within-subject correlation for repeated measures: samples from the same individual are more similar than samples across individuals
      corfit_sub <- duplicateCorrelation(sub_expr, design = design_sub, block = sub_meta$participant_id)
# Estimate sample-specific quality weights using arrayWeights: down-weights arrays with excessive noise to improve statistical power
      aw_sub <- arrayWeights(sub_expr, design_sub)
      
# Fit linear model per gene using weighted least squares: array weights down-weight noisy arrays; block accounts for subject-level clustering
      fit_sub <- lmFit(sub_expr, 
                       design = design_sub, 
                       weights = aw_sub,
                       block = sub_meta$participant_id, 
                       correlation = corfit_sub$consensus)
      
# Define contrasts of interest: specify which group means to subtract (e.g. Treatment − Control) to test specific hypotheses
      cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(conditionFLUADD.Day.1 - conditionFLUADD.Day.0,
                                   conditionFLUADD.Day.3 - conditionFLUADD.Day.0,
                                   conditionFLUADD.Day.7 - conditionFLUADD.Day.0,
                                   levels = design_sub)
      
      # Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2_sub <- contrasts.fit(fit_sub, cont.matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink gene-wise variances toward a common value: improves stability for low-variance genes
      fit2_sub <- eBayes(fit2_sub, robust = TRUE, trend = TRUE)
      
      res_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2_sub), function(i) {
        # Extract DEGs for this contrast using topTreat
        df_res <- topTreat(fit2_sub, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE)
        df_res$symbol <- rownames(df_res)
        df_res$comparison <- colnames(fit2_sub)[i]
        rownames(df_res) <- NULL
        return(df_res)
      })
      
      # Combine results from all contrasts into a single table
do.call(rbind, res_list)
    })
  )

# Aggregate results via median across iterations
fluad_human_subsampled_degs <- df_global_runs %>%
  select(iteration, limma_results) %>%
# Unnest the list-column of Limma results into a flat data frame: one row per gene × comparison × iteration
  unnest(limma_results) %>%
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>%
  #Calculate errors by iteration
  mutate(
    se_iteration = abs(log_fc / t),
    sd_iteration = se_iteration / sqrt(0.4) # N = 5
  ) %>% 
  group_by(comparison, symbol) %>%
  summarise(
    p_value = median(p_value),
    adj_p_val = median(adj_p_val),
    mean_l2fc = median(log_fc),
    sd_sampling_stability = sd(log_fc),
    se = median(se_iteration),
    sd = median(sd_iteration),
    ci_lower = median(ci_l),
    ci_upper = median(ci_r),
    t = median(t),
    b = median(b),
    ave_expr = median(ave_expr),
    pct_iterations_significant = mean(adj_p_val <= 0.05) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(comparison = stringr::str_replace_all(comparison, "\\.", " "),
         comparison = stringr::str_replace_all(comparison, "condition", "")) %>% 
# Split contrast name into comparison and reference columns (e.g. 'Time1 - Time0' → comparisonA / comparisonRef)
  separate(comparison, sep = " - ", into = c("comparisonA", "comparisonRef")) %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(condition = comparisonA, everything(), -comparisonRef) %>% 
  inner_join(meta_df %>% 
               select(condition, timepoint, vaccine, sample_type) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
               distinct(), by = "condition") %>% 
# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human") %>%
  rename(human_symbol = symbol)

# Save aggregated results
fluad_human_subsampled_degs %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_human_dge_subsampled_degs.rds"))

# Print summary
fluad_human_subsampled_degs %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
  summarise(n_robust_degs = n()) %>% 
  print()

```

#### Simple t-Test

Compute log2 fold-changes for human Fluad samples (days 1, 3, 7 vs day 0), save both long and wide format results.

```{r}
eset_human_mouse = readRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_human_mouse_eset.rds"))
human_mouse_fluad_matrix = eset_human_mouse %>% exprs()
human_mouse_fluad_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_human_mouse_metadata.rds.png"))

# Subset to human samples, excluding outlier participants
human_mouse_fluad_matrix_human = human_mouse_fluad_matrix %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  select(c(human_mouse_fluad_metadata %>% 
           filter(organism == "Human") %>% 
# Remove outlier participants: filters out samples flagged during quality control inspection
             filter(!participant_id %in% c("CRC305DGENT1483036",
                                             "CRC305DGENT0351013",
                                             "CRC305DGENT1471032")) %>% 
             pull(sample_id))) %>% 
  as.matrix()

# Build human metadata with covariates
human_mouse_fluad_metadata_pData = human_mouse_fluad_metadata %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
                                   column_to_rownames("sample_id") %>% 
                                   filter(organism == "Human") %>% 
# Remove outlier participants: filters out samples flagged during quality control inspection
                                   filter(!participant_id %in% c("CRC305DGENT1483036",
                                             "CRC305DGENT0351013",
                                             "CRC305DGENT1471032")) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint = as.factor(timepoint),
         sex = as.factor(sex),
         age = scale(as.numeric(age)),
         race = as.factor(race))

# Compute log2 fold-change relative to day 0
human_fluad_log2fc_filtered_sample_long = human_mouse_fluad_matrix_human %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("human_symbol") %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -human_symbol,
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "log2") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(human_mouse_fluad_metadata_pData %>% 
               rownames_to_column("geo_sample") %>% 
               select(geo_sample, participant_id, timepoint),
             by = "geo_sample") %>% 
  select(human_symbol, participant_id, timepoint, log2) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  select(participant_id, human_symbol, timepoint, value = log2) %>%
  # Reshape to wide format with one column per timepoint
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value, names_prefix = "day_") %>%
# Reshape columns from wide to long using a common prefix pattern: separates metric type from timepoint via names_pattern
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("day_"),
               names_to = "timepoint",
               names_prefix = "day_",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(participant_id, human_symbol) %>% 
# Extract baseline (day 0) expression value for each participant × gene pair: reference for fold-change calculation
  mutate(day0 = value[timepoint == "0"]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Compute log2 fold-change relative to baseline
mutate(log2fc = value - day0) %>%
# Remove baseline rows: only post-vaccination/infection timepoints are relevant for differential expression analysis
  filter(timepoint != "0") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(human_mouse_fluad_metadata_pData %>% 
               rownames_to_column("geo_sample") %>% 
               select(participant_id, timepoint, geo_sample),
             by = join_by("participant_id", "timepoint"))

#Save
human_fluad_log2fc_filtered_sample_long %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_human_log2fc_sample_long.rds"))

# Pivot to wide
human_fluad_log2fc_filtered_sample_wide = human_fluad_log2fc_filtered_sample_long %>% 
  select(-c(value:day0)) %>% 
# Widen data: reshape so that each timepoint becomes a separate column (required format for t-test input)
  pivot_wider(names_from = "participant_id",
              values_from = "log2fc")

# Play notification sound: alerts that a long-running chunk has finished execution
beep()
```

Compute summary statistics (mean log2FC, SE, effect size) and perform paired/unpaired t-tests for each gene, then combine and save the results.

```{r}
# Load log2 fold-change data
human_fluad_log2fc_filtered_sample_long = 
# Load dataset from disk or GEO: reads pre-saved expression matrix / metadata into the R environment
  readRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_human_log2fc_sample_long.rds"))

# Compute per-gene summary statistics
human_fluad_log2fc_summary = human_fluad_log2fc_filtered_sample_long %>% 
  group_by(human_symbol, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_log2fc = mean(log2fc, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_subjects = n(),
    sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd / sqrt(n_subjects),
    effect_size = avg_log2fc / sd)

# Pivot to wide format for t-tests
human_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol_wide = human_mouse_fluad_matrix_human %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("human_symbol") %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -human_symbol,
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "log2") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(human_mouse_fluad_metadata_pData %>% 
               rownames_to_column("geo_sample") %>% 
               select(geo_sample, participant_id, timepoint),
             by = "geo_sample") %>% 
  select(human_symbol, participant_id, timepoint, log2) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  select(participant_id, human_symbol, timepoint, value = log2) %>%
  # Reshape to wide format with one column per timepoint
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value, names_prefix = "day_")

# Paired t-test per gene
human_fluad_log2fc_paired_ttest <- human_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_day1 = tryCatch(t.test(day_1, day_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_day3 = tryCatch(t.test(day_3, day_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_day7 = tryCatch(t.test(day_7, day_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_day1 = p.adjust(pval_day1, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day3 = p.adjust(pval_day3, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day7 = p.adjust(pval_day7, method = "fdr")
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(day\d+)"
  ) %>% 
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  mutate(condition = case_when(timepoint == "day1"	~ "Fluad_24_PBMC",
                                timepoint == "day3"	~ "Fluad_72_PBMC",
                                timepoint == "day7"	~ "Fluad_168_PBMC",
                                T~timepoint),
         timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "day"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Paired")

# Unpaired t-test per gene
human_fluad_log2fc_unpaired_ttest <- human_fluad_log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
    pval_day1 = tryCatch(
      t.test(day_1, day_0, paired = FALSE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    ),
    pval_day3 = tryCatch(
      t.test(day_3, day_0, paired = FALSE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    ),
    pval_day7 = tryCatch(
      t.test(day_7, day_0, paired = FALSE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    ),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_day1 = p.adjust(pval_day1, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day3 = p.adjust(pval_day3, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day7 = p.adjust(pval_day7, method = "fdr")
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(day\d+)"
  ) %>% 
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  mutate(condition = case_when(timepoint == "day1"	~ "Fluad_24_PBMC",
                                timepoint == "day3"	~ "Fluad_72_PBMC",
                                timepoint == "day7"	~ "Fluad_168_PBMC",
                                T~timepoint),
         timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "day"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Unpaired")

# Combine and save
human_fluad_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest = human_fluad_log2fc_paired_ttest %>% 
  bind_rows(human_fluad_log2fc_unpaired_ttest) 

#Save
human_fluad_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds"))

```





## Combine datasets

Merge human and mouse DEG results, log2FC sample-level data, and metadata into unified tables for the Fluad condition.

```{r}
# Combine DEG lists
all_degs_human = readRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_human_dge_subsampled_degs.rds")) 
all_degs_mouse = readRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))  %>% 
  mutate(se = abs(mean_l2fc / t),
         #N = 5
         sd = se / sqrt(5))

all_degs_human_mouse = all_degs_mouse %>% 
# Merge DEG results from all conditions into a unified table: enables cross-pathogen comparison of transcriptional responses
  bind_rows(all_degs_human) 

# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
all_degs_human_mouse %>% saveRDS(here("tables", "influenza_fluad_human_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

# Combine sample-level log2FC
```

### Prepare data

Filter the GSE120661 dataset to Engerix B-treated PBMC mouse samples, recode timepoints from hours to days, save metadata and expression matrix.

```{r}
# Filter to the treatment of interest: removes control/saline samples from this branch
  filter(treatment == "Engerix B",
         tissue == "PBMC") %>%

  mutate(timepoint = (timepoint / 24) %>% round(1),
         participant_id = paste0("ENG_BL_", animal_replicate)) %>%

  filter(timepoint %in% c(0, 1, 3, 7))

#Save
mouse_engerixb_metadata %>%
```
