```{r}
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_metadata.rds"))

# Subset expression matrix
mouse_engerixb_log2 = GSE120661_counts_not_normalized_log2 %>% 
  select(mouse_engerixb_metadata %>% pull(geo_sample))

```
Annotate genes
Map probe IDs to gene symbols using BioMart and orthology lookup.

Map Agilent probe IDs to human gene symbols using BioMart and FIT.mouse2man orthology lookup, then save the annotated expression matrix.

```{r}
# Set up Ensembl BioMart for mouse
ensembl_mart <- useMart("ensembl")
# Select the mouse genome (mmusculus_gene_ensembl) as the annotation dataset in BioMart
ensembl_mart <- useDataset("mmusculus_gene_ensembl", mart = ensembl_mart)

# Get probe IDs
gene_id <- mouse_engerixb_log2 %>% rownames()

# List available attributes
listAttributes(ensembl_mart)

# Retrieve annotations
annot <- getBM(
  attributes = c("agilent_sureprint_g3_ge_8x60k", #Agilent microarray data (design ID 028005, retrieved from GEO)
                 "ensembl_gene_id",
                 "entrezgene_id",
                 "mgi_symbol",
                 "description"),
  filters = "agilent_sureprint_g3_ge_8x60k",
  values = gene_id,
  mart = ensembl_mart)

#Save
annot %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "probe_annot_hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse.rds"))

# Play notification sound: alerts that a long-running chunk has finished execution
beep()

# Load mouse-to-human orthology lookup table
library(FIT.mouse2man)
HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez = FIT.mouse2man::HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(mouse_entrez = mouse_ortholog)

# Summarise expression per probe, collapse to one row per gene
mouse_engerixb_log2summary = mouse_engerixb_log2 %>% #20,845 probes
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe") %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -probe,
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "expression") %>% 
# Group by probe ID to collapse multiple probe-to-gene mappings later
  group_by(probe) %>% 
# Compute per-probe summary statistics (mean, median) across all samples to select the most representative probe
  summarise(mean = mean(expression,na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(expression, na.rm = T)) %>%  
# Join BioMart gene annotation to expression data by probe ID: adds gene symbol, Entrez ID, and description
  inner_join(annot %>% 
              rename(probe = agilent_sureprint_g3_ge_8x60k), 
            by = "probe") %>%  #24.009 rows
  # Collapse multiple probes per Ensembl ID
  group_by(ensembl_gene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-ensembl_gene_id) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  
  # Collapse multiple Ensembl IDs per Entrez ID
  group_by(entrezgene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%  #21.863 probes/entrez_ids
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(mouse_entrez = entrezgene_id) %>% 
  
  # Join human orthologs, collapse to one row per HGNC symbol
  inner_join(HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez, by = c("mouse_entrez", "mgi_symbol")) %>% 
# Group by human gene symbol: after orthology mapping, collapse mouse genes that map to the same human gene
  group_by(hgnc_symbol) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1)  %>% #14.396
  ungroup()

# Remove HGNC symbols that map to multiple MGI symbols
hgnc_symbol_dupes = mouse_engerixb_log2summary %>% 
# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
  get_dupes(hgnc_symbol)

mouse_engerixb_log2summary = mouse_engerixb_log2summary %>% 
# Remove genes with ambiguous human symbol mappings: retains only one-to-one mouse-to-human orthologs
  filter(!hgnc_symbol %in% c(hgnc_symbol_dupes$hgnc_symbol %>% unique())) 

# Build filtered expression matrix with human gene symbols
mouse_engerixb_log2_filtered_probes = mouse_engerixb_log2 %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe") %>% 
# Join expression data with annotation by probe ID: adds gene symbols to raw probe-level measurements
  inner_join(mouse_engerixb_log2summary, by = "probe") %>%   #214,396
  select(probe, mouse_entrez, human_symbol = hgnc_symbol, c(mouse_engerixb_metadata %>% pull(geo_sample)))

mouse_engerixb_log2_filtered %>% dim()
mouse_engerixb_log2_hgnc_symbol = mouse_engerixb_log2_filtered_probes %>% 
  select(probe_id = probe, human_symbol, c(mouse_engerixb_metadata$geo_sample)) %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
  column_to_rownames("human_symbol")

#Save 
mouse_engerixb_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_exprs.rds"))
```
Create expression set

Create expression set
Build an ExpressionSet with the expression matrix and phenotype data.

Build an ExpressionSet and compute log2 fold-changes relative to day 0 for Engerix B mouse samples.

```{r}
# Load data
mouse_engerixb_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_exprs.rds"))
mouse_engerixb_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_metadata.rds"))

# Create ExpressionSet
eset_mouse_engerixb <- ExpressionSet(
  assayData = mouse_engerixb_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
    as.matrix(),
# Convert metadata to AnnotatedDataFrame: formal phenotype data structure required by ExpressionSet
  phenoData = AnnotatedDataFrame(mouse_engerixb_metadata %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
                                   column_to_rownames("geo_sample")))

#Save
eset_mouse_engerixb %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_eset.rds"))
```

Compute log2 fold-change relative to day 0 for each gene and participant, save in long and wide formats.

```{r}
# Compute log2FC
mouse_engerixb_log2fc_filtered_sample_long = mouse_engerixb_log2_hgnc_symbol %>%
  rownames_to_column("human_symbol") %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(human_symbol, probe_id),
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "log2") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(mouse_engerixb_metadata %>% 
               select(geo_sample, participant_id, timepoint),
             by = "geo_sample") %>% 
  select(human_symbol,probe_id, participant_id, timepoint, log2) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  select(participant_id,probe_id, human_symbol, timepoint, value = log2) %>%
  # Reshape to wide format with one column per timepoint
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value, names_prefix = "day_") %>%
# Reshape columns from wide to long using a common prefix pattern: separates metric type from timepoint via names_pattern
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("day_"),
               names_to = "timepoint",
               names_prefix = "day_",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(participant_id, human_symbol) %>% 
# Extract baseline (day 0) expression value for each participant × gene pair: reference for fold-change calculation
  mutate(day0 = value[timepoint == "0"]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Compute log2 fold-change relative to baseline
mutate(log2fc = value - day0) %>%
# Remove baseline rows: only post-vaccination/infection timepoints are relevant for differential expression analysis
  filter(timepoint != "0")

#Save
mouse_engerixb_log2fc_filtered_sample_long %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))

# Pivot to wide
mouse_engerixb_log2fc_filtered_sample_wide = mouse_engerixb_log2fc_filtered_sample_long %>% 
  select(-c(value:day0)) %>% 
# Widen data: reshape so that each timepoint becomes a separate column (required format for t-test input)
  pivot_wider(names_from = "participant_id",
              values_from = "log2fc")

# Play notification sound: alerts that a long-running chunk has finished execution
beep()
```

#### Differential expression 

##### Limma
Paired samples design
```{r}

# Load data
mouse_engerixb_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_exprs.rds"))
mouse_engerixb_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_metadata.rds"))
eset_mouse = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_eset.rds"))

# Keeping only genes with intensity > 6 (log2) in at least 5 samples
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_mouse) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>% 
  rowSums() %>% 
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_mouse[genes_to_keep, ]

# Build design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ condition + 0, # 0 defines the way we compare the samples
                       eset_filtered) 
# Ensure syntactically valid column names: replaces spaces/special characters with dots for model.matrix compatibility
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))  # Avoids blank spaces

# Estimate the correlation between measurements made on the same subject (paired-samples)
corfit <- duplicateCorrelation(eset_filtered, 
                               design = design, 
                               block = eset_filtered$participant_id)
corfit$consensus #-0.02688727


# Estimate sample-specific quality weights using arrayWeights: down-weights arrays with excessive noise to improve statistical power
aw <- arrayWeights(eset_filtered, design)
# Barplot of array weights: visual diagnostic to identify low-quality arrays (bars near zero indicate problematic samples)
barplot(aw, 
        names.arg = eset_filtered$condition, # Label x-axis with condition names
        main = "Sample Weights Diagnostic", 
        ylab = "Weight", 
        las = 2,           # Rotate x-axis labels 90 degrees
        cex.names = 0.7,   # Reduce font size when many labels
        col = "skyblue")


# Fit linear model
fit <- lmFit(eset_filtered, 
             design, 
             weights = aw,
             block = eset_filtered$participant_id, 
             correlation = corfit$consensus) #Use inter-subject correlation as input into the linear model fit

# List conditions
colnames(design) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  arrange(.)

# Define contrasts
cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(conditionEngerix.B_24_PBMC	 - conditionEngerix.B_0_PBMC,
                             conditionEngerix.B_72_PBMC	 - conditionEngerix.B_0_PBMC,
                             conditionEngerix.B_168_PBMC	 - conditionEngerix.B_0_PBMC,
                             levels=design)
# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont.matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink gene-wise variances toward a common value: improves stability for low-variance genes
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2, 
               robust = T, 
               trend = T)

# Diagnostic plot: scatterplot of log2 residual variance vs average expression (should show no strong trend after moderation)
plotSA(fit2, main = "Sigma vs Abundance (Weights Applied)")
# Extract DEGs for every contrast

## For every contrast
# Iterate over each contrast column: extract DEGs from every comparison in one pass
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2), function(i) {
# Extract differentially expressed genes using the treat method (tests whether log2FC exceeds a minimum threshold, not just non-zero)
  topTreat(fit2, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(comparison = colnames(fit2)[i]) %>% 
    rownames_to_column("symbol")
  })

# Combine all results
all_contrasts_degs <- bind_rows(results_list)

# Get all DEGs and clean dataset
all_degs_mouse_engerixb = all_contrasts_degs %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  select(comparison, everything()) %>% 
  mutate(comparison = str_replace(comparison, "\\.\\.\\.", "_") %>% 
           str_replace(., "timepoint", "Time") %>% 
           str_replace(., "treatment", "")) %>% 
# Split contrast name into comparison and reference columns (e.g. 'Time1 - Time0' → comparisonA / comparisonRef)
  separate(comparison, sep = " - ", into = c("comparisonA", "comparisonRef")) %>% 
  mutate(comparisonRef = str_replace(comparisonRef, "treatment", "Time0")) %>% 
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  mutate(condition = case_when(comparisonA == "conditionEngerix.B_24_PBMC"	~ "Engerix_24_PBMC",
                               comparisonA == "conditionEngerix.B_72_PBMC"	~ "Engerix_72_PBMC",
                               comparisonA == "conditionEngerix.B_168_PBMC"	~ "Engerix_168_PBMC",
                               T~comparisonA),
         organism = "Mouse") %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(condition, everything()) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(human_symbol = symbol,
         mean_l2fc = log_fc,
         ci_upper = ci_r,
         ci_lower = ci_l)
	
# #Save
all_degs_mouse_engerixb %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

all_degs_mouse_engerixb %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
# Count the number of differentially expressed genes (adj.p ≤ 0.05) per comparison
  summarise(n_degs = n())

```

##### Simple t-Test
Load the dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r}
# Load data
mouse_log2fc_filtered_sample_long = 
# Load dataset from disk or GEO: reads pre-saved expression matrix / metadata into the R environment
  readRDS(here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))
# Load data
mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_exprs.rds")) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct()

mouse_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_metadata.rds"))

```


Compute summary statistics and perform paired and unpaired t-tests for each timepoint.

```{r}
#Compute summary statistics
mouse_log2fc_summary = mouse_log2fc_filtered_sample_long %>% 
  group_by(human_symbol, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_log2fc = mean(log2fc, na.rm = TRUE),  # mean log2 fold change
    n_subjects = n(),                         # number of samples
    sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),             # standard deviation
    se = sd / sqrt(n_subjects),               # standard error
    effect_size = avg_log2fc / sd)            # Cohen’s d-like effect size

mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol_wide = mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol %>%
  rownames_to_column("human_symbol") %>%
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -human_symbol,
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "log2") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(mouse_metadata %>% 
               select(geo_sample, participant_id, timepoint),
             by = "geo_sample") %>% 
  select(human_symbol, participant_id, timepoint, log2) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  select(participant_id, human_symbol, timepoint, value = log2) %>%
  # Reshape to wide format with one column per timepoint
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value, names_prefix = "day_") 

# Paired t-test
mouse_log2fc_paired_ttest <- mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_day1 = tryCatch(t.test(day_1, day_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_day3 = tryCatch(t.test(day_3, day_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_day7 = tryCatch(t.test(day_7, day_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_day1 = p.adjust(pval_day1, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day3 = p.adjust(pval_day3, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day7 = p.adjust(pval_day7, method = "fdr")
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(day\\d+)"
  ) %>% 
  # Clean timepoint labels and annotate test type
  mutate(timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "day"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Paired")

#Unpaired
mouse_log2fc_unpaired_ttest <- mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_day1 = tryCatch(t.test(day_1, day_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_day3 = tryCatch(t.test(day_3, day_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_day7 = tryCatch(t.test(day_7, day_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_day1 = p.adjust(pval_day1, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day3 = p.adjust(pval_day3, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day7 = p.adjust(pval_day7, method = "fdr")
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(day\\d+)"
  ) %>% 
  # Clean timepoint labels and annotate test type
  mutate(timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "day"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Unpaired")

mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest = mouse_log2fc_paired_ttest %>% 
  bind_rows(mouse_log2fc_unpaired_ttest) 

mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds"))

```

```{r}
probes_annotation <- read.delim(here("tables", "GPL21272-58809.txt"), skip = 19, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", quote = "") %>% 
  select(gene_id = ID, entrez_id = ENTREZ_GENE_ID, ensembl_id = ENSEMBL_ID, gene_symbol = GENE_SYMBOL) %>%

### Filter probes with highest median expression
human_engerix_log2summary = human_exprs_engerixb %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe") %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -probe,
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "expression") %>% 
# Group by probe ID to collapse multiple probe-to-gene mappings later
  group_by(probe) %>% 
# Compute per-probe summary statistics (mean, median) across all samples to select the most representative probe
  summarise(mean = mean(expression,na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(expression, na.rm = T)) %>%  
# Join BioMart gene annotation to expression data by probe ID: adds gene symbol, Entrez ID, and description
  inner_join(probes_annotation %>% 
              rename(probe = gene_id,
                     entrezgene_id = entrez_id,
                     human_symbol = gene_symbol), 
            by = "probe") %>% 
  # Collapse to one row per Ensembl ID
  group_by(ensembl_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-ensembl_id) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  
  # Collapse to one row per Entrez ID
  group_by(entrezgene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%  #21.863 probes/entrez_ids
  ungroup()

  get_dupes(human_symbol)
```

```{r}
# Load data

human_engerixb_log2fc_filtered_sample_long = human_engerix_log2_hgnc_symbol %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -(human_symbol),
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "log2") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(human_metadata_filtered %>% 
               select(geo_sample, participant_id, timepoint),
             by = "geo_sample") %>% 
  select(human_symbol, participant_id, timepoint, log2) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  select(participant_id, human_symbol, timepoint, value = log2)

  # filter(!human_symbol %in% c(overduplicated %>% 
  #                               ungroup() %>% 
  #                               filter(n > median(n)) %>% 
  #                               pull(human_symbol))) %>% 
  # Reshape to wide format with one column per timepoint
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value, names_prefix = "day_") %>% 
# Reshape columns from wide to long using a common prefix pattern: separates metric type from timepoint via names_pattern
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("day_"),
               names_to = "timepoint",
               names_prefix = "day_",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(participant_id, human_symbol) %>% 
# Extract baseline (day 0) expression value for each participant × gene pair: reference for fold-change calculation
  mutate(day0 = value[timepoint == "0"]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Compute log2 fold-change relative to baseline
mutate(log2fc = value - day0) %>%
# Remove baseline rows: only post-vaccination/infection timepoints are relevant for differential expression analysis
  filter(timepoint != "0")

  pivot_wider(names_from = "participant_id",
```

### Differential expression


##### Limma

###### All samples
Load the Engerix B human dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r All samples}
# Load data
human_engerix_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
human_metadata_filtered = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_metadata.rds"))
eset_human = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_eset.rds"))

# Filter low-expressed genes (log2 > 6 in >= 5 samples)
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_human) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>% 
  rowSums() %>% 
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_human[genes_to_keep, ]

# Build design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ timepoint + sex + age + race + 0, eset_filtered) 

#Avoid blank spaces
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))

# Estimate intra-individual correlation
corfit <- duplicateCorrelation(eset_filtered, 
                               design = design, 
                               block = eset_filtered$participant_id)
corfit$consensus #0.30

# Estimate sample-specific quality weights using arrayWeights: down-weights arrays with excessive noise to improve statistical power
aw <- arrayWeights(eset_filtered, design)
# Barplot of array weights: visual diagnostic to identify low-quality arrays (bars near zero indicate problematic samples)
barplot(aw, 
        names.arg = eset_filtered$condition,
        main = "Sample Weights Diagnostic", 
        ylab = "Weight", 
        las = 2,           
        cex.names = 0.7,   
        col = "skyblue")


# Fit
engerix_human_limma_fit <- lmFit(eset_filtered, 
                                 design, 
                                 weights = aw,
                                 block = eset_filtered$participant_id, 
                                 correlation = corfit$consensus)

# Contrasts
cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(
  timepoint1 - timepoint0,
  timepoint3 - timepoint0,
  timepoint7 - timepoint0,
  levels = design
)

# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(engerix_human_limma_fit, cont.matrix)

# Empirical Bayes moderation
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2, 
               robust = T, 
               trend = T)

# Diagnostic plot: scatterplot of log2 residual variance vs average expression (should show no strong trend after moderation)
plotSA(fit2, main = "Sigma vs Abundance (Weights Applied)")

# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
fit2 %>% saveRDS(here("tables","hepatitisb_engerixb_human_limma_fit.rds"))

#Import results from Cluster 
fit2 = readRDS(here("tables","hepatitisb_engerixb_human_limma_fit.rds"))

# Extract
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2), function(i) {
  topTable(fit2, coef = i, adjust.method = "fdr", number = Inf, confint = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(comparison = colnames(fit2)[i]) %>%
    rownames_to_column("symbol")
})


# Combine all results
all_contrasts_degs <- bind_rows(results_list)

# Get all DEGs
all_degs_human = all_contrasts_degs %>% 
  #Clean table
  select(comparison, everything()) %>% 
  mutate(comparison = str_replace(comparison, "\\.\\.\\.", "_") %>% 
           str_replace(., "timepoint", "Time") %>% 
           str_replace(., "treatment", "")) %>% 
# Split contrast name into comparison and reference columns (e.g. 'Time1 - Time0' → comparisonA / comparisonRef)
  separate(comparison, sep = " - ", into = c("comparisonA", "comparisonRef")) %>% 
  mutate(comparisonRef = str_replace(comparisonRef, "treatment", "Time0")) %>% 
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  mutate(condition = case_when(comparisonA == "Time1"	~ "EngerixB_Day1",
                               comparisonA == "Time3"	~ "EngerixB_Day3",
                               comparisonA == "Time7"	~ "EngerixB_Day7",
                               T~comparisonA),
         organism = "Human") %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(condition, everything()) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(human_symbol = symbol,
         mean_l2fc = log_fc,
         ci_upper = ci_r,
         ci_lower = ci_l)

all_degs_human %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
# Count the number of differentially expressed genes (adj.p ≤ 0.05) per comparison
  summarise(n_degs = n())
	
#Save
all_degs_human %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_dge_limma_degs.rds"))
```


###### Subsampling


Run the subsampling loop to assess the impact of cohort composition on differential expression results.

```{r Subsampling loop}
## 1. Load and Pre-Filter ExpressionSet Data
human_metadata_filtered = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_metadata.rds"))
eset_human = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_eset.rds"))

# Baseline expression intensity filtering threshold
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_human) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>% 
  rowSums() %>% 
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_human[genes_to_keep, ]
meta_df <- as_tibble(pData(eset_filtered), rownames = "sample_id")
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
expr_matrix <- exprs(eset_filtered)
unique_participants <- meta_df %>% pull(participant_id) %>% unique()

## 2. Defensive Longitudinal Subsampling Function
# Define a defensive sampling function: draws independent samples while ensuring balanced representation of all groups
draw_flexible_subset <- function(participants_list, metadata, target_n = 5) {
  valid_draw <- FALSE
  attempts <- 0
  
  while(!valid_draw) {
    attempts <- attempts + 1
    if(attempts > 500) stop("Could not find a balanced subset. Please check metadata variance.")
    
    # Randomly sample N individuals
    selected_ids <- sample(participants_list, size = target_n, replace = FALSE)
    
    sub_meta <- metadata %>% 
      filter(participant_id %in% selected_ids)
    
    # Check that all 4 timepoints are present in the sampled subset
    has_all_timepoints <- (length(unique(sub_meta$timepoint)) == 4)
    
    if(has_all_timepoints) {
      valid_draw <- TRUE
    }
  }
  return(sub_meta)
}

## 3. Run Multi-Iteration Simulation Loop
n_iterations <- 200 
cohort_n <- 5       

# Set random seed for reproducibility: ensures that subsampling draws the same iterations across runs
set.seed(123) 

df_global_runs <- tibble(iteration = 1:n_iterations) %>%
  mutate(
# Apply the sampling function to each iteration: generates a list-column of sampled metadata sets
    sampled_metadata = map(iteration, ~ draw_flexible_subset(unique_participants, meta_df, target_n = cohort_n)),
    
# Apply Limma to each subsample: fits a linear model per iteration to assess DEG stability
    limma_results = map(sampled_metadata, ~ {
      sub_meta <- .x
      sub_expr <- expr_matrix[, sub_meta$sample_id]
      
      # Design matrix WITHOUT sex, age, race
      design_sub <- model.matrix(~ timepoint + 0, data = sub_meta)
      colnames(design_sub) <- make.names(colnames(design_sub))
      
# Estimate within-subject correlation for repeated measures: samples from the same individual are more similar than samples across individuals
      corfit_sub <- duplicateCorrelation(sub_expr, design = design_sub, block = sub_meta$participant_id)
# Estimate sample-specific quality weights using arrayWeights: down-weights arrays with excessive noise to improve statistical power
      aw_sub <- arrayWeights(sub_expr, design_sub)
      
# Fit linear model per gene using weighted least squares: array weights down-weight noisy arrays; block accounts for subject-level clustering
      fit_sub <- lmFit(sub_expr, 
                       design = design_sub, 
                       weights = aw_sub,
                       block = sub_meta$participant_id, 
                       correlation = corfit_sub$consensus)
      
      # Adjust contrasts for EngerixB
      cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(timepoint1 - timepoint0,
                                   timepoint3 - timepoint0,
                                   timepoint7 - timepoint0,
                                   levels = design_sub)
      
      # Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2_sub <- contrasts.fit(fit_sub, cont.matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink gene-wise variances toward a common value: improves stability for low-variance genes
      fit2_sub <- eBayes(fit2_sub, robust = TRUE, trend = TRUE)
      
      res_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2_sub), function(i) {
        # Extract DEGs for this contrast using topTreat
        df_res <- topTreat(fit2_sub, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE)
        df_res$symbol <- rownames(df_res)
        df_res$comparison <- colnames(fit2_sub)[i]
        rownames(df_res) <- NULL
        return(df_res)
      })
      
# Row-bind all contrast results into a single data frame: combines list of per-contrast results into a tidy DEG table
      do.call(rbind, res_list)
    })
  )

## 4. Data Processing & Summary
engerixb_human_subsampled_degs <- df_global_runs %>%
  select(iteration, limma_results) %>%
# Unnest the list-column of Limma results into a flat data frame: one row per gene × comparison × iteration
  unnest(limma_results) %>%
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>%
  #Calculate errors by iteration
    #Calculate errors by iteration
  mutate(
    se_iteration = abs(log_fc / t),
    sd_iteration = se_iteration / sqrt(0.4) # N = 5
  ) %>% 
  group_by(comparison, symbol) %>%
  summarise(
    p_value = median(p_value),
    adj_p_val = median(adj_p_val),
    mean_l2fc = median(log_fc),
    sd_sampling_stability = sd(log_fc),
    se = median(se_iteration),
    sd = median(sd_iteration),
    ci_lower = median(ci_l),
    ci_upper = median(ci_r),
    t = median(t),
    b = median(b),
    ave_expr = median(ave_expr),
    pct_iterations_significant = mean(adj_p_val <= 0.05) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  #Clean table
  select(comparison, everything()) %>% 
  mutate(comparison = str_replace(comparison, "\\.\\.\\.", "_") %>% 
           str_replace(., "timepoint", "Time") %>% 
           str_replace(., "treatment", "")) %>% 
# Split contrast name into comparison and reference columns (e.g. 'Time1 - Time0' → comparisonA / comparisonRef)
  separate(comparison, sep = " - ", into = c("comparisonA", "comparisonRef")) %>% 
  mutate(comparisonRef = str_replace(comparisonRef, "treatment", "Time0")) %>% 
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  mutate(condition = case_when(comparisonA == "Time1"	~ "EngerixB_Day1",
                               comparisonA == "Time3"	~ "EngerixB_Day3",
                               comparisonA == "Time7"	~ "EngerixB_Day7",
                               T~comparisonA),
         timepoint = readr::parse_number(condition) %>% as.character(),
         organism = "Human") %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(condition, everything()) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(human_symbol = symbol)



# Save
engerixb_human_subsampled_degs %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_dge_subsampled_degs.rds"))

# Summary report
engerixb_human_subsampled_degs %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>% 
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
  summarise(n_robust_degs = n()) %>% 
  print()
```

```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=6}
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(tidyverse)
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(patchwork)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. PROCESS SIMULATION ITERATIONS DATA (RAW METRICS)
# ==============================================================================
# Calculate mean age and male proportions per loop iteration
demographics_summary <- df_global_runs %>%
  select(iteration, sampled_metadata) %>%
  unnest(sampled_metadata) %>%
# Extract demographic columns (age, sex, race) per iteration for visualisation
  select(iteration, participant_id, age, sex) %>%
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>%
  group_by(iteration) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_age   = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    prop_male  = mean(sex == "male", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(iteration = factor(iteration, levels = 1:max(iteration)))

# Separate long format extraction for categorical group distributions
subsample_race_distribution <- df_global_runs %>%
  select(iteration, sampled_metadata) %>%
  unnest(sampled_metadata) %>%
  select(iteration, participant_id, race) %>%
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>%
  dplyr::count(iteration, race) %>%
  group_by(iteration) %>%
# Convert counts to proportions: facilitates stacked bar charts of demographic distributions
  mutate(Proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(iteration = factor(iteration, levels = 1:max(as.numeric(iteration)))) 

# ==============================================================================

  theme(

    axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  ) +
# Set informative axis labels, legend titles, and overall plot title
  labs(x = "Race Distribution")

# Combine top sub-plots side-by-side using patchwork weights
top_panel <- plot_age + plot_sex + plot_race + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1, 1))

# ==============================================================================
# 3. BUILD BOTTOM PANEL: ORIGINAL TOTAL COHORT BASELINE (N=100)
# ==============================================================================
original_demographics <- human_metadata_filtered %>%
  mutate(age = str_remove(age, "y") %>% as.numeric()) %>% 
  select(participant_id, age, sex, race) %>%
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct()

# Baseline A: Continuous Raw Age Density Curve
base_age <- ggplot(original_demographics, aes(x = age)) +
# Add density plot: smooth distribution of age values for the full cohort baseline
  geom_density(fill = "#3182bd", alpha = 0.4, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
# Add vertical dashed line at the cohort mean age: reference for comparing subsample distributions
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(original_demographics$age, na.rm = TRUE), 
             color = "black", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
# Create faceted plot: split data into sub-panels by condition or organism for side-by-side comparison
  facet_wrap(~"Age") +
# Configure x-axis: set position, expansion, breaks, and labels
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo() +
# Customise theme elements: remove/minimise gridlines, adjust axis text, and fine-tune legend placement
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9)
  ) +
# Set informative axis labels, legend titles, and overall plot title
  labs(x = "Age (Years)", y = "Density")

# Baseline B: Total Cohort Sex Proportions Anchor Bar
base_sex <- original_demographics %>%
  dplyr::count(sex) %>%
# Convert counts to proportions: facilitates stacked bar charts of demographic distributions
  mutate(Proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
# Initialise ggplot with aesthetic mappings: defines variables for x-axis, y-axis, colour, and fill
  ggplot(aes(x = Proportion, y = "Original\nCohort (n=100)", fill = sex)) +
# Create faceted plot: split data into sub-panels by condition or organism for side-by-side comparison
  facet_wrap(~"Original\nCohort") +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = "stack", show.legend = FALSE) +
# Apply manual colour scale: uses predefined colour palette (typically from project's colour scheme)
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("male" = "#3182bd", "female" = "#fa9fb5")) +
# Configure x-axis: set position, expansion, breaks, and labels
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo() +
# Customise theme elements: remove/minimise gridlines, adjust axis text, and fine-tune legend placement
  theme(
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )

# Baseline C: Total Cohort Race Proportions Anchor Bar (Multi-Categorical Configuration)
base_race <- original_demographics %>%
  mutate(race = str_replace(race, "black or african american", "black"),
         race = str_to_title(race)) %>% 
  dplyr::count(race) %>%
# Convert counts to proportions: facilitates stacked bar charts of demographic distributions
  mutate(Proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
# Initialise ggplot with aesthetic mappings: defines variables for x-axis, y-axis, colour, and fill
  ggplot(aes(x = Proportion, y = "Original\nCohort (n=100)", fill = race)) +
# Create faceted plot: split data into sub-panels by condition or organism for side-by-side comparison
  facet_wrap(~"Race") +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = "stack", show.legend = TRUE) +
# Apply manual colour scale: uses predefined colour palette (typically from project's colour scheme)
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Race",
    values = colors$race
  ) +
# Configure x-axis: set position, expansion, breaks, and labels
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo() +
# Customise theme elements: remove/minimise gridlines, adjust axis text, and fine-tune legend placement
  theme(
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )

# Combine baseline anchors horizontally using matching grid widths
bottom_panel <- base_age + base_sex + base_race + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1, 1))

# ==============================================================================
# 4. STITCH COMPLETE GRAPHICAL CANVAS
# ==============================================================================
final_canvas <- top_panel / bottom_panel + 
  plot_layout(heights = c(4, 1), guides = "collect") +
# Add overall title to the combined figure using patchwork
  plot_annotation(title = "EngerixB, Human")

print(final_canvas)
```

##### Simple t-Test
Load the dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r}
# Load data
human_log2fc_filtered_sample_long = 
# Load dataset from disk or GEO: reads pre-saved expression matrix / metadata into the R environment
  readRDS(here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))
# Load data
human_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds")) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct()

human_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_metadata.rds"))

#Compute summary statistics
human_log2fc_summary = human_log2fc_filtered_sample_long %>% 
  group_by(human_symbol, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_log2fc = mean(log2fc, na.rm = TRUE),  # mean log2 fold change
    n_subjects = n(),                         # number of samples
    sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),             # standard deviation
    se = sd / sqrt(n_subjects),               # standard error
    effect_size = avg_log2fc / sd)            # Cohen’s d-like effect size

human_log2_hgnc_symbol_wide = human_log2_hgnc_symbol %>%
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -human_symbol,
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "log2") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(human_metadata %>% 
               select(geo_sample, participant_id, timepoint),
             by = "geo_sample") %>% 
  select(human_symbol, participant_id, timepoint, log2) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  select(participant_id, human_symbol, timepoint, value = log2) %>%
  # Reshape to wide format with one column per timepoint
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value, names_prefix = "day_")

# Paired t-test
human_log2fc_paired_ttest <- human_log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_day1 = tryCatch(t.test(day_1, day_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_day3 = tryCatch(t.test(day_3, day_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_day7 = tryCatch(t.test(day_7, day_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_day1 = p.adjust(pval_day1, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day3 = p.adjust(pval_day3, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day7 = p.adjust(pval_day7, method = "fdr")
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(day\\d+)"
  ) %>% 
  # Clean timepoint labels and annotate test type
  mutate(timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "day"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Paired")

#Unpaired
human_log2fc_unpaired_ttest <- human_log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_day1 = tryCatch(t.test(day_1, day_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_day3 = tryCatch(t.test(day_3, day_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_day7 = tryCatch(t.test(day_7, day_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_day1 = p.adjust(pval_day1, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day3 = p.adjust(pval_day3, method = "fdr"),
    padj_day7 = p.adjust(pval_day7, method = "fdr")
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(day\\d+)"
  ) %>% 
  # Clean timepoint labels and annotate test type
  mutate(timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "day"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Unpaired")

human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest = human_log2fc_paired_ttest %>% 
  bind_rows(human_log2fc_unpaired_ttest) 

human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds"))

```

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=5}
GSE124533_counts_log2_summary_annotated_probes =
```

## Combine datasets
Combine differential expression results from human and mouse datasets for cross-species comparison.

```{r}
# Unite DEGs =================
all_degs_human = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_dge_subsampled_degs.rds"))

all_degs_mouse = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds")) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint = str_remove(condition, "Engerix_") %>% str_remove("_PBMC")) %>% 
  mutate(se = abs(mean_l2fc / t),
         #N = 5
         sd = se / sqrt(5))

all_degs_human_mouse = all_degs_human %>% 
# Merge DEG results from all conditions into a unified table: enables cross-pathogen comparison of transcriptional responses
  bind_rows(all_degs_mouse) %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(condition, timepoint, human_symbol, everything()) %>% 
  mutate(pathogen = "Hepatitis B", vaccine = "EngerixB",
         timepoint = as.numeric(timepoint),
         timepoint = if_else(organism == "Mouse", as.numeric(timepoint)/24, timepoint))

# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
all_degs_human_mouse %>% saveRDS(here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

#Unite Mouse and Human datasets samples ===============
human_mouse_log2fc_samples = 
#Mouse
mouse_engerixb_log2fc_filtered_sample_long %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(human_symbol, log2fc, participant_id,
         timepoint, value, day0) %>% 
# Tag rows as Mouse: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Mouse") %>% 
  
  #Human
  bind_rows(human_engerixb_log2fc_filtered_sample_long %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(human_symbol, log2fc, participant_id,
         timepoint,  value, day0) %>% 
# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human"))

human_mouse_log2fc_samples %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
```

### Compare DGE methods
Import t-test and Limma results and merge them for comparison of differential expression methods.

```{r}
#Import ------
#t-Test
human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest =
# Load dataset from disk or GEO: reads pre-saved expression matrix / metadata into the R environment
  readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds")) %>% 
# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human")
mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest =
# Load dataset from disk or GEO: reads pre-saved expression matrix / metadata into the R environment
  readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds")) %>% 
# Tag rows as Mouse: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Mouse")

#Limma
human_degs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_dge_subsampled_degs.rds")) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(padj = adj_p_val) %>% 
# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human",
         test = "Limma",
         paired = "Paired",
         timepoint = str_remove(comparison_a, "Time"))

mouse_degs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds")) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(padj = adj_p_val) %>% 
# Tag rows as Mouse: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Mouse",
         test = "Limma",
         paired = "Paired",
         timepoint = str_remove(condition, "Engerix_") %>% str_remove("_PBMC"),
         timepoint = (as.numeric(timepoint)/24) %>% as.character())

#Merge datasets
degs_ttest_limma =
  bind_rows(
    human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest,
    human_degs,
    mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest,
    mouse_degs
    )

#Summarize  
degs_ttest_limma_summary = degs_ttest_limma %>% 
  group_by(organism, timepoint, test, paired) %>% 
  summarise(
    n_degs = sum(padj <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint_num = readr::parse_number(timepoint),
    timepoint = paste0("Day ", timepoint),
    timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = unique(timepoint[order(timepoint_num)]))) 

degs_ttest_limma_summary

```

### Retrieve dataset
Retrieve Exprs and Metadata from GEO
```{r}
#S aureus: GSE19668 -----
filename = "saureus_infection_GSE19668"
# Download GEO ExpressionSet using GEOquery package: retrieves both expression data and phenotype metadata
GSE19668 <- getGEO("GSE19668", GSEMatrix = TRUE) 
# Unlist the GEO download result: extract the ExpressionSet object from the list wrapper
eset <- GSE19668[[1]]

#Metadata ------
GSE19668_metadata = eset %>% 
  pData() %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  dplyr::select( 
    geo_sample = "geo_accession", 
    subject_id = "title",
    # sex = "gender:ch1", 
    treatment = "infection:ch1", 
    # tissue = "tissue:ch1",
    timepoint = "time point:ch1",
    # animal_replicate = "animal replicate:ch1",
    strain = "strain:ch1") %>% 
# Relevel treatment factor: set saline/control as the reference level for proper contrast encoding
  mutate(treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "none"),
         timepoint = fct_relevel(timepoint, "0"),
         condition = paste(treatment, strain, timepoint, sep = "_"))

#Save
GSE19668_metadata %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", paste0(filename, "_metadata.rds")))


#Get counts matrix ------
GSE_exprs <- eset %>% exprs()

#Save as RDS
GSE_exprs %>% as.data.frame() %>% saveRDS(here("tables", paste0(filename, "_exprs.rds")))
```

```{r}
  filter(strain == "C57BL/6J") %>% 
  separate(subject_id, into = c("tissue", "strain1", "timepoint1", "participant_id"), sep = " ") %>% 
  select(!c(tissue:timepoint1)) %>% 
  arrange(participant_id, timepoint) %>% 
  separate(timepoint, into = c("timepoint_number", "time_unit")) %>% 
  mutate(time_unit = "hours",
         timepoint = timepoint_number %>% as.numeric(),
         organism = "Mouse") %>% 
  arrange(timepoint) %>% 
  select(-timepoint_number) %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(geo_sample, participant_id, condition, timepoint, time_unit, everything())

#Save
GSE19668_metadata_filtered %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_metadata_filtered.rds"))
```

Annotate probes with gene symbols by querying the Ensembl BioMart database.

```{r}
########### Filter and annotate probes -----
# Configure Ensembl BioMart
ensembl_mart <- useMart("ensembl")
# Select the mouse genome (mmusculus_gene_ensembl) as the annotation dataset in BioMart
ensembl_mart <- useDataset("mmusculus_gene_ensembl", mart = ensembl_mart)

# Get probe IDs from expression matrix
gene_id <- mouse_exprs %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe_id") %>% 
  pull(probe_id) %>% unique()

# listAttributes(ensembl_mart)
# Annotate data
annot <- getBM(
  attributes = c("affy_mouse430_2",
                 "ensembl_gene_id",
                 "entrezgene_id",
                 "mgi_symbol",
                 "description"),
  filters = "affy_mouse430_2", #Probes
  values = gene_id,
  mart = ensembl_mart)

annot %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "probe_annot_saureus_infection_mouse.rds"))

# Load mouse-to-human orthology lookup
# (Install orthology package if needed)
# library(devtools)
# devtools::install_github('shenorrLabTRDF/FIT.mouse2man')
library(FIT.mouse2man)
HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez = FIT.mouse2man::HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(mouse_entrez = mouse_ortholog)

#Get annotations for each probe 
### Filter probes with highest median expression
mouse_log2summary = mouse_exprs %>% #20,845 probes
  rownames_to_column("probe_id") %>% 
  rename(probe = probe_id) %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -probe,
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "expression") %>% 
# Group by probe ID to collapse multiple probe-to-gene mappings later
  group_by(probe) %>% 
# Compute per-probe summary statistics (mean, median) across all samples to select the most representative probe
  summarise(mean = mean(expression,na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(expression, na.rm = T)) %>%  
# Join BioMart gene annotation to expression data by probe ID: adds gene symbol, Entrez ID, and description
  inner_join(annot %>% 
              rename(probe = affy_mouse430_2), 
            by = "probe") %>%  #24.009 rows
  # Collapse to one row per Ensembl ID
  group_by(ensembl_gene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-ensembl_gene_id) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  
  # Collapse to one row per Entrez ID
  group_by(entrezgene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%  #21.863 probes/entrez_ids
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(mouse_entrez = entrezgene_id) %>% 
  
  # Join human orthologs, collapse to one row per HGNC symbol
  inner_join(HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez, by = c("mouse_entrez", "mgi_symbol")) %>% 
# Group by human gene symbol: after orthology mapping, collapse mouse genes that map to the same human gene
  group_by(hgnc_symbol) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1)  %>% #14.396
  ungroup()

# Remove HGNC symbols with multiple MGI mappings
hgnc_symbol_dupes = mouse_log2summary %>% 
  #filter ensembl id with multiple mgi_symbols
  get_dupes(hgnc_symbol)

#Filter out probes with multiple mgi and hgnc symbols
probe_dupes = mouse_log2summary %>% get_dupes(probe)

mouse_log2summary = mouse_log2summary %>% 
  select(probe, hgnc_symbol) %>% 
# Remove genes with ambiguous human symbol mappings: retains only one-to-one mouse-to-human orthologs
  filter(!hgnc_symbol %in% c(hgnc_symbol_dupes$hgnc_symbol %>% unique()),
         !probe %in% c(probe_dupes$probe %>% unique())) 

# Build filtered expression matrix with human symbols

# Join expression with annotation, keep only mapped probes
mouse_log2_filtered_probes = mouse_exprs %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe_id") %>% 
  rename(probe = probe_id) %>% 
# Join expression data with annotation by probe ID: adds gene symbols to raw probe-level measurements
  inner_join(mouse_log2summary, by = "probe") %>%   #214,396
  select(human_symbol = hgnc_symbol,
         probe,
         c(mouse_metadata %>% 
             pull(geo_sample)))
#Check
mouse_log2_filtered_probes %>% dim()
mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol = mouse_log2_filtered_probes 
# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% get_dupes(probe)

#Save
mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables","saureus_infection_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
```

### Differential expression 

#### Limma
Paired samples design
```{r}

# Load data
mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
mouse_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_metadata_filtered.rds"))
eset_mouse = readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_eset.rds"))

# Filter low-expressed genes (log2 > 6 in >= 5 samples)
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_mouse) %>%
as.data.frame() %>%
mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>%
rowSums() %>%
{ . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_mouse[genes_to_keep, ]
# Build design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ condition + 0, # 0 defines the way we compare the samples
                       eset_filtered) 

# Ensure syntactically valid column names: replaces spaces/special characters with dots for model.matrix compatibility
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))  # Avoids blank spaces

# Estimate the correlation between measurements made on the same subject (paired-samples)
corfit <- duplicateCorrelation(eset_filtered, 
                               design = design, 
                               block = eset_filtered$participant_id)
corfit$consensus #0.001357108


# Estimate sample-specific quality weights using arrayWeights: down-weights arrays with excessive noise to improve statistical power
aw <- arrayWeights(eset_filtered, design)
# Barplot of array weights: visual diagnostic to identify low-quality arrays (bars near zero indicate problematic samples)
barplot(aw,
names.arg = eset_filtered$condition, 
main = "Sample Weights Diagnostic",
ylab = "Weight",
las = 2,
cex.names = 0.7, 
col = "skyblue")


# Fit linear model
fit <- lmFit(eset_filtered, 
             design, 
             weights = aw,
             block = eset_filtered$participant_id, 
             correlation = corfit$consensus) #Use inter-subject correlation as input into the linear model fit

# List available conditions
colnames(design) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  arrange(.)

# Define contrasts
cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(conditionStaphylococcus.aureus_C57BL.6J_2.hours - conditionnone_C57BL.6J_0,
                             conditionStaphylococcus.aureus_C57BL.6J_4.hours - conditionnone_C57BL.6J_0,
                             conditionStaphylococcus.aureus_C57BL.6J_6.hours - conditionnone_C57BL.6J_0,
                             conditionStaphylococcus.aureus_C57BL.6J_12.hours - conditionnone_C57BL.6J_0,
                             levels=design)
# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont.matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink gene-wise variances toward a common value: improves stability for low-variance genes
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2,
               robust = T,
               trend = T)

# Diagnostic plot: scatterplot of log2 residual variance vs average expression (should show no strong trend after moderation)
plotSA(fit2, main = "Sigma vs Abundance (Weights Applied)")

# Extract DEGs for every contrast

## For every contrast
# Iterate over each contrast column: extract DEGs from every comparison in one pass
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2), function(i) {
# Extract differentially expressed genes using the treat method (tests whether log2FC exceeds a minimum threshold, not just non-zero)
  topTreat(fit2, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(comparison = colnames(fit2)[i]) %>% 
    rownames_to_column("symbol")
  })

# Combine all results
all_contrasts_degs <- bind_rows(results_list)

# Get all DEGs and clean dataset
all_degs = all_contrasts_degs %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  select(comparison, everything()) %>% 
  mutate(comparison = str_replace(comparison, "\\.\\.\\.", "_") %>% 
           str_replace(., "timepoint", "Time") %>% 
           str_replace(., "treatment", "")) %>% 
# Split contrast name into comparison and reference columns (e.g. 'Time1 - Time0' → comparisonA / comparisonRef)
  separate(comparison, sep = " - ", into = c("comparisonA", "comparisonRef")) %>% 
  mutate(comparisonRef = str_replace(comparisonRef, "conditionnone_C57BL.6J_0", "0")) %>% 
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  mutate(condition = case_when(comparisonA == "conditionStaphylococcus.aureus_C57BL.6J_2.hours"	~ "Saureus_2h",
                               comparisonA == "conditionStaphylococcus.aureus_C57BL.6J_4.hours"	~ "Saureus_4h",
                               comparisonA == "conditionStaphylococcus.aureus_C57BL.6J_6.hours"	~ "Saureus_6h",
                               comparisonA == "conditionStaphylococcus.aureus_C57BL.6J_12.hours"	~ "Saureus_12h",
                               T~comparisonA),
         organism = "Mouse",
         timepoint = str_remove(condition, "Saureus_") %>% str_remove("h")) %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(condition, everything()) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(human_symbol = symbol,
         mean_l2fc = log_fc,
         ci_upper = ci_r,
         ci_lower = ci_l)
	
# #Save
all_degs %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

all_degs %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
# Count the number of differentially expressed genes (adj.p ≤ 0.05) per comparison
  summarise(n_degs = n())

```




#### T test 
Load the S. aureus mouse dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r}
# Load data
mouse_exprs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds")) %>% 
  ungroup()
mouse_metadata =  readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_metadata_filtered.rds"))
log2fc_sample = readRDS(here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))
log2fc_sample_symbol = log2fc_sample %>% 
  inner_join(mouse_exprs %>% 
               select(human_symbol, probe_id = probe) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
               distinct(),
             by = "probe_id")

#Compute summary statistics
log2fc_summary = log2fc_sample_symbol %>% 
  group_by(human_symbol, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_log2fc = mean(log2fc, na.rm = TRUE),  # mean log2 fold change
    n_subjects = n(),                         # number of samples
    sd = sd(log2fc, na.rm = TRUE),             # standard deviation
    se = sd / sqrt(n_subjects),               # standard error
    effect_size = avg_log2fc / sd)            # Cohen’s d-like effect size

log2_hgnc_symbol_wide = mouse_exprs %>%
  # Reshape expression data from wide to long format
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(human_symbol, probe),
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "log2") %>% 
  # Join sample-level metadata (subject, timepoint)
  inner_join(mouse_metadata %>% 
               select(geo_sample, subject_id = participant_id, timepoint),
             by = "geo_sample") %>% 
  select(human_symbol, subject_id, timepoint, log2) %>% 
  # Remove duplicate probe-to-gene mappings
  distinct() %>% 
  select(subject_id, human_symbol, timepoint, value = log2) %>%
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  # Reshape to wide format with one column per timepoint
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value, names_prefix = "hour_") 

# Paired t-test
log2fc_paired_ttest <- log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_hour2 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_2, hour_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_hour4 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_4, hour_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_hour6 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_6, hour_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_hour12 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_12, hour_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),

    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_hour2 = p.adjust(pval_hour2, method = "fdr"),
    padj_hour4 = p.adjust(pval_hour4, method = "fdr"),
    padj_hour6 = p.adjust(pval_hour6, method = "fdr"),
    padj_hour12 = p.adjust(pval_hour12, method = "fdr"),
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(hour\\d+)"
  ) %>% 
  # Clean timepoint labels and annotate test type
  mutate(timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "hour"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Paired")

#Unpaired
log2fc_unpaired_ttest = log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_hour2 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_2, hour_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_hour4 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_4, hour_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_hour6 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_6, hour_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_hour12 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_12, hour_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_hour2 = p.adjust(pval_hour2, method = "fdr"),
    padj_hour4 = p.adjust(pval_hour4, method = "fdr"),
    padj_hour6 = p.adjust(pval_hour6, method = "fdr"),
    padj_hour12 = p.adjust(pval_hour12, method = "fdr"),
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(hour\\d+)"
  ) %>% 
  # Clean timepoint labels and annotate test type
  mutate(timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "hour"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Unpaired") 

log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest = log2fc_unpaired_ttest %>% 
  bind_rows(log2fc_paired_ttest) 

log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds"))

```


#### Compare DGE methods

Import t-test and Limma results and merge them for comparison of differential expression methods.

```{r}
#Import ------
#t-Test
mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest =
# Load dataset from disk or GEO: reads pre-saved expression matrix / metadata into the R environment
  readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds")) %>% 
# Tag rows as Mouse: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Mouse")

#Limma
mouse_degs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds")) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(padj = adj_p_val) %>% 
# Tag rows as Mouse: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Mouse",
         test = "Limma",
         paired = "Paired") 


#Merge datasets
degs_ttest_limma =
  bind_rows(
    mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest,
    mouse_degs
    )

#Summarize  
degs_ttest_limma_summary = degs_ttest_limma %>% 
  group_by(organism, timepoint, test, paired) %>% 
  summarise(
    n_degs = sum(padj <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint_num = readr::parse_number(timepoint),
    timepoint = paste0(timepoint, "h"),
    timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = unique(timepoint[order(timepoint_num)]))) 

degs_ttest_limma_summary

```


Plot the number of DEGs identified by each method (t-test vs Limma) across significance levels.

```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=5}

degs_ttest_limma_summary_plot_gg <- degs_ttest_limma_summary %>%
# Initialise ggplot with aesthetic mappings: defines variables for x-axis, y-axis, colour, and fill
  ggplot(aes(

    y = n_degs,

  facet_wrap(~organism, scales = "free_y") +
```

## Human

### Prepare data
Prepare the S. aureus human dataset: download, import, and annotate.

```{r}
#S. aureus: GSE33341 -----
filename = "GSE33341"
GSE <- getGEO("GSE33341", GSEMatrix = TRUE) 
eset <- GSE[[2]] #The matrix #1 the mouse annotated

#Metadata ------
GSE_metadata = eset %>% 
  pData() %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  dplyr::select( 
    geo_sample = "geo_accession", 
    participant_id = "title",
    sex = "host gender:ch1",
    condition = "source_name_ch1",
    pathogen = "pathogen:ch1",
    description = "source_name_ch1", 
    ethnicity = "ethnicity:ch1",
    tissue_infection = "anatomic site of infection:ch1",
    batch_experimental = "experimental batch:ch1",
    age = "host age (yr):ch1") %>% 
  mutate(condition = pathogen,
         organism = "Human",
         timepoint = 1,
         time_unit = "Day",
         tissue = "Blood",
         participant_id = str_extract(participant_id, "\\[.*?\\]") %>% 
           str_remove("\\[") %>% 
           str_remove("\\]"),
         condition = case_when(description == "blood patient with E. coli bacteremia prior antibiotic treatment (Emergency Department)" ~ "E. coli prior antibiotic",
                               description == "blood patient with S. aureus bacteremia prior antibiotic treatment (Emergency Department)" ~ "S aureus prior antibiotic",
                               description == "blood human NOT infected" ~ "No infection",
                               T ~ description),
         pathogen = if_else(pathogen == "-", "Healthy", pathogen))
#Save
GSE_metadata %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_metadata.rds"))

#Filter metadata
GSE_metadata_filtered = GSE_metadata %>%
  filter(pathogen %in% c("Staphylococcus aureus", "Healthy")) %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(geo_sample, participant_id, condition, timepoint, everything()) %>% 
  mutate(ethnicity = str_to_title(ethnicity)) %>% 
  filter(batch_experimental != "2739",
         ethnicity != "Unknown",
         age != "unknown")

GSE_metadata_filtered %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_metadata.rds"))



#Expression data----
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
GSE_exprs <- exprs(eset) %>% as.data.frame()

#Save
GSE_exprs %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_exprs.rds"))
```
