Annotate gene symbols and map probes to human orthologs via BioMart.

```{r}
#Annotate genes ------
#Human -----
#Annotate data and calculate log2fc
human_exprs_metadata  = human_exprs %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe_id") %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -probe_id,
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "value_raw") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(human_metadata, 
             by = "geo_sample") 

#Get value from healthy and calculate Log2FC
human_exprs_log2fc_sample = human_exprs_metadata %>% 
  filter(pathogen == "Healthy") %>% 
  select(probe_id, value_raw_ref = value_raw) %>% 
# Group by probe ID to collapse multiple probe-to-gene mappings later
  group_by(probe_id) %>% 
  summarise(value_raw_ref = mean(value_raw_ref)) %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(human_exprs_metadata %>% 
               filter(pathogen != "Healthy"),
             by = join_by("probe_id")) %>% 
  filter(condition != "No infection") %>% 
  # Compute log2 fold-change relative to baseline
mutate(log2fc = value_raw - value_raw_ref) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() 

#Check duplicates
human_exprs_log2fc_sample %>% 
  filter(participant_id == "CSD4620.CEL",
         probe_id == "1007_s_at")

human_exprs_log2fc_sample %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))
```


Annotate probes with gene symbols by querying the Ensembl BioMart database.

```{r}
########### Filter and annotate probes -----
# Configure Ensembl BioMart
ensembl_mart <- useMart("ensembl")
# listDatasets(ensembl_mart)
ensembl_mart <- useDataset("hsapiens_gene_ensembl", mart = ensembl_mart)

# Get probe IDs from expression matrix
gene_id <- human_exprs_log2fc_sample$probe_id %>% unique()

# Annotate data
annot <- getBM(
  attributes = c("affy_hg_u133a_2",
                 "ensembl_gene_id",
                 "entrezgene_id",
                 "hgnc_symbol",
                 "description"),
  filters = "affy_hg_u133a_2",
  values = gene_id,
  mart = ensembl_mart) %>% 
  #Standardize
  rename(probe = affy_hg_u133a_2,
                     entrezgene_id = entrezgene_id,
                     human_symbol = hgnc_symbol,
                     ensembl_id = ensembl_gene_id)

#Filter genes with highest median expression
human_log2summary = human_exprs %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe") %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -probe,
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "expression") %>% 
# Group by probe ID to collapse multiple probe-to-gene mappings later
  group_by(probe) %>% 
# Compute per-probe summary statistics (mean, median) across all samples to select the most representative probe
  summarise(mean = mean(expression,na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(expression, na.rm = T)) %>%  
# Join BioMart gene annotation to expression data by probe ID: adds gene symbol, Entrez ID, and description
  inner_join(annot, 
            by = "probe") %>% 
  # Collapse to one row per Ensembl ID
  group_by(ensembl_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-ensembl_id) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  
  # Collapse to one row per Entrez ID
  group_by(entrezgene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%  #21.863 probes/entrez_ids
  ungroup()  


#Filter out genes with multiple hgnc_symbols
hgnc_symbol_dupes = human_log2summary %>% 
  #filter ensembl id with multiple hgnc_symbols
  get_dupes(human_symbol)

human_log2summary = human_log2summary %>% 
  filter(!human_symbol %in% c(hgnc_symbol_dupes$human_symbol %>% unique())) 

# Build filtered expression matrix with human symbols

# Join expression with annotation, keep only mapped probes
human_log2_filtered_probes = human_exprs %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe") %>% 
# Join expression data with annotation by probe ID: adds gene symbols to raw probe-level measurements
  inner_join(human_log2summary, by = "probe") %>%   #214,396
  select(human_symbol, probe,
         c(human_metadata$geo_sample))
#14395
human_log2_filtered_probes %>% dim()

human_log2_filtered_probes = human_log2_filtered_probes 

human_log2_filtered_probes %>% 
# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
  get_dupes(human_symbol)

#Save 
human_log2_filtered_probes %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
```

```{r}
         timepoint = as.factor(timepoint),

eset_human <- ExpressionSet(
  assayData = human_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
    select(-probe) %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
    column_to_rownames("human_symbol") %>% 
    select(c(human_metadata_eset$geo_sample)) %>% 
    as.matrix(),
# Convert metadata to AnnotatedDataFrame: formal phenotype data structure required by ExpressionSet
  phenoData = AnnotatedDataFrame(human_metadata_eset))
```

### Differential expression

#### Limma

##### All samples
Load the S. aureus human dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r}
# Load data
eset_human = readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_eset.rds"))

# Filter low-expressed genes (log2 > 6 in >= 5 samples)
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_human) %>%
as.data.frame() %>%
mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>%
rowSums() %>%
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_human[genes_to_keep, ]

# Build design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ pathogen +
                         age +
                         sex +
                         ethnicity +
                         batch_experimental,
                       data = pData(eset_filtered))

# Ensure syntactically valid column names: replaces spaces/special characters with dots for model.matrix compatibility
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))  
rownames(design) <- rownames(pData(eset_filtered))


# Estimate sample-specific quality weights using arrayWeights: down-weights arrays with excessive noise to improve statistical power
aw <- arrayWeights(eset_filtered, design,
                   var.group = eset_filtered$batch_experimental
                   )
barplot(
  aw,
  names.arg = eset_filtered$condition,
  main = "Sample Weights Diagnostic",
  ylab = "Weight",
  las = 2,
  cex.names = 0.7,
  col = "skyblue"
)

# Fit linear model
fit <- lmFit(eset_filtered, 
             design,
             weights = aw
             ) 

# List available conditions
colnames(design) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  arrange(.)

# Define contrasts
cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(pathogenStaphylococcus.aureus, levels = design)

# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont.matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink gene-wise variances toward a common value: improves stability for low-variance genes
fit2 <- limma::eBayes(fit2,
                      robust = T,
                      trend = T
                      )

# Diagnostic plot: scatterplot of log2 residual variance vs average expression (should show no strong trend after moderation)
plotSA(fit2, main = "Sigma vs Abundance (Weights Applied)")

# Extract DEGs for every contrast
# For every contrast
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2), function(i) {
# Extract differentially expressed genes using the treat method (tests whether log2FC exceeds a minimum threshold, not just non-zero)
  topTreat(fit2, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(comparison = colnames(fit2)[i]) %>%
    rownames_to_column("symbol")
  })

# Combine all results
all_contrasts_degs <- bind_rows(results_list)

# Get all DEGs and clean dataset
all_degs_human = all_contrasts_degs %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  dplyr::select(comparison, everything()) %>% 
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  dplyr::mutate(condition = case_when(comparison == "pathogenStaphylococcus.aureus"	~ "Saureus_Day1",
                               T~comparison),
         organism = "Human",
         timepoint = "1") %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  dplyr::select(condition, everything()) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  dplyr::rename(human_symbol = symbol,
         mean_l2fc = log_fc,
         ci_upper = ci_r,
         ci_lower = ci_l)

all_degs_human %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(condition) %>%
  dplyr::filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
# Count the number of differentially expressed genes (adj.p ≤ 0.05) per comparison
  dplyr::summarise(n_degs = n())

#Save
all_degs_human %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

```


##### Subsampling

Run the subsampling loop to assess the impact of cohort composition on differential expression results.

```{r Subsampling loop}
## 1. Load and Pre-Filter ExpressionSet Data
eset_human <- readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_eset.rds"))
human_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_metadata.rds"))

# Filtering genes with intensity > 6 (log2) in at least 5 samples
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_human) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>%
  rowSums() %>%
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_human[genes_to_keep, ]
meta_df <- as_tibble(pData(eset_filtered), rownames = "sample_id")
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
expr_matrix <- exprs(eset_filtered)

## 2. Defensive Subsampling Function (Independent Samples)
# Samples independent individuals balanced by pathogen status
draw_flexible_subset <- function(metadata, target_n = 10) {
  valid_draw <- FALSE
  attempts <- 0
  
  while(!valid_draw) {
    attempts <- attempts + 1
    if(attempts > 500) stop("Could not find a balanced subset.")
    
    # Sample target_n independent samples
    sub_meta <- metadata %>% 
      group_by(pathogen) %>%
      sample_n(target_n) %>% 
      ungroup()
    
    # Ensure both pathogen classes are present
    has_diversity <- (length(unique(sub_meta$pathogen)) > 1)
    
    if(has_diversity) valid_draw <- TRUE
  }
  return(sub_meta)
}

## 3. Multi-Iteration Simulation Loop

n_iterations <- 200 
cohort_n <- 10      

# Set random seed for reproducibility: ensures that subsampling draws the same iterations across runs
set.seed(123) 

df_global_runs <- tibble(iteration = 1:n_iterations) %>%
  mutate(
# Apply the sampling function to each iteration: generates a list-column of sampled metadata sets
    sampled_metadata = map(iteration, ~ draw_flexible_subset(meta_df, target_n = cohort_n)),
    
# Apply Limma to each subsample: fits a linear model per iteration to assess DEG stability
    limma_results = map(sampled_metadata, ~ {
      sub_meta <- .x
      sub_expr <- expr_matrix[, sub_meta$sample_id]
      
      # Design matrix: pathogen + batch_experimental (as requested)
      design_sub <- model.matrix(~ pathogen + batch_experimental, data = sub_meta)
      colnames(design_sub) <- make.names(colnames(design_sub))
      
      # Array weights (including batch_experimental)
      aw_sub <- arrayWeights(sub_expr, design_sub, var.group = sub_meta$batch_experimental)
      
      # Fit Limma model
      fit_sub <- lmFit(sub_expr, design = design_sub, weights = aw_sub) 
      
      # Contrasts (pathogenStaphylococcus.aureus vs reference/control)
      cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(pathogenStaphylococcus.aureus, levels = design_sub)
      
      # Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2_sub <- contrasts.fit(fit_sub, cont.matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink gene-wise variances toward a common value: improves stability for low-variance genes
      fit2_sub <- eBayes(fit2_sub, robust = TRUE, trend = TRUE)
      
      # Extract results
      res_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2_sub), function(i) {
        # Extract DEGs for this contrast using topTreat
        df_res <- topTreat(fit2_sub, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE)
        df_res$symbol <- rownames(df_res)
        df_res$comparison <- colnames(fit2_sub)[i]
        rownames(df_res) <- NULL
        return(df_res)
      })
      
# Row-bind all contrast results into a single data frame: combines list of per-contrast results into a tidy DEG table
      do.call(rbind, res_list)
    })
  )

## 4. Data Processing & Summary
saureus_human_subsampled_degs <- df_global_runs %>%
  select(iteration, limma_results) %>%
# Unnest the list-column of Limma results into a flat data frame: one row per gene × comparison × iteration
  unnest(limma_results) %>%
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>%
    #Calculate errors by iteration
  mutate(
    se_iteration = abs(log_fc / t),
    sd_iteration = se_iteration / sqrt(0.4) # N = 5
  ) %>% 
  group_by(comparison, symbol) %>%
  summarise(
    p_value = median(p_value),
    adj_p_val = median(adj_p_val),
    mean_l2fc = median(log_fc),
    sd_sampling_stability = sd(log_fc),
    se = median(se_iteration),
    sd = median(sd_iteration),
    ci_lower = median(ci_l),
    ci_upper = median(ci_r),
    t = median(t),
    b = median(b),
    ave_expr = median(ave_expr),
    pct_iterations_significant = mean(adj_p_val <= 0.05) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(condition = "Saureus_Day1", organism = "Human", timepoint = "24") %>% 
  rename(human_symbol = symbol)

# Save
saureus_human_subsampled_degs %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_dge_subsampled_degs.rds"))

# Summary report
saureus_human_subsampled_degs %>% 
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
  summarise(n_robust_degs = n()) %>% 
  print()
```

Demographics
Visualise the demographic composition (age, sex, race) across subsampling iterations to confirm balance.
Visualise demographic composition across subsampling iterations.
```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=6}
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(tidyverse)
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(patchwork)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. PROCESS SIMULATION ITERATIONS DATA (RAW METRICS)
# ==============================================================================
# Calculate mean age and male proportions per loop iteration
demographics_summary <- df_global_runs %>%
  select(iteration, sampled_metadata) %>%
  unnest(sampled_metadata) %>%
# Extract demographic columns (age, sex, race) per iteration for visualisation
  select(iteration, participant_id, age, sex) %>%
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>%
  group_by(iteration) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_age   = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    prop_male  = mean(sex == "male", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(iteration = factor(iteration, levels = 1:max(iteration)))

# Separate long format extraction for categorical group distributions
subsample_race_distribution <- df_global_runs %>%
  select(iteration, sampled_metadata) %>%
  unnest(sampled_metadata) %>%
  select(iteration, participant_id, ethnicity) %>%
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>%
# Count participants per race category in each iteration for proportion calculations
  dplyr::count(iteration, ethnicity) %>%
  group_by(iteration) %>%
# Convert counts to proportions: facilitates stacked bar charts of demographic distributions
  mutate(Proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(iteration = factor(iteration, levels = 1:max(as.numeric(iteration)))) 

# ==============================================================================
# 2. BUILD TOP PANEL: SUBSAMPLING RUNS (n=5 PER ITERATION)
# ==============================================================================

# Block A: Raw Mean Age Matrix Tiles with Explicit Number Rendering
plot_age <- ggplot(demographics_summary, aes(x = "Mean Age", y = iteration)) +
# Add tile layer: creates a heatmap-like grid where colour encodes numeric values (e.g. mean age per iteration)
  geom_tile(aes(fill = mean_age), color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
# Add text annotation to tiles: displays the numeric mean age value inside each tile
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", mean_age)), 
            color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
# Apply viridis continuous colour scale: perceptually uniform colour mapping for numeric fill values
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", name = "Mean Age\n(Years)", direction = -1) +
# Configure x-axis: set position, expansion, breaks, and labels
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top", expand = c(0.01, 0.01)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0.01, 0.01)) +
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo() +
# Customise theme elements: remove/minimise gridlines, adjust axis text, and fine-tune legend placement
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid   = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "left"
  ) +
# Set informative axis labels, legend titles, and overall plot title
  labs(y = "Subsampling Iterations (n=5)")

# Block B: Subsample Sex Proportions Track
plot_sex <- demographics_summary %>%
  select(iteration, Male = prop_male) %>%
  mutate(Female = 1 - Male) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Male, Female), names_to = "Sex", values_to = "Proportion") %>%
# Initialise ggplot with aesthetic mappings: defines variables for x-axis, y-axis, colour, and fill
  ggplot(aes(x = Proportion, y = iteration, fill = Sex)) +

# Combine top sub-plots side-by-side using patchwork weights
top_panel <- plot_age + plot_sex + plot_race + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1, 1))

# ==============================================================================
# 3. BUILD BOTTOM PANEL: ORIGINAL TOTAL COHORT BASELINE (N=100)
# ==============================================================================
original_demographics <- human_metadata %>%
  mutate(age = str_remove(age, "y") %>% as.numeric()) %>% 
  select(participant_id, age, sex, ethnicity) %>%
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct()

# Baseline A: Continuous Raw Age Density Curve
base_age <- ggplot(original_demographics, aes(x = age)) +
# Add density plot: smooth distribution of age values for the full cohort baseline
  geom_density(fill = "#3182bd", alpha = 0.4, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
# Add vertical dashed line at the cohort mean age: reference for comparing subsample distributions
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(original_demographics$age, na.rm = TRUE), 
             color = "black", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
# Create faceted plot: split data into sub-panels by condition or organism for side-by-side comparison
  facet_wrap(~"Age") +
# Configure x-axis: set position, expansion, breaks, and labels
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo() +
# Customise theme elements: remove/minimise gridlines, adjust axis text, and fine-tune legend placement
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9)
  ) +
# Set informative axis labels, legend titles, and overall plot title
  labs(x = "Age (Years)", y = "Density")

# Baseline B: Total Cohort Sex Proportions Anchor Bar
base_sex <- original_demographics %>%
  dplyr::count(sex) %>%
# Convert counts to proportions: facilitates stacked bar charts of demographic distributions
  mutate(Proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
# Initialise ggplot with aesthetic mappings: defines variables for x-axis, y-axis, colour, and fill
  ggplot(aes(x = Proportion, y = "Original\nCohort (n=100)", fill = sex)) +
# Create faceted plot: split data into sub-panels by condition or organism for side-by-side comparison
  facet_wrap(~"Original\nCohort") +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = "stack", show.legend = FALSE) +
# Apply manual colour scale: uses predefined colour palette (typically from project's colour scheme)
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Male" = "#3182bd", 
                               "Female" = "#fa9fb5")) +
# Configure x-axis: set position, expansion, breaks, and labels
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo() +
# Customise theme elements: remove/minimise gridlines, adjust axis text, and fine-tune legend placement
  theme(
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )

# Baseline C: Total Cohort Race Proportions Anchor Bar (Multi-Categorical Configuration)
base_race <- original_demographics %>%
  mutate(ethnicity = str_to_title(ethnicity)) %>% 
  dplyr::count(ethnicity) %>%
# Convert counts to proportions: facilitates stacked bar charts of demographic distributions
  mutate(Proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
# Initialise ggplot with aesthetic mappings: defines variables for x-axis, y-axis, colour, and fill
  ggplot(aes(x = Proportion, y = "Original\nCohort (n=100)", fill = ethnicity)) +
# Create faceted plot: split data into sub-panels by condition or organism for side-by-side comparison
  facet_wrap(~"Race") +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = "stack", show.legend = TRUE) +
# Apply manual colour scale: uses predefined colour palette (typically from project's colour scheme)
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Race",
    values = colors$race
  ) +
# Configure x-axis: set position, expansion, breaks, and labels
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo() +
# Customise theme elements: remove/minimise gridlines, adjust axis text, and fine-tune legend placement
  theme(
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )

# Combine baseline anchors horizontally using matching grid widths
bottom_panel <- base_age + base_sex + base_race + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1, 1))

# ==============================================================================
# 4. STITCH COMPLETE GRAPHICAL CANVAS
# ==============================================================================
final_canvas <- top_panel / bottom_panel + 
  plot_layout(heights = c(4, 1), guides = "collect") +
# Add overall title to the combined figure using patchwork
  plot_annotation(title = "S. aureus infection, Human")

print(final_canvas)
```



#### T test 
Load the S. aureus human dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r}
# Load data
human_exprs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds")) 
human_metadata =  readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_metadata.rds")) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint = if_else(condition == "No infection", 0, timepoint))
log2fc_sample = readRDS(here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))
log2fc_sample_symbol = log2fc_sample %>% 
  inner_join(human_exprs %>% 
               select(human_symbol, probe_id = probe) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
               distinct(),
             by = "probe_id")

#Compute summary statistics
log2fc_summary = log2fc_sample_symbol %>% 
  group_by(human_symbol, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_log2fc = mean(log2fc, na.rm = TRUE),  # mean log2 fold change
    n_subjects = n(),                         # number of samples
    sd = sd(log2fc, na.rm = TRUE),             # standard deviation
    se = sd / sqrt(n_subjects),               # standard error
    effect_size = avg_log2fc / sd)            # Cohen’s d-like effect size

log2_hgnc_symbol_wide = human_exprs %>%
  # Reshape expression data from wide to long format
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(human_symbol, probe),
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "log2") %>% 
  # Join sample-level metadata (subject, timepoint)
  inner_join(human_metadata %>% 
               select(geo_sample, subject_id = participant_id, timepoint),
             by = "geo_sample") %>% 
  select(human_symbol, subject_id, timepoint, log2) %>% 
  # Remove duplicate probe-to-gene mappings
  distinct() %>% 
  select(subject_id, human_symbol, timepoint, value = log2) %>%
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  # Reshape to wide format with one column per timepoint
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value, names_prefix = "day_") 


#Unpaired
log2fc_unpaired_ttest = log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_day1 = tryCatch(t.test(day_1, day_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_day1  = p.adjust(pval_day1, method = "fdr")
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(day\\d+)"
  ) %>% 
  # Clean timepoint labels and annotate test type
  mutate(timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "day"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Unpaired") 

log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest = log2fc_unpaired_ttest 

log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds"))

```

### Compare DGE methods
Import t-test and Limma results and merge them for comparison of differential expression methods.

```{r}
#Import ------
#t-Test
human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest =
# Load dataset from disk or GEO: reads pre-saved expression matrix / metadata into the R environment
  readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds")) %>% 
# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human",
         timepoint = "24")
mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest =
# Load dataset from disk or GEO: reads pre-saved expression matrix / metadata into the R environment
  readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds")) %>% 
# Tag rows as Mouse: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Mouse")

#Limma
human_degs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_dge_limma_degs.rds")) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(padj = adj_p_val) %>% 
# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human",
         test = "Limma",
         paired = "Unpaired",
         timepoint = "24") 

mouse_degs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds")) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(padj = adj_p_val) %>% 
# Tag rows as Mouse: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Mouse",
         test = "Limma",
         paired = "Paired") 

#Merge datasets
degs_ttest_limma =
  bind_rows(
    human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest,
    human_degs,
    mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest,
    mouse_degs
    )

#Summarize  
degs_ttest_limma_summary = degs_ttest_limma %>% 
  group_by(organism, timepoint, test, paired) %>% 
  summarise(
    n_degs = sum(padj <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint_num = readr::parse_number(timepoint),
    timepoint = paste0(timepoint, "h"),
    timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = unique(timepoint[order(timepoint_num)]))) 

degs_ttest_limma_summary

```

```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
  ggplot(aes(
```

```{r}
#E. coli: GSE33341 -----
filename = "GSE33341"
# Download GEO ExpressionSet using GEOquery package: retrieves both expression data and phenotype metadata
GSE33341 <- getGEO("GSE33341", GSEMatrix = TRUE) 
eset_mouse <- GSE33341[[1]]
eset_human <- GSE33341[[2]]

#Metadata ------
#Mouse
ecoli_mouse_metadata = eset_mouse %>% 
  pData() %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  dplyr::select( 
    geo_sample = "geo_accession", 
    #Host
    subject_title = "title",
    subject_num = "replicate number:ch1",
    batch = "experimental batch:ch1",
    host_strain = "host strain:ch1",
    organism = "organism_ch1",
    age = "host age (yr):ch1",
    sex = "host gender:ch1", 
    #Pathogen
    pathogen = "pathogen:ch1",
    status = "infection status:ch1",
    site_infection = "anatomic site of infection:ch1",
    route_infection = "inoculum route:ch1",
    dosage = "pathogen   dosage cfu/g:ch1",
    timepoint = "time after infection (h):ch1",
    bac_strain = "bacterial strain:ch1"
    ) %>% 
  filter(pathogen %in% c("Escherichia  coli", "-")) %>%
  mutate(pathogen = if_else(pathogen == "Escherichia  coli", "escherichia coli", "none"),
         subject_id = paste0("Mouse_", host_strain, "_Animal", subject_num, "_Batch", batch),
         status = str_replace(status, "-", "Healthy"),
         condition = paste("Mouse", host_strain, timepoint, sep = "_"),
         comparison = paste0("Mouse_", host_strain, "_Batch", batch)) %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(geo_sample, comparison, condition, subject_id, everything())


#Human
ecoli_human_metadata = eset_human %>% 
  pData() %>% 
  filter(`pathogen:ch1` %in% c("Escherichia coli", "-")) %>%
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  dplyr::select( 
    geo_sample = "geo_accession", 
    #Host
    subject_title = "title",
    # subject_num = "replicate number:ch1",
    batch = "experimental batch:ch1",
    # host_strain = "host strain:ch1",
    organism = "organism_ch1",
    age = "host age (yr):ch1",
    sex = "host gender:ch1", 
    ethnicity = "ethnicity:ch1",
    #Pathogen
    pathogen = "pathogen:ch1",
    # status = "infection status:ch1",
    site_infection = "anatomic site of infection:ch1"
    # route_infection = "inoculum route:ch1",
    # dosage = "pathogen   dosage cfu/g:ch1",
    # timepoint = "time after infection (h):ch1",
    # bac_strain = "bacterial strain:ch1"
    ) %>% 
  mutate(site_infection = str_to_lower(site_infection),
         organism = "Human",
         pathogen = if_else(pathogen == "-", "Healthy", pathogen),
         status = if_else(pathogen == "Healthy", pathogen, "infected"),
         timepoint = "0",
         subject_id = if_else(pathogen == "Escherichia coli", 
                              paste0("Ecoli_human_", site_infection,"_",geo_sample), 
                              paste0("Healthy_human_", geo_sample)),
         site_infection = if_else(site_infection == "-", "none", site_infection),
         condition = subject_id) %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(geo_sample, condition, subject_id, everything()) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint = if_else(pathogen == "Escherichia coli", "24", timepoint))

ecoli_human_metadata

#Unite metadata
ecoli_mouse_human_metadata = ecoli_human_metadata %>% 
  bind_rows(ecoli_mouse_metadata)

ecoli_mouse_human_metadata %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
```

#### Mouse

##### Annotate genes

This procedure was done using only one batch (8)

```{r}
# Load data
ecoli_human_exprs = readRDS(here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_exprs.rds"))
ecoli_mouse_exprs = readRDS(here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_exprs.rds"))
ecoli_mouse_human_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_mouse_metadata.rds"))

#Annotate genes ------
#Mouse -----
#Annotate data and calculate log2fc
mouse_expression_metadata  = ecoli_mouse_exprs %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = 2:125,
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "value_raw") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(ecoli_mouse_human_metadata, 
             by = "geo_sample") 

mouse_metadata =  ecoli_mouse_human_metadata %>% 
               filter(host_strain == "C57BL/6J",
                      batch == "8")

mouse_metadata %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_metadata.rds"))

#Get value from day 0 and calculate Log2FC
log2fc_sample = mouse_expression_metadata %>% 
  #Filter batch
  filter(organism == "Mus musculus",
         status == "Healthy",
         host_strain == "C57BL/6J",
         batch == "8") %>% 
  select(probe_id, batch, subject_num, day0_value_raw = value_raw) %>% 
  #Get the mean expression value for healthy
  group_by(probe_id, batch) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            #Mean of healthy
            day0_value_raw = sum(day0_value_raw)/n,
            batch) %>% 
  select(probe_id, day0_value_raw) %>% 
  #Filter batch
  inner_join(mouse_expression_metadata %>% 
               filter(timepoint != "0",
                      host_strain == "C57BL/6J",
                      batch == "8"),
             by = join_by("probe_id", "batch")) %>% 
  # Compute log2 fold-change relative to baseline
mutate(log2fc = value_raw - day0_value_raw) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() 

#Check duplicates
log2fc_sample %>% 
  filter(subject_id == "Mouse_C57BL/6J_Animal1_Batch8",
         probe_id == "1415670_at")


#Save
```

```{r}
# Select the mouse genome (mmusculus_gene_ensembl) as the annotation dataset in BioMart

# Get probe IDs from expression matrix

# listAttributes(ensembl_mart)

  attributes = c("affy_mouse430_2",
                 "ensembl_gene_id",

                 "mgi_symbol",
                 "description"),
  filters = "affy_mouse430_2",
  values = gene_id,
  mart = ensembl_mart)

annot %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "probe_annot_ecoli_infection_mouse.rds"))

# Load mouse-to-human orthology lookup
# (Install orthology package if needed)
# library(devtools)
# devtools::install_github('shenorrLabTRDF/FIT.mouse2man')
library(FIT.mouse2man)
HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez = FIT.mouse2man::HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(mouse_entrez = mouse_ortholog)

#Get annotations for each probe 
### Filter probes with highest median expression
mouse_log2summary = ecoli_mouse_exprs %>% #20,845 probes
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rename(probe = probe_id) %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -probe,
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "expression") %>% 
# Group by probe ID to collapse multiple probe-to-gene mappings later
  group_by(probe) %>% 
# Compute per-probe summary statistics (mean, median) across all samples to select the most representative probe
  summarise(mean = mean(expression,na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(expression, na.rm = T)) %>%  
# Join BioMart gene annotation to expression data by probe ID: adds gene symbol, Entrez ID, and description
  inner_join(annot %>% 
              rename(probe = affy_mouse430_2), 
            by = "probe") %>%  #24.009 rows
  # Collapse to one row per Ensembl ID
  group_by(ensembl_gene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-ensembl_gene_id) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  
  # Collapse to one row per Entrez ID
  group_by(entrezgene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%  #21.863 probes/entrez_ids
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(mouse_entrez = entrezgene_id) %>% 
  
  # Join human orthologs, collapse to one row per HGNC symbol
  inner_join(HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez, by = c("mouse_entrez", "mgi_symbol")) %>% 
# Group by human gene symbol: after orthology mapping, collapse mouse genes that map to the same human gene
  group_by(hgnc_symbol) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1)  %>% #14.396
  ungroup()

# Remove HGNC symbols with multiple MGI mappings
hgnc_symbol_dupes = mouse_log2summary %>% 
  #filter ensembl id with multiple mgi_symbols
  get_dupes(hgnc_symbol)

mouse_log2summary = mouse_log2summary %>% 
  select(probe, hgnc_symbol) %>% 
# Remove genes with ambiguous human symbol mappings: retains only one-to-one mouse-to-human orthologs
  filter(!hgnc_symbol %in% c(hgnc_symbol_dupes$hgnc_symbol %>% unique())) 

# Build filtered expression matrix with human symbols

# Join expression with annotation, keep only mapped probes
mouse_log2_filtered_probes = ecoli_mouse_exprs %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rename(probe = probe_id) %>% 
# Join expression data with annotation by probe ID: adds gene symbols to raw probe-level measurements
  inner_join(mouse_log2summary, by = "probe") %>%   #214,396
  select(human_symbol = hgnc_symbol, 
         probe,
         c(mouse_metadata %>% 
             pull(geo_sample)))
#14395
mouse_log2_filtered_probes %>% dim()

mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol = mouse_log2_filtered_probes 

mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
  get_dupes(human_symbol)

mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol %>%

  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol_long.rds"))
```

###### Limma
Paired samples design
```{r}

# Load data
ecoli_mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol_long.rds"))
ecoli_mouse_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_metadata.rds"))
eset_mouse_ecoli = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_eset.rds"))

# Filter low-expressed genes (log2 > 6 in >= 5 samples)
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_mouse_ecoli) %>%
as.data.frame() %>%
mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>%
rowSums() %>%
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_mouse_ecoli[genes_to_keep, ]

# Build design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ condition + 0, # 0 defines the way we compare the samples
                       eset_filtered) 

# Ensure syntactically valid column names: replaces spaces/special characters with dots for model.matrix compatibility
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))  # Avoids blank spaces

# Estimate the correlation between measurements made on the same subject (paired-samples)
corfit <- duplicateCorrelation(eset_filtered, 
                               design = design, 
                               block = eset_filtered$subject_id)
corfit$consensus #-0.06

# Estimate sample-specific quality weights using arrayWeights: down-weights arrays with excessive noise to improve statistical power
aw <- arrayWeights(eset_filtered, design)
barplot(
  aw,
  names.arg = eset_filtered$condition,
  main = "Sample Weights Diagnostic",
  ylab = "Weight",
  las = 2,
  cex.names = 0.7,
  col = "skyblue"
)



# Fit linear model
fit <- lmFit(eset_filtered, 
             design, 
             weights = aw,
             block = eset_filtered$subject_id, 
             correlation = corfit$consensus)

# List available conditions
colnames(design) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  arrange(.)

# Define contrasts
cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(conditionMouse_C57BL.6J_2	 - conditionMouse_C57BL.6J_0,
                             conditionMouse_C57BL.6J_6	 - conditionMouse_C57BL.6J_0,
                             conditionMouse_C57BL.6J_12	 - conditionMouse_C57BL.6J_0,
                             conditionMouse_C57BL.6J_24	 - conditionMouse_C57BL.6J_0,
                             levels=design)
# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont.matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink gene-wise variances toward a common value: improves stability for low-variance genes
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2,
               robust = T,
               trend = T)

# Diagnostic plot: scatterplot of log2 residual variance vs average expression (should show no strong trend after moderation)
plotSA(fit2, main = "Sigma vs Abundance (Weights Applied)")

# Extract DEGs for every contrast

## For every contrast
# Iterate over each contrast column: extract DEGs from every comparison in one pass
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2), function(i) {
# Extract differentially expressed genes using the treat method (tests whether log2FC exceeds a minimum threshold, not just non-zero)
  topTreat(fit2, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(comparison = colnames(fit2)[i]) %>% 
    rownames_to_column("symbol")
  })

# Combine all results
all_contrasts_degs <- bind_rows(results_list)

# Get all DEGs and clean dataset
all_degs_mouse_ecoli= all_contrasts_degs %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  select(comparison, everything()) %>% 
  mutate(comparison = str_replace(comparison, "\\.\\.\\.", "_") %>% 
           str_replace(., "timepoint", "Time") %>% 
           str_replace(., "treatment", "")) %>% 
# Split contrast name into comparison and reference columns (e.g. 'Time1 - Time0' → comparisonA / comparisonRef)
  separate(comparison, sep = " - ", into = c("comparisonA", "comparisonRef")) %>% 
  mutate(comparisonRef = str_replace(comparisonRef, "treatment", "Time0")) %>% 
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  mutate(condition = case_when(comparisonA == "conditionMouse_C57BL.6J_2"	~ "Ecoli_2h",
                               comparisonA == "conditionMouse_C57BL.6J_6"	~ "Ecoli_6h",
                               comparisonA == "conditionMouse_C57BL.6J_12"	~ "Ecoli_12h",
                               comparisonA == "conditionMouse_C57BL.6J_24"	~ "Ecoli_24h",
                               T~comparisonA),
         organism = "Mouse",
         timepoint = str_remove(condition, "Ecoli_") %>% str_remove("h")) %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(condition, everything()) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(human_symbol = symbol,
         mean_l2fc = log_fc,
         ci_upper = ci_r,
         ci_lower = ci_l)
	
# #Save
all_degs_mouse_ecoli %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

all_degs_mouse_ecoli %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
# Count the number of differentially expressed genes (adj.p ≤ 0.05) per comparison
  summarise(n_degs = n())

```



###### T test
Load the E. coli mouse dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r}
# Load data
mouse_exprs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol_long.rds"))
mouse_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_metadata.rds"))
log2fc_sample = readRDS(here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))
log2fc_sample_symbol = log2fc_sample %>% 
  inner_join(mouse_exprs %>% 
               select(human_symbol, probe_id = probe),
             by = "probe_id")

```


Compute summary statistics and perform paired and unpaired t-tests for each timepoint.

```{r}
#Compute summary statistics
log2fc_summary = log2fc_sample_symbol %>% 
  group_by(human_symbol, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_log2fc = mean(log2fc, na.rm = TRUE),  # mean log2 fold change
    n_subjects = n(),                         # number of samples
    sd = sd(log2fc, na.rm = TRUE),             # standard deviation
    se = sd / sqrt(n_subjects),               # standard error
    effect_size = avg_log2fc / sd)            # Cohen’s d-like effect size

log2_hgnc_symbol_wide = mouse_exprs %>%
  select(-probe) %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -human_symbol,
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "log2") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(mouse_metadata %>% 
               select(geo_sample, subject_id, timepoint),
             by = "geo_sample") %>% 
  select(human_symbol, subject_id, timepoint, log2) %>% 
  # Remove duplicate probe-to-gene mappings
  distinct() %>% 
  select(subject_id, human_symbol, timepoint, value = log2) %>%
  # Reshape to wide format with one column per timepoint
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value, names_prefix = "hour_") 

# Paired t-test
log2fc_paired_ttest <- log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_hour2 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_2, hour_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_hour6 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_6, hour_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_hour12 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_12, hour_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap paired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with insufficient paired observations (e.g. missing baseline)
    pval_hour24 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_24, hour_0, paired = TRUE, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_hour2 = p.adjust(pval_hour2, method = "fdr"),
    padj_hour6 = p.adjust(pval_hour6, method = "fdr"),
    padj_hour12 = p.adjust(pval_hour12, method = "fdr"),
    padj_hour24 = p.adjust(pval_hour24, method = "fdr"),
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(hour\\d+)"
  ) %>% 
  # Clean timepoint labels and annotate test type
  mutate(timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "hour"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Paired")

#Unpaired
log2fc_unpaired_ttest = log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
  # Compute paired/unpaired t-test for each gene at each timepoint vs baseline
  summarise(
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_hour2 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_2, hour_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_hour6 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_6, hour_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_hour12 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_12, hour_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
# Wrap unpaired t-test in tryCatch: returns NA for genes with zero variance or insufficient samples
    pval_hour24 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_24, hour_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
  # Apply FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) to p-values
  mutate(
    padj_hour2 = p.adjust(pval_hour2, method = "fdr"),
    padj_hour6 = p.adjust(pval_hour6, method = "fdr"),
    padj_hour12 = p.adjust(pval_hour12, method = "fdr"),
    padj_hour24 = p.adjust(pval_hour24, method = "fdr"),
  ) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(hour\\d+)"
  ) %>% 
  # Clean timepoint labels and annotate test type
  mutate(timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "hour"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Unpaired") 

log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest = log2fc_unpaired_ttest %>% 
  bind_rows(log2fc_paired_ttest) 

log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds"))

```

###### Limma
Load the E. coli human dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r}

# Load data
human_ecoli_log2_filtered_symbol = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
ecoli_human_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_metadata.rds"))
eset_human_ecoli = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_eset.rds"))


# Filter low-expressed genes (log2 > 6 in >= 5 samples)
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_human_ecoli) %>%
as.data.frame() %>%
mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>%
rowSums() %>%
{ . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_human_ecoli[genes_to_keep, ]

# Build design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ status + age + sex + ethnicity,
                       data = pData(eset_filtered))

# Ensure syntactically valid column names: replaces spaces/special characters with dots for model.matrix compatibility
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))  # Avoids blank spaces
rownames(design) <- rownames(pData(eset_filtered))

# Estimate sample-specific quality weights using arrayWeights: down-weights arrays with excessive noise to improve statistical power
aw <- arrayWeights(eset_filtered, design)
# Barplot of array weights: visual diagnostic to identify low-quality arrays (bars near zero indicate problematic samples)
barplot(aw,
names.arg = eset_filtered$condition,
main = "Sample Weights Diagnostic",
ylab = "Weight",
las = 2,
cex.names = 0.7,
col = "skyblue")

# Fit linear model
fit <- lmFit(eset_filtered, 
             design,
             weights = aw) 

# List available conditions
colnames(design) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  arrange(.)

# Define contrasts
cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(statusinfected, levels = design)

# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont.matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink gene-wise variances toward a common value: improves stability for low-variance genes
fit2 <- limma::eBayes(fit2,
                      trend = T,
                      robust = T)

# Diagnostic plot: scatterplot of log2 residual variance vs average expression (should show no strong trend after moderation)
plotSA(fit2, main = "Sigma vs Abundance (Weights Applied)")

# Extract DEGs for every contrast

## For every contrast
# Iterate over each contrast column: extract DEGs from every comparison in one pass
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2), function(i) {
# Extract differentially expressed genes using the treat method (tests whether log2FC exceeds a minimum threshold, not just non-zero)
  topTreat(fit2, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(comparison = colnames(fit2)[i]) %>% 
    rownames_to_column("symbol")
  })

# Combine all results
all_contrasts_degs <- bind_rows(results_list)

# Get all DEGs and clean dataset
all_degs_human_ecoli= all_contrasts_degs %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  dplyr::select(comparison, everything()) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(comparison = str_replace(comparison, "\\.\\.\\.", "_") %>% 
           str_replace(., "timepoint", "Time") %>% 
           str_replace(., "treatment", "")) %>% 
# Split contrast name into comparison and reference columns (e.g. 'Time1 - Time0' → comparisonA / comparisonRef)
  separate(comparison, sep = " - ", into = c("comparisonA", "comparisonRef")) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(comparisonRef = str_replace(comparisonRef, "treatment", "Time0")) %>% 
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  dplyr::mutate(condition = case_when(comparisonA == "statusinfected"	~ "Ecoli_24h",
                               T~comparisonA),
         organism = "Human",
        timepoint = str_remove(condition, "Ecoli_") %>% str_remove("h")) %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  dplyr::select(condition, everything()) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  dplyr::rename(human_symbol = symbol,
         mean_l2fc = log_fc,
         ci_upper = ci_r,
         ci_lower = ci_l)
	
# #Save
all_degs_human_ecoli %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

all_degs_human_ecoli %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(condition) %>%
  dplyr::filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
# Count the number of differentially expressed genes (adj.p ≤ 0.05) per comparison
  dplyr::summarise(n_degs = n())

```



####### Subsampling

Run the subsampling loop to assess the impact of cohort composition on differential expression results.

```{r Subsampling loop}
## 1. Load Data & Prepare ExpressionSet
human_metadata <- readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_metadata.rds"))
eset_human <- readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_eset.rds"))

# Filtering genes with intensity > 6 (log2) in at least 5 samples
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_human) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>%
  rowSums() %>%
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_human[genes_to_keep, ]
meta_df <- honest_df <- as_tibble(pData(eset_filtered), rownames = "sample_id")
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
expr_matrix <- exprs(eset_filtered)

# Slices exactly n_per_status arrays per distinct clinical phenotype group
draw_stratified_samples_ecoli <- function(metadata, n_per_status = 5) {
  valid_draw <- FALSE
  attempts <- 0
  
  while(!valid_draw) {
    attempts <- attempts + 1
    if(attempts > 2000) stop("Could not find a mathematically stable stratified sample subset.")
    
    # Explicitly slice exactly 5 control/healthy and 5 infected sample arrays
    sub_meta <- metadata %>%
      group_by(status) %>%
      slice_sample(n = n_per_status, replace = FALSE) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      mutate(
        status = as.factor(status),
        sex = as.factor(sex)
      )
    
    # Check 1: Verify both phenotypic statuses are captured in the slice
    has_all_conditions <- (length(unique(sub_meta$status)) == 2)
    
    # Check 2: Verify both Sexes are captured to avoid model matrix collinearity
    has_sex_diversity   <- (length(unique(sub_meta$sex)) > 1)
    
    if(has_all_conditions && has_sex_diversity) {
      # Direct model formula structure: status + age + sex + 0
      test_design <- model.matrix(~ status, data = sub_meta)
      colnames(test_design) <- make.names(colnames(test_design))
      
      # Confirm the subset design matrix is full rank (invertible)
      bad_coefs <- limma::nonEstimable(test_design)
      if(is.null(bad_coefs)) {
        valid_draw <- TRUE
      }
    }
  }
  return(sub_meta)
}

## 3. Multi-Iteration Simulation Loop

n_iterations <- 200 
samples_per_group <- 5  # 5 control/healthy + 5 infected = 10 total samples per iteration

# Set random seed for reproducibility: ensures that subsampling draws the same iterations across runs
set.seed(123) 

df_global_runs <- tibble(iteration = 1:n_iterations) %>%
  mutate(
    # Draw sample configurations via the corrected stratified logic
    sampled_metadata = map(iteration, ~ draw_stratified_samples_ecoli(meta_df, n_per_status = samples_per_group)),
    
# Apply Limma to each subsample: fits a linear model per iteration to assess DEG stability
    limma_results = map(sampled_metadata, ~ {
      sub_meta <- .x
      sub_expr <- expr_matrix[, sub_meta$sample_id]
      
      # Build the multivariable model matrix matching your original setup
      design_sub <- model.matrix(~ status, data = sub_meta)
      colnames(design_sub) <- make.names(colnames(design_sub))
      
      # Compute localized array weights natively at the sample level
      aw_sub <- arrayWeights(sub_expr, design_sub)
      
      # Fit linear model directly without block correlation factors
      fit_sub <- lmFit(sub_expr, design = design_sub, weights = aw_sub)
      
      # Define directional mathematical contrasts matching column identities
      cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(
        statusinfected,
        levels = design_sub
      )
      
      # Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2_sub <- contrasts.fit(fit_sub, cont.matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink gene-wise variances toward a common value: improves stability for low-variance genes
      fit2_sub <- eBayes(fit2_sub, robust = TRUE, trend = TRUE)
      
      res_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2_sub), function(i) {
        # Extract DEGs for this contrast using topTreat
        df_res <- topTreat(fit2_sub, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE)
        df_res$symbol <- rownames(df_res)
        df_res$comparison <- colnames(fit2_sub)[i]
        rownames(df_res) <- NULL
        return(df_res)
      })
      
# Row-bind all contrast results into a single data frame: combines list of per-contrast results into a tidy DEG table
      do.call(rbind, res_list)
    })
  )

## 4. Data Processing & Summary
ecoli_human_subsampled_degs <- df_global_runs %>%
  select(iteration, limma_results) %>%
# Unnest the list-column of Limma results into a flat data frame: one row per gene × comparison × iteration
  unnest(limma_results) %>%
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
   clean_names() %>%
    #Calculate errors by iteration
  mutate(
    se_iteration = abs(log_fc / t),
    sd_iteration = se_iteration / sqrt(0.4) # N = 5
  ) %>% 
  group_by(comparison, symbol) %>%
  summarise(
    p_value = median(p_value),
    adj_p_val = median(adj_p_val),
    mean_l2fc = median(log_fc),
    sd_sampling_stability = sd(log_fc),
    se = median(se_iteration),
    sd = median(sd_iteration),
    ci_lower = median(ci_l),
    ci_upper = median(ci_r),
    t = median(t),
    b = median(b),
    ave_expr = median(ave_expr),
    pct_iterations_significant = mean(adj_p_val <= 0.05) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
# Map timepoint codes to human-readable condition labels (condition_timepoint_celltype format)
  dplyr::mutate(condition = case_when(comparison == "statusinfected"	~ "Ecoli_24h",
                               T~comparison),
         organism = "Human",
        timepoint = str_remove(condition, "Ecoli_") %>% 
          str_remove("h")
        ) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(human_symbol = symbol) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() 

# Save
ecoli_human_subsampled_degs %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_dge_subsampled_degs.rds"))

# Summary report
ecoli_human_subsampled_degs %>% 
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
  summarise(n_robust_degs = n()) %>% 
  print()
```

###### T test
Load the E. coli human dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r}
# Load data
human_exprs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
human_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_metadata.rds"))
log2fc_sample = readRDS(here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))
log2fc_sample_symbol = log2fc_sample %>% 
  inner_join(human_exprs %>% 
               select(human_symbol, probe_id = probe),
             by = "probe_id")


#Compute summary statistics
log2fc_summary = log2fc_sample_symbol %>% 
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_log2fc = mean(log2fc, na.rm = TRUE),  # mean log2 fold change
    n_subjects = n(),                         # number of samples
    sd = sd(log2fc, na.rm = TRUE),             # standard deviation
    se = sd / sqrt(n_subjects),               # standard error
    effect_size = avg_log2fc / sd)            # Cohen’s d-like effect size

log2_hgnc_symbol_wide = log2fc_sample_symbol %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(human_metadata %>% 
               select(geo_sample, timepoint),
             by = "geo_sample") %>% 
  select(human_symbol, subject_id, timepoint, day0_value_raw, value_raw) %>% 
  # Remove duplicate probe-to-gene mappings
  distinct() %>% 
  select(subject_id, human_symbol, timepoint, hour_0 = day0_value_raw, value = value_raw) %>%
  # Reshape to wide format with one column per timepoint
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value, names_prefix = "hour_")

#Unpaired
log2fc_unpaired_ttest = log2_hgnc_symbol_wide %>%
  group_by(human_symbol) %>%
  
# Compute paired or unpaired t-test per gene comparing each post-baseline timepoint to baseline
  summarise(pval_hour24 = tryCatch(t.test(hour_24, hour_0, paired = F, var.equal = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  
# Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) correction to raw p-values: controls the expected proportion of false discoveries among rejected hypotheses
  mutate(padj_hour24 = p.adjust(pval_hour24, method = "fdr")) %>% 
  # Reshape from wide to long, splitting pval/padj into separate columns
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("pval_", "padj_")),
    names_to = c(".value", "timepoint"),
    names_pattern = "(pval|padj)_(hour\\d+)"
  ) %>% 
  # Clean timepoint labels and annotate test type
  mutate(timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "hour"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Unpaired") 


log2fc_unpaired_ttest %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_log2fc_unpaired_ttest.rds"))

```






## Combine datasets

Combine differential expression results from human and mouse datasets for cross-species comparison.

```{r}

#Merge DGE results ===========
all_degs_mouse = read_rds(here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds")) %>% 
  mutate(se = abs(mean_l2fc / t),
         #N = 5
         sd = se / sqrt(5))

all_degs_human = read_rds(here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_dge_subsampled_degs.rds"))

all_degs_human_mouse = all_degs_mouse %>% 
# Merge DEG results from all conditions into a unified table: enables cross-pathogen comparison of transcriptional responses
  bind_rows(all_degs_human)

#Save
all_degs_human_mouse %>% saveRDS(here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

               select(human_symbol, probe_id = probe),

# Tag rows as Mouse: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results

# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human",

human_mouse_ecoli_log2fc_samples = bind_rows(mouse_log2fc_sample_symbol, human_log2fc_sample_symbol) %>%

human_mouse_ecoli_log2fc_samples %>%
```

#### Compare DGE methods
Import t-test and Limma results and merge them for comparison of differential expression methods.

```{r}
#Import ------
#t-Test
human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest =
# Load dataset from disk or GEO: reads pre-saved expression matrix / metadata into the R environment
  readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_log2fc_unpaired_ttest.rds")) %>% 
# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human")
mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest =
# Load dataset from disk or GEO: reads pre-saved expression matrix / metadata into the R environment
  readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds")) %>% 
# Tag rows as Mouse: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Mouse")

#Limma
human_degs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_dge_limma_degs.rds")) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(padj = adj_p_val) %>% 
# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human",
         test = "Limma",
         paired = "Unpaired") 

mouse_degs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "ecoli_infection_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds")) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(padj = adj_p_val) %>% 
# Tag rows as Mouse: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Mouse",
         test = "Limma",
         paired = "Paired") 

#Merge datasets
degs_ttest_limma =
  bind_rows(
    human_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest,
    human_degs,
    mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest,
    mouse_degs
    )

#Summarize  
degs_ttest_limma_summary = degs_ttest_limma %>% 
  group_by(organism, timepoint, test, paired) %>% 
  summarise(
    n_degs = sum(padj <= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint_num = readr::parse_number(timepoint),
    timepoint = paste0(timepoint, "h"),
    timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = unique(timepoint[order(timepoint_num)]))) 

degs_ttest_limma_summary

```


Plot the number of DEGs identified by each method (t-test vs Limma) across significance levels.

```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=5}
# Plot number of DEGs per test and significance level
degs_ttest_limma_summary_plot_gg <- degs_ttest_limma_summary %>%
# Initialise ggplot with aesthetic mappings: defines variables for x-axis, y-axis, colour, and fill
  ggplot(aes(
    x = timepoint,
    y = n_degs,
    fill = test,
    alpha = paired
  )) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, position = position_dodge2()) +
  
  # Manual colors per test
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "t-Test" = "gray25",
    "Limma" = "#4DBBD5FF"
  )) +
  
  # Alpha: paired = 1, unpaired = 0.5
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("Paired" = 1, "Unpaired" = 0.2)) +
  
  # Continuous x-axis for numeric timepoints
  scale_x_discrete(
    breaks = sort(unique(degs_ttest_limma_summary$timepoint)),
    expand = c(0.01, 0.01)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo() +

    title = "Total DEGs by test and timepoint",
    subtitle = "Comparison across tests (FDR ≤ 0.05)",
    x = "Day",
    y = "Number of DEGs",
    fill = "Test",
    alpha = "Pairing"
  ) +
# Create faceted plot: split data into sub-panels by condition or organism for side-by-side comparison
  facet_wrap(~organism, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
# Customise theme elements: remove/minimise gridlines, adjust axis text, and fine-tune legend placement
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    axis.line.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "gray75", linetype = 3),

  )

# Render plot
```

##Download datasets

### Human

#### Trauma, Human (GSE36809)
Clinical metadata were curated and standardized to ensure consistency across the dataset. The time elapsed since injury, originally recorded in hours, was converted to days and rounded to one decimal place. To account for the irregular temporal distribution of samples, timepoints were discretized into seven categorical bins: <1 day (Early Hours), 1–2 days, 2–5 days, 5–10 days, 10–18 days, 18–25 days, and >25 days. Samples were stratified into 'Trauma' and 'Control' groups based on subject identifiers. Rigorous quality control was applied by excluding samples explicitly flagged in the metadata for low RNA quality or incomplete temporal data. Finally, temporal bins were treated as ordered factors to facilitate downstream differential expression modeling.

```{r eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, cache = TRUE}
#Download datasets
filename = "trauma_human"
GSE_matrix <- getGEO(filename = here("tables", "GSE36809_series_matrix.txt.gz"), 
                     GSEMatrix = T)

#Get Expression Set
eset <- GSE_matrix

#Get metadata -------
GSE_metadata = eset %>% Biobase::pData()

#Select, clean, and standardize attributes
GSE_metadata_annotated = GSE_metadata %>% 
  select(geo_sample = "geo_accession",
         sample_id = "source_name_ch1",
         description = title,
         tissue = `tissue:ch1`,
         sex = `Sex:ch1`,
         age = "age:ch1",
         timepoint = `hours_since_injury:ch1`,
         platform_id
         ) %>% 
  separate(sample_id, sep = ", ", into = c("subject_id", "delete")) %>% 
  select(-delete) %>% 
    mutate(timepoint = if_else(timepoint == "N/A", "0", timepoint),
         timepoint = (as.numeric(timepoint)/24) %>% round(x = ., digits = 1),
         subject_id = str_remove(subject_id, "Subject "),
         geo = "GSE36809",
         organism = "Human",
         treatment = if_else(subject_id != "Control", "Trauma", "Control")) %>% 
  filter(!description %in% c("Please notice that this sample with low RNA quality.", 
                            "Sample from patients with incomplete time points.")) %>% 
  mutate(
    
    # Binned timepoints
    timepoints_new = case_when(
      timepoint < 1            ~ "Early_Hours",
      timepoint >= 1 & timepoint < 2  ~ "Day_1",
      timepoint >= 2 & timepoint < 5  ~ "Day_3",
      timepoint >= 5 & timepoint < 10 ~ "Day_7",
      timepoint >= 10 & timepoint < 18 ~ "Day_14",
      timepoint >= 18 & timepoint < 25 ~ "Day_21",
      timepoint >= 25          ~ "Day_28",
      TRUE                         ~ "Other"
    ),
    
    #Explicit bins
    timepoints_bin = case_when(
      timepoint < 1            ~ "<Day_1",
      timepoint >= 1 & timepoint < 2  ~ "Day_1_>=1 to <2",
      timepoint >= 2 & timepoint < 5  ~ "Day_3_>=2 to <5",
      timepoint >= 5 & timepoint < 10 ~ "Day_7_>=5 to <10",
      timepoint >= 10 & timepoint < 18 ~ "Day_14_>=10 to <18",
      timepoint >= 18 & timepoint < 25 ~ "Day_21_>=18 to <25",
      timepoint >= 25          ~ "Day_28_>25",
      TRUE                         ~ "Other"
    ),
    
    timepoints_new = factor(timepoints_new, levels = c("Early_Hours", "Day_1", "Day_3", "Day_7", "Day_14", "Day_21", "Day_28"))
  )



GSE_metadata_annotated %>% 
  group_by(subject_id)%>%
  arrange(subject_id, timepoint) %>%
  View()

GSE_metadata_annotated %>% 
  filter(subject_id != "Control") %>% 
  group_by(subject_id)%>%
  summarise(n_timepoints = n()) %>% 
  arrange(subject_id, n_timepoints) %>% 
  filter(n_timepoints > 1) # -10 participants


GSE_metadata_annotated %>% 
  group_by(timepoints_new, treatment)%>%
  summarise(n_sample = n()) %>% 
  arrange(timepoints_new) %>% 
# Create ggplot object: maps data to aesthetic (x = expression value)
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = timepoints_new,
      size = n_sample,
      y = treatment,
      color = treatment) +
# Add scatter plot points: each point represents a sample in PCA/MDS space
  geom_point()

GSE_metadata_annotated_filtered = GSE_metadata_annotated %>% 
  filter(timepoints_new %in% c("Early_Hours", "Day_1", "Day_3", "Day_7"))


#Save metadata
write_csv(GSE_metadata_annotated_filtered, file = here("tables", paste0(filename, "_metadata.csv")))

#Get counts matrix ------
GSE_exprs <- eset %>% exprs()

#Save as RDS
GSE_exprs %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  select(GSE_metadata_annotated_filtered$geo_sample) %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", paste0(filename, "_exprs.rds")))

```

```{r eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, cache = TRUE}
#Download datasets
filename = "trauma_burn_mouse"
GSE_matrix <- getGEO(filename = here("tables", "GSE7404_series_matrix.txt.gz"), 
                     GSEMatrix = T)

#Get Expression Set
eset <- GSE_matrix

#Get metadata -------

#Select, clean, and standardize attributes
GSE_metadata_annotated = GSE_metadata %>% 
  select(geo_sample = "geo_accession",
         sample_id = "source_name_ch1",
         participant_description = title,
         characteristics = characteristics_ch1,
         timepoint = `time:ch1`,
         genetic = `genetic background:ch1`,
         tissue = `source_name_ch1`,
         organism = organism_ch1,
         description = description,
         # sex = `Sex:ch1`,
         platform_id
         ) %>% 
# Filter to PBMC samples only: restricts analysis to peripheral blood mononuclear cells
  filter(tissue == "mouse leukocytes") %>% 
  fill(genetic, .direction = "up") %>% 
  mutate(treatment = case_when(str_detect(description, "burn") ~ "Burn", 
                               str_detect(description, "trauma") ~ "Trauma", 
                               str_detect(description, "LPS") ~ "LPS",
                               T~description),
         treatment = if_else(str_detect(participant_description, "Sham"), paste0(treatment, "_", "Control"), treatment),
         tissue = str_remove(tissue, "mouse "), 
         sex = "male",
         geo = "GSE7404") %>% 
  extract(
    col = participant_description, 
    into = c("timepoint", "participant_id"), 
    regex = "(\\d+\\s?(?:day|Day|hr))\\s+(rep\\s?\\d+)", 
    remove = T 
  ) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint = str_replace(timepoint, "hr", "Hour") %>% str_replace("day", "Day"),
         timepoint = fct_reorder(timepoint, parse_number(timepoint))) %>% 
  select(geo_sample, participant_id, timepoint, sex, 
         strain = genetic, tissue, organism, treatment, platform_id)
```
