##Annotate genes

#### Mouse datasets

##### Trauma and Burn

Import previously saved analysis results for combined processing.

```{r}
#Import datasets
mouse_exprs = readRDS(here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_exprs.rds")) %>% 
  as.matrix() %>%
  { log2(. + 1) } %>% 
  as.data.frame()
mouse_metadata = read_csv(file = here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_metadata.csv")) %>% 
  mutate(status = if_else(str_detect(treatment, "_Control"), "Control", "Treated"),
         treatment = str_remove(treatment, "_Control"))

#Inputs
filename = "trauma_burn_mouse"

#Annotate genes ------
#Mouse -----
#Annotate data and calculate log2fc
mouse_exprs_metadata  = mouse_exprs %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe_id") %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = 2:145,
               names_to = "geo_sample",
               values_to = "value_raw") %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(mouse_metadata, 
             by = "geo_sample") 

#Get value from day 0 and calculate Log2FC (non-paired)
mouse_exprs_log2fc_sample = mouse_exprs_metadata %>% 
  filter(status == "Control") %>% 
  select(probe_id, treatment, timepoint, subject_num = participant_id, value_raw_ref = value_raw) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
# Group by probe ID to collapse multiple probe-to-gene mappings later
  group_by(timepoint, treatment, probe_id) %>% 
  summarise(value_raw_ref = mean(value_raw_ref)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
# Attach sample metadata (participant ID, timepoint, condition) to expression values by GEO sample ID
  inner_join(mouse_exprs_metadata %>% 
               filter(status != "Control"),
             by = join_by("probe_id", "treatment", "timepoint")) %>% 
  # Compute log2 fold-change relative to baseline
mutate(log2fc = value_raw - value_raw_ref) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() 

#Check duplicates
mouse_exprs_log2fc_sample %>% 
  filter(participant_id == "rep 1",
         treatment == "Burn",
         probe_id == "1415670_at")
```


Annotate probes with gene symbols by querying the Ensembl BioMart database.

```{r}
########### Filter and annotate probes -----
# Configure Ensembl BioMart
ensembl_mart <- useMart("ensembl")
# Select the mouse genome (mmusculus_gene_ensembl) as the annotation dataset in BioMart
ensembl_mart <- useDataset("mmusculus_gene_ensembl", mart = ensembl_mart)

# Get probe IDs from expression matrix
gene_id <- rownames(mouse_exprs) %>% unique()

# listAttributes(ensembl_mart) %>% View()
# Annotate data
annot <- getBM(
  attributes = c("affy_mouse430_2",
                 "ensembl_gene_id",
                 "entrezgene_id",
                 "mgi_symbol",
                 "description"),
  filters = "affy_mouse430_2", #Probes
  values = gene_id,
  mart = ensembl_mart)

# Load mouse-to-human orthology lookup
# (Install orthology package if needed)
# library(devtools)
# devtools::install_github('shenorrLabTRDF/FIT.mouse2man')
library(FIT.mouse2man)
HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez = FIT.mouse2man::HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(mouse_entrez = mouse_ortholog)

#Get annotations for each probe 
### Filter probes with highest median expression
mouse_log2summary = mouse_exprs %>% #20,845 probes
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe_id") %>% 
  rename(probe = probe_id) %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -probe,
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "expression") %>% 
# Group by probe ID to collapse multiple probe-to-gene mappings later
  group_by(probe) %>% 
  summarise(median = median(expression, na.rm = T)) %>%  
# Join BioMart gene annotation to expression data by probe ID: adds gene symbol, Entrez ID, and description
  inner_join(annot %>% 
              rename(probe = affy_mouse430_2), 
            by = "probe") %>%  #24.009 rows
  # Collapse to one row per Ensembl ID
  group_by(ensembl_gene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-ensembl_gene_id) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  
  # Collapse to one row per Entrez ID
  group_by(entrezgene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%  #21.863 probes/entrez_ids
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(mouse_entrez = entrezgene_id) %>% 
  
  # Join human orthologs, collapse to one row per HGNC symbol
  inner_join(HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez, by = c("mouse_entrez", "mgi_symbol")) %>% 
# Group by human gene symbol: after orthology mapping, collapse mouse genes that map to the same human gene
  group_by(hgnc_symbol) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1)  %>% #14.396
  ungroup()

# Remove HGNC symbols with multiple MGI mappings
hgnc_symbol_dupes = mouse_log2summary %>% 
  #filter out ensembl id with multiple mgi_symbols
  get_dupes(hgnc_symbol)

mouse_log2summary = mouse_log2summary %>% 
  select(probe, hgnc_symbol) %>% 
# Remove genes with ambiguous human symbol mappings: retains only one-to-one mouse-to-human orthologs
  filter(!hgnc_symbol %in% c(hgnc_symbol_dupes$hgnc_symbol %>% unique())) 

# Build filtered expression matrix with human symbols

# Join expression with annotation, keep only mapped probes
mouse_log2_filtered_probes = mouse_exprs %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe_id") %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rename(probe = probe_id) %>% 
# Join expression data with annotation by probe ID: adds gene symbols to raw probe-level measurements
  inner_join(mouse_log2summary, by = "probe") %>%   #214,396
  select(human_symbol = hgnc_symbol,
         probe,
         c(mouse_metadata %>% 
             pull(geo_sample)))
#Check
mouse_log2_filtered_probes %>% dim()
mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol = mouse_log2_filtered_probes 
# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% get_dupes(human_symbol)

#Save
mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", paste0(filename, "_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds")))
```

```{r}
  attributes = c("affy_hg_u133_plus_2",
                 "ensembl_gene_id",
                 "entrezgene_id",
                 "hgnc_symbol",
                 "description"),
  filters = "affy_hg_u133_plus_2", #Probes
  values = gene_id,
  mart = ensembl_mart) %>% #Standardize

  rownames_to_column("probe") %>%

# Group by probe ID to collapse multiple probe-to-gene mappings later
  group_by(probe) %>% 
  summarise(median = median(expression, na.rm = T)) %>%

  inner_join(annot,

  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%

# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>%

  group_by(entrezgene_id) %>%

  ungroup()
```

## Differential expression

### Mouse
#### Burn
##### Limma


Calculate array weights and fit a Limma model with SVA-adjusted design matrix.

```{r}
# Load data
mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
mouse_metadata = read_csv(file = here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_metadata.csv")) %>% 
  filter(str_detect(treatment, "Burn"))

#Create Expression Set
eset_mouse <- ExpressionSet(
  assayData = mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
    column_to_rownames("human_symbol") %>% 
    select(all_of(mouse_metadata$geo_sample)) %>%
    as.matrix(),
# Convert metadata to AnnotatedDataFrame: formal phenotype data structure required by ExpressionSet
  phenoData = AnnotatedDataFrame(mouse_metadata %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
                                   column_to_rownames("geo_sample") %>% 
                                   mutate(condition = paste0(treatment, "_", timepoint))))

# Filter low-expressed genes (log2 > 6 in >= 5 samples)
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_mouse) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>% 
  rowSums() %>% 
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_mouse[genes_to_keep, ]

design <- model.matrix(~ condition + 0, # 0 defines the way we compare the samples
                       eset_filtered) 


# --- 2. Sample Weighting Diagnostic ---
aw <- arrayWeights(eset_filtered, design)

# Barplot of array weights: visual diagnostic to identify low-quality arrays (bars near zero indicate problematic samples)
barplot(aw, 
        names.arg = eset_filtered$condition, 
        main = "Sample Weights Diagnostic (with SVA)", 
        ylab = "Weight", 
        las = 2, 
        cex.names = 0.7, 
        col = "skyblue")

# --- 3. Linear Modeling (Limma) ---
fit <- lmFit(eset_filtered, design, weights = aw)

# --- 4. Contrast Matrix & Empirical Bayes ---
# We compare Burn vs Control at each specific timepoint
cont_matrix <- makeContrasts(
  Burn_2h = conditionBurn_2.Hour - conditionBurn_Control_2.Hour,
  Burn_D1 = conditionBurn_1.Day  - conditionBurn_Control_1.Day,
  Burn_D3 = conditionBurn_3.Day  - conditionBurn_Control_3.Day,
  Burn_D7 = conditionBurn_7.Day  - conditionBurn_Control_7.Day,
  levels = design
)

# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont_matrix)

# Using trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE to handle mean-variance trends and outliers
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2, trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE)

# Diagnostic: Check the residual variance trend
plotSA(fit2, main = "Sigma vs Abundance (SVA + Weights Applied)")

# --- 5. DEG Extraction & Result Formatting ---
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2), function(i) {
# Extract differentially expressed genes using the treat method (tests whether log2FC exceeds a minimum threshold, not just non-zero)
  topTreat(fit2, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(comparison = colnames(fit2)[i]) %>% 
    rownames_to_column("symbol")
})

# Combine all results into a clean, tidy dataframe
all_degs_mouse_burn <- bind_rows(results_list) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>%
  rename(human_symbol = symbol,
         mean_l2fc = log_fc,
         ci_upper = ci_r,
         ci_lower = ci_l,
         condition = comparison) %>%
# Tag rows as Mouse: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Mouse")

# Summary of Significant DEGs (Adj P-Value <= 0.05)
all_degs_mouse_burn %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
# Count the number of differentially expressed genes (adj.p ≤ 0.05) per comparison
  summarise(n_degs = n())
	
#Save
# all_degs_mouse_burn %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "burn_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

```

Perform PCA on the filtered expression data to assess variance structure.
```{r}
# 1. Compute PCA on transposed expression matrix
# Note: t() transposes so samples are in rows
# Transpose expression matrix (samples in rows, genes in columns) for PCA
pca_matrix <- t(exprs(eset_filtered))
pca_res <- prcomp(pca_matrix, scale. = TRUE)

# 2. Calculate variance explained for each axis
vars <- round(100 * pca_res$sdev^2 / sum(pca_res$sdev^2), 1)

# 3. Build data.frame following MDS logic
df_pca <- data.frame(
  Sample    = colnames(eset_filtered),
  PC1       = pca_res$x[,1],
  PC2       = pca_res$x[,2],
  Condition = eset_filtered$condition,
  timepoint = eset_filtered$timepoint
) %>% 
  mutate(group = if_else(str_detect(Condition, "Control"), "Control", "Burn"))

# 4. Plotar com ggplot2
ggplot(df_pca, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = group, shape = timepoint)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.8) +
  # Add ellipses around main groups (Burn vs Control)
  stat_ellipse(aes(group = group), linetype = 2, size = 0.5) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "PCA Plot - Mouse Burn Study",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", vars[1], "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", vars[2], "%)"),
    color = "Treatment Group",
    shape = "Timepoint/Condition"
  ) +
  # Opcional: Melhora a diferenciação visual se houver muitos shapes
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(15, 16, 17, 18, 7, 8, 9, 10))
```

##### T test
Load the Burn mouse dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r}
# Load data
mouse_exprs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
mouse_metadata = read_csv(file = here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_metadata.csv"))
log2fc_sample = readRDS(here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))

log2fc_sample_symbol = log2fc_sample %>% 
  inner_join(mouse_exprs %>% 
               select(human_symbol, probe_id = probe),
             by = "probe_id") %>% 
  select(-probe_id) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
# Filter to the treatment of interest: removes control/saline samples from this branch
  filter(treatment == "Burn")

log2fc_unpaired_ttest = log2fc_sample_symbol %>%
  group_by(human_symbol, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(
    res = list(t.test(value_raw, value_raw_ref, paired = F, alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = F)),
    pval = res[[1]]$p.value,
    diff = res[[1]]$estimate[1] - res[[1]]$estimate[2],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
# Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) correction to raw p-values: controls the expected proportion of false discoveries among rejected hypotheses
  mutate(padj = p.adjust(pval, method = "BH"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Unpaired"
         )

log2fc_unpaired_ttest %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "burn_mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds"))

```

##### Limma
Run Limma differential expression analysis on the trauma mouse dataset with unpaired samples.
```{r}
# Load data
mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
mouse_metadata = read_csv(file = here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_metadata.csv")) %>% 
  filter(str_detect(treatment, "Trauma"))

#Create Expression Set
eset_mouse <- ExpressionSet(
  assayData = mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
    column_to_rownames("human_symbol") %>% 
    select(all_of(mouse_metadata$geo_sample)) %>%
    #Check if expression is log2 transformed
    as.matrix(),
# Convert metadata to AnnotatedDataFrame: formal phenotype data structure required by ExpressionSet
  phenoData = AnnotatedDataFrame(mouse_metadata %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
                                   column_to_rownames("geo_sample") %>% 
                                   mutate(condition = paste0(treatment, "_", timepoint))))

#Check if expression is log2 transformed
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
exprs(eset_mouse) #values must be in the 0-16 range typically

# Filter low-expressed genes (log2 > 6 in >= 5 samples)
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_mouse) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>% 
  rowSums() %>% 
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_mouse[genes_to_keep, ]

# Build design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ condition + 0, # 0 defines the way we compare the samples
                       eset_filtered) 

# Ensure syntactically valid column names: replaces spaces/special characters with dots for model.matrix compatibility
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))  # Avoids blank spaces

# Estimate sample-specific quality weights using arrayWeights: down-weights arrays with excessive noise to improve statistical power
aw <- arrayWeights(eset_filtered, design)
# Barplot of array weights: visual diagnostic to identify low-quality arrays (bars near zero indicate problematic samples)
barplot(aw, 
        names.arg = eset_filtered$condition, # Label x-axis with condition names
        main = "Sample Weights Diagnostic", 
        ylab = "Weight", 
        las = 2,           # Rotate x-axis labels 90 degrees
        cex.names = 0.7,   # Reduce font size when many labels
        col = "skyblue")

# Fit linear model
fit <- lmFit(eset_filtered, 
             design, weights = aw) 

# List available conditions
colnames(design) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  arrange(.)

# Define contrasts
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))

# Define contrasts of interest: specify which group means to subtract (e.g. Treatment − Control) to test specific hypotheses
cont_matrix <- makeContrasts(
  # --- Trauma Comparisons ---
  Trauma_2h = conditionTrauma_2.Hour - conditionTrauma_Control_2.Hour,
  Trauma_D1 = conditionTrauma_1.Day  - conditionTrauma_Control_1.Day,
  Trauma_D3 = conditionTrauma_3.Day  - conditionTrauma_Control_3.Day,
  Trauma_D7 = conditionTrauma_7.Day  - conditionTrauma_Control_7.Day,
  levels = design
)

# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont_matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink gene-wise variances toward a common value: improves stability for low-variance genes
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2, trend = T, robust = T)

# Check whether high-weight genes distort the fit
plotSA(fit2, main = "Sigma vs Abundance (Weights Applied)")

# Extract DEGs for every contrast

## For every contrast
# Iterate over each contrast column: extract DEGs from every comparison in one pass
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2), function(i) {
# Extract differentially expressed genes using the treat method (tests whether log2FC exceeds a minimum threshold, not just non-zero)
  topTreat(fit2, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(comparison = colnames(fit2)[i]) %>% 
    rownames_to_column("symbol")
  })

# Combine all results
all_contrasts_degs <- bind_rows(results_list)

# Get all DEGs and clean dataset
all_degs_mouse = all_contrasts_degs %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  select(comparison, everything()) %>% 
# Tag rows as Mouse: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Mouse") %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(condition = comparison, everything()) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(human_symbol = symbol,
         mean_l2fc = log_fc,
         ci_upper = ci_r,
         ci_lower = ci_l)

all_degs_mouse$condition %>% unique()
	
# #Save
all_degs_mouse %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

all_degs_mouse %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
# Count the number of differentially expressed genes (adj.p ≤ 0.05) per comparison
  summarise(n_degs = n())

```



##### T test
Load the Burn mouse dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r}
# Load data
mouse_exprs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
mouse_metadata = read_csv(file = here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_metadata.csv"))
log2fc_sample = readRDS(here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))

log2fc_sample_symbol = log2fc_sample %>% 
  inner_join(mouse_exprs %>% 
               select(human_symbol, probe_id = probe),
             by = "probe_id") %>% 
  select(-probe_id) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
# Filter to the treatment of interest: removes control/saline samples from this branch
  filter(treatment == "Trauma")

log2fc_unpaired_ttest = log2fc_sample_symbol %>%
  group_by(human_symbol, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(
    # row_ttests is fast within small groups or on matrices
    res = list(t.test(value_raw, value_raw_ref, paired = F, alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = F)),
    pval = res[[1]]$p.value,
    diff = res[[1]]$estimate[1] - res[[1]]$estimate[2],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
# Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) correction to raw p-values: controls the expected proportion of false discoveries among rejected hypotheses
  mutate(padj = p.adjust(pval, method = "BH"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Unpaired"
         )

log2fc_unpaired_ttest %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_mouse_log2fc_paired_unpaired_ttest.rds"))
```

##### Subsampling 

Run the subsampling loop to assess the impact of cohort composition on differential expression results.

```{r Subsampling loop}
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(tidyverse)
library(limma)
library(here)
library(janitor)

## 1. Load Data & Prepare ExpressionSet
human_log2_hgnc_symbol <- readRDS(file = here("tables", "burn_human_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
human_metadata <- read_csv(file = here("tables", "burn_human_metadata.csv")) %>%  
  mutate(
    condition = paste0(treatment, "_", timepoints_new),
    condition = fct_relevel(condition, "Control_Early_Hours")
  )

# Build an ExpressionSet container: assayData = expression matrix, phenoData = sample-level covariates for Limma
eset_human <- ExpressionSet(
  assayData = human_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
    column_to_rownames("human_symbol") %>% 
    select(all_of(human_metadata$geo_sample)) %>%
    as.matrix(),
# Convert metadata to AnnotatedDataFrame: formal phenotype data structure required by ExpressionSet
  phenoData = AnnotatedDataFrame(human_metadata %>% column_to_rownames("geo_sample"))
)

# Filtering genes with intensity > 6 (log2) in at least 5 samples
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_human) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>%
  rowSums() %>%
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_human[genes_to_keep, ]
meta_df <- as_tibble(pData(eset_filtered), rownames = "sample_id")
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
expr_matrix <- exprs(eset_filtered)
unique_participants <- meta_df$sample_id %>% unique()

# Slices exactly n_per_condition arrays per distinct biological state grouping
draw_stratified_samples <- function(metadata, n_per_condition = 5) {
  valid_draw <- FALSE
  attempts <- 0
  
  while(!valid_draw) {
    attempts <- attempts + 1
    if(attempts > 2000) stop("Could not find a mathematically stable stratified sample subset.")
    
    # Draw exactly n_per_condition independent samples (sample_id) from EACH group
    sub_meta <- metadata %>%
      group_by(condition) %>%
      slice_sample(n = n_per_condition, replace = FALSE) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      mutate(
        condition = as.factor(condition),
        sex = as.factor(sex)
      )
    
    # Check 1: Verify all 5 categorical clinical groups are captured in the slice
    has_all_conditions <- (length(unique(sub_meta$condition)) == 5)
    
    # Check 2: Verify both Sexes are captured to avoid model matrix collinearity
    has_sex_diversity   <- (length(unique(sub_meta$sex)) > 1)
    
    if(has_all_conditions && has_sex_diversity) {
      # Aligned precisely with the original design: condition + age + sex + 0
      test_design <- model.matrix(~ condition + age + sex + 0, data = sub_meta)
      colnames(test_design) <- make.names(colnames(test_design))
      
      # Confirm the subset design matrix is full rank (invertible)
      bad_coefs <- limma::nonEstimable(test_design)
      if(is.null(bad_coefs)) {
        valid_draw <- TRUE
      }
    }
  }
  return(sub_meta)
}

# ==============================================================================
# 3. RUN MULTI-ITERATION SIMULATION LOOP (DIRECT SAMPLE ESTIMATION)
# ==============================================================================
n_iterations <- 200 
samples_per_group <- 5  # 5 control + (5 samples * 4 timepoints) = 25 total samples per iteration

# Set random seed for reproducibility: ensures that subsampling draws the same iterations across runs
set.seed(123) 

df_global_runs <- tibble(iteration = 1:n_iterations) %>%
  mutate(
    # Draw sample configurations via the corrected stratified logic
    sampled_metadata = map(iteration, ~ draw_stratified_samples(meta_df, n_per_condition = samples_per_group)),
    
# Apply Limma to each subsample: fits a linear model per iteration to assess DEG stability
    limma_results = map(sampled_metadata, ~ {
      sub_meta <- .x
      sub_expr <- expr_matrix[, sub_meta$sample_id]
      
      # Build the multivariable model matrix identical to your original code
      design_sub <- model.matrix(~ condition + age + sex + 0, data = sub_meta)
      colnames(design_sub) <- make.names(colnames(design_sub))
      
      # Compute localized array weights natively at the sample level
      aw_sub <- arrayWeights(sub_expr, design_sub)
      
      # Fit linear model directly without block correlation factors
      fit_sub <- lmFit(sub_expr, design = design_sub, weights = aw_sub)
      
      # Define directional mathematical contrasts matching column identities
      cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(
        Burn_Early = conditionBurn_Early_Hours - conditionControl_Early_Hours,
        Burn_D1    = conditionBurn_Day_1  - conditionControl_Early_Hours,
        Burn_D3    = conditionBurn_Day_3  - conditionControl_Early_Hours,
        Burn_D7    = conditionBurn_Day_7  - conditionControl_Early_Hours,
        levels = design_sub
      )
      
      # Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2_sub <- contrasts.fit(fit_sub, cont.matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink gene-wise variances toward a common value: improves stability for low-variance genes
      fit2_sub <- eBayes(fit2_sub, robust = TRUE, trend = TRUE)
      
      res_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2_sub), function(i) {
        # Extract DEGs for this contrast using topTreat
        df_res <- topTreat(fit2_sub, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE)
        df_res$symbol <- rownames(df_res)
        df_res$comparison <- colnames(fit2_sub)[i]
        rownames(df_res) <- NULL
        return(df_res)
      })
      
# Row-bind all contrast results into a single data frame: combines list of per-contrast results into a tidy DEG table
      do.call(rbind, res_list)
    })
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 4. POST-SIMULATION COMPILATION & SIGNIFICANCE SUMMARIES
# ==============================================================================
burn_human_subsampled_degs <- df_global_runs %>%
  select(iteration, limma_results) %>%
# Unnest the list-column of Limma results into a flat data frame: one row per gene × comparison × iteration
  unnest(limma_results) %>%
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
    clean_names() %>%
    #Calculate errors by iteration
  mutate(
    se_iteration = abs(log_fc / t),
    sd_iteration = se_iteration / sqrt(0.4) # N = 5
  ) %>% 
  group_by(comparison, symbol) %>%
  summarise(
    p_value = median(p_value),
    adj_p_val = median(adj_p_val),
    mean_l2fc = median(log_fc),
    sd_sampling_stability = sd(log_fc),
    se = median(se_iteration),
    sd = median(sd_iteration),
    ci_lower = median(ci_l),
    ci_upper = median(ci_r),
    t = median(t),
    b = median(b),
    ave_expr = median(ave_expr),
    pct_iterations_significant = mean(adj_p_val <= 0.05) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rename(human_symbol = symbol, condition = comparison) %>%
# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human") 

# Save Downsampled DEGs Output Object
burn_human_subsampled_degs %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "burn_human_dge_subsampled_degs.rds"))

# Print Robust Differential Expression Signatures Summary
burn_human_subsampled_degs %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
  summarise(n_robust_degs = n()) %>%
  print()
```


Demographics
Visualise the demographic composition (age, sex, race) across subsampling iterations to confirm balance.
Visualise demographic composition across subsampling iterations.
```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=8}
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(tidyverse)
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(patchwork)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. PROCESS SIMULATION ITERATIONS DATA (RAW METRICS)
# ==============================================================================
demographics_summary <- df_global_runs %>%
  select(iteration, sampled_metadata) %>%
  unnest(sampled_metadata) %>%
# Extract demographic columns (age, sex, race) per iteration for visualisation
  select(iteration, sample_id, age, sex) %>%
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>%
  group_by(iteration) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_age   = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE), 
    prop_male  = mean(sex == "male", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(iteration = factor(iteration, levels = 1:max(iteration)))

# ==============================================================================
# 2. BUILD TOP PANEL: SUBSAMPLING RUNS (n=5 PER ITERATION)
# ==============================================================================

# Initialise ggplot with aesthetic mappings: defines variables for x-axis, y-axis, colour, and fill
plot_age <- ggplot(demographics_summary, aes(x = "Mean Age", y = iteration)) +
# Add tile layer: creates a heatmap-like grid where colour encodes numeric values (e.g. mean age per iteration)
  geom_tile(aes(fill = mean_age), color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
# Add text annotation to tiles: displays the numeric mean age value inside each tile
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", mean_age)), 
            color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
# Apply viridis continuous colour scale: perceptually uniform colour mapping for numeric fill values
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", name = "Mean Age\n(Years)", direction = -1) +
# Configure x-axis: set position, expansion, breaks, and labels
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top", expand = c(0.01, 0.01)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0.01, 0.01)) +
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo() +
# Customise theme elements: remove/minimise gridlines, adjust axis text, and fine-tune legend placement
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid   = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "left"
  ) +
# Set informative axis labels, legend titles, and overall plot title
  labs(y = "Subsampling Iterations (n=5)")

plot_sex <- demographics_summary %>%
  select(iteration, Male = prop_male) %>%
  mutate(Female = 1 - Male) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Male, Female), names_to = "Sex", values_to = "Proportion") %>%
# Initialise ggplot with aesthetic mappings: defines variables for x-axis, y-axis, colour, and fill
  ggplot(aes(x = Proportion, y = iteration, fill = Sex)) +
# Add stacked bar chart: shows proportional distribution of categories (sex or race) per iteration
  geom_col(width = 0.75, position = "stack") +
# Apply manual colour scale: uses predefined colour palette (typically from project's colour scheme)
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Male" = "#3182bd", "Female" = "#fa9fb5")) +
# Configure x-axis: set position, expansion, breaks, and labels
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top", expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0.01, 0.01)) +
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo() +
# Customise theme elements: remove/minimise gridlines, adjust axis text, and fine-tune legend placement
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  ) +
# Set informative axis labels, legend titles, and overall plot title
  labs(x = "Sex Distribution")


# Configure patchwork layout: assign relative widths to sub-plots for balanced display
top_panel <- plot_age + plot_sex + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1))

# ==============================================================================
# 3. BUILD BOTTOM PANEL: ORIGINAL TOTAL COHORT BASELINE (N=100)
# ==============================================================================
original_demographics <- human_metadata %>%
  mutate(age = str_remove(age, "y") %>% as.numeric(),
         sex = case_when(sex == "F" ~ "Female",
                         sex == "M" ~ "Male",
                         T~sex)) %>% 
  select(geo_sample, age, sex) %>%
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct()

# Initialise ggplot with aesthetic mappings: defines variables for x-axis, y-axis, colour, and fill
base_age <- ggplot(original_demographics, aes(x = age)) +
# Add density plot: smooth distribution of age values for the full cohort baseline
  geom_density(fill = "#3182bd", alpha = 0.4, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
# Add vertical dashed line at the cohort mean age: reference for comparing subsample distributions
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(original_demographics$age, na.rm = TRUE), 
             color = "black", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
# Create faceted plot: split data into sub-panels by condition or organism for side-by-side comparison
  facet_wrap(~"Age") +
# Configure x-axis: set position, expansion, breaks, and labels
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo() +
# Customise theme elements: remove/minimise gridlines, adjust axis text, and fine-tune legend placement
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9)
  ) +
# Set informative axis labels, legend titles, and overall plot title
  labs(x = "Age (Years)", y = "Density")

base_sex <- original_demographics %>%
  dplyr::count(sex) %>%
# Convert counts to proportions: facilitates stacked bar charts of demographic distributions
  mutate(Proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
# Initialise ggplot with aesthetic mappings: defines variables for x-axis, y-axis, colour, and fill
  ggplot(aes(x = Proportion, y = "Original\nCohort", fill = sex)) +
# Create faceted plot: split data into sub-panels by condition or organism for side-by-side comparison
  facet_wrap(~"Original\nCohort") +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = "stack", show.legend = FALSE) +
# Apply manual colour scale: uses predefined colour palette (typically from project's colour scheme)
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Male" = "#3182bd", "Female" = "#fa9fb5")) +
# Configure x-axis: set position, expansion, breaks, and labels
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo() +
# Customise theme elements: remove/minimise gridlines, adjust axis text, and fine-tune legend placement
  theme(
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )

# Configure patchwork layout: assign relative widths to sub-plots for balanced display
bottom_panel <- base_age + base_sex + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1))

# ==============================================================================
# 4. STITCH COMPLETE GRAPHICAL CANVAS
# ==============================================================================
final_canvas <- top_panel / bottom_panel + 
  plot_layout(heights = c(4, 1), guides = "collect") +
# Add overall title to the combined figure using patchwork
  plot_annotation(title = "Burn Injury, Human Cohort Validation")

print(final_canvas)
```

##### T test
Load the Burn human dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r}
# Load data
human_exprs = readRDS(file = here("tables", "burn_human_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
human_metadata = read_csv(file = here("tables", "burn_human_metadata.csv"))
burn_human_log2fc_sample = readRDS(here("tables", "burn_human_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))

log2fc_sample_symbol = burn_human_log2fc_sample %>% 
  inner_join(human_exprs %>% 
               select(human_symbol, probe_id = probe),
             by = "probe_id") %>% 
  select(-probe_id) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() 

log2fc_unpaired_ttest = log2fc_sample_symbol %>%
  group_by(human_symbol, timepoints_new) %>%
  summarise(
    res = list(t.test(value_raw, value_raw_ref, paired = F, alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = F)),
    pval = res[[1]]$p.value,
    diff = res[[1]]$estimate[1] -  res[[1]]$estimate[2],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
# Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) correction to raw p-values: controls the expected proportion of false discoveries among rejected hypotheses
  mutate(padj = p.adjust(pval, method = "BH"),
         test = "t-Test",
         paired = "Unpaired"
         )

log2fc_unpaired_ttest %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "burn_human_log2fc_unpaired_ttest.rds"))
```

##### Limma
Run unpaired statistical tests comparing each timepoint to baseline.

```{r}
# Load data
human_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_human_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
outliers = readRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_human_metadata_outliers.rds"))

human_metadata = read_csv(file = here("tables", "trauma_human_metadata.csv")) %>% 
  mutate(
        condition = paste0(treatment, "_", timepoints_new),
        condition = fct_relevel(condition, "Control_Early_Hours"),
        sex = fct_relevel(sex, "F"),
        age = scale(age)
      ) %>% 
  filter(!subject_id %in% c(outliers))

#Create Expression Set
eset_human <- ExpressionSet(
  assayData = human_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
    select(-probe) %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
    column_to_rownames("human_symbol") %>% 
    select(all_of(human_metadata$geo_sample)) %>%
    #Check if expression is log2 transformed
    as.matrix(),
# Convert metadata to AnnotatedDataFrame: formal phenotype data structure required by ExpressionSet
  phenoData = AnnotatedDataFrame(human_metadata %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
                                   column_to_rownames("geo_sample")))

#Check if expression is log2 transformed
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
exprs(eset_human) #values must be in the 0-16 range typically

# Filter low-expressed genes (log2 > 6 in >= 5 samples)
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_human) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>% 
  rowSums() %>% 
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_human[genes_to_keep, ]

# Build design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ condition + age + sex + 0,
                       eset_filtered) 

# Ensure syntactically valid column names: replaces spaces/special characters with dots for model.matrix compatibility
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))  # Avoids blank spaces

# aw <- arrayWeights(eset_filtered, design)
# 
# barplot(aw, 
#         names.arg = eset_filtered$condition, 
#         main = "Sample Weights Diagnostic", 
#         ylab = "Weight", 
#         las = 2,           
#         cex.names = 0.7,  
#         col = "skyblue")

# Fit linear model
fit <- lmFit(eset_filtered, 
             design, 
             # weights = aw
             ) 

# List available conditions
colnames(design) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  arrange(.)

# Define contrasts
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))

# Define contrasts of interest: specify which group means to subtract (e.g. Treatment − Control) to test specific hypotheses
cont_matrix <- makeContrasts(
  # --- Trauma Comparisons ---
  Trauma_Early = conditionTrauma_Early_Hours - conditionControl_Early_Hours,
  Trauma_D1 = conditionTrauma_Day_1  - conditionControl_Early_Hours,
  Trauma_D3 = conditionTrauma_Day_3  - conditionControl_Early_Hours,
  Trauma_D7 = conditionTrauma_Day_7  - conditionControl_Early_Hours,
  levels = design
)

# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont_matrix)
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink gene-wise variances toward a common value: improves stability for low-variance genes
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2, 
               # trend = T, #Does not need trend
               robust = T
               )

# Check whether high-weight genes distort the fit
plotSA(fit2, main = "Sigma vs Abundance (Weights Applied)")

# Extract DEGs for every contrast

## For every contrast
# Iterate over each contrast column: extract DEGs from every comparison in one pass
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2), function(i) {
# Extract differentially expressed genes using the treat method (tests whether log2FC exceeds a minimum threshold, not just non-zero)
  topTreat(fit2, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(comparison = colnames(fit2)[i]) %>% 
    rownames_to_column("symbol")
  })

# Combine all results
all_contrasts_degs <- bind_rows(results_list)

# Get all DEGs and clean dataset
all_degs_human = all_contrasts_degs %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  select(comparison, everything()) %>% 
# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human") %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(condition = comparison, everything()) %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(human_symbol = symbol,
         mean_l2fc = log_fc,
         ci_upper = ci_r,
         ci_lower = ci_l)

all_degs_human$condition %>% unique()
	
# #Save
all_degs_human %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_human_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

all_degs_human %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
# Count the number of differentially expressed genes (adj.p ≤ 0.05) per comparison
  summarise(n_degs = n())

```


###### Subsampling

Run the subsampling loop to assess the impact of cohort composition on differential expression results.

```{r Subsampling loop}
# Load required R package: makes its functions available in the current session
library(tidyverse)
library(limma)
library(here)
library(janitor)

## 1. Load Data, Filter Outliers, & Prepare ExpressionSet
human_log2_hgnc_symbol <- readRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_human_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
outliers <- readRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_human_metadata_outliers.rds"))

human_metadata <- read_csv(file = here("tables", "trauma_human_metadata.csv")) %>%  
  mutate(
    condition = paste0(treatment, "_", timepoints_new),
    condition = fct_relevel(condition, "Control_Early_Hours")
  ) %>% 
  filter(!subject_id %in% c(outliers))

# Build an ExpressionSet container: assayData = expression matrix, phenoData = sample-level covariates for Limma
eset_human <- ExpressionSet(
  assayData = human_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
    select(-probe) %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
    column_to_rownames("human_symbol") %>% 
    select(all_of(human_metadata$geo_sample)) %>%
    as.matrix(),
# Convert metadata to AnnotatedDataFrame: formal phenotype data structure required by ExpressionSet
  phenoData = AnnotatedDataFrame(human_metadata %>% column_to_rownames("geo_sample"))
)

# Filtering genes with intensity > 6 (log2) in at least 5 samples
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_human) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>%
  rowSums() %>%
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_human[genes_to_keep, ]

# Extract core matrix references for safe downsampling slices
meta_df <- honest_df <- as_tibble(pData(eset_filtered), rownames = "sample_id")
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
expr_matrix <- exprs(eset_filtered)

# Slices exactly n_per_condition independent samples (sample_id) from EACH group
draw_stratified_samples <- function(metadata, n_per_condition = 5) {
  valid_draw <- FALSE
  attempts <- 0
  
  while(!valid_draw) {
    attempts <- attempts + 1
    if(attempts > 2000) stop("Could not find a mathematically stable stratified sample subset.")
    
    # Draw exactly n_per_condition independent arrays per condition group
    sub_meta <- metadata %>%
      group_by(condition) %>%
      slice_sample(n = n_per_condition, replace = FALSE) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      mutate(
        condition = as.factor(condition),
        sex = as.factor(sex)
      )
    
    # Check 1: Verify all 5 categorical clinical groups are captured in the slice
    has_all_conditions <- (length(unique(sub_meta$condition)) == 5)
    
    # Check 2: Verify both Sexes are captured to avoid model matrix collinearity
    has_sex_diversity   <- (length(unique(sub_meta$sex)) > 1)
    
    if(has_all_conditions && has_sex_diversity) {
      # Aligned precisely with original design: condition + age + sex + 0
      test_design <- model.matrix(~ condition + age + sex + 0, data = sub_meta)
      colnames(test_design) <- make.names(colnames(test_design))
      
      bad_coefs <- limma::nonEstimable(test_design)
      if(is.null(bad_coefs)) {
        valid_draw <- TRUE
      }
    }
  }
  return(sub_meta)
}

# ==============================================================================
# 3. RUN MULTI-ITERATION SIMULATION LOOP (DIRECT SAMPLE ESTIMATION)
# ==============================================================================
n_iterations <- 200 
samples_per_group <- 5  # 5 control + (5 samples * 4 timepoints) = 25 total samples per iteration

# Set random seed for reproducibility: ensures that subsampling draws the same iterations across runs
set.seed(123) 

df_global_runs <- tibble(iteration = 1:n_iterations) %>%
  mutate(
# Apply the sampling function to each iteration: generates a list-column of sampled metadata sets
    sampled_metadata = map(iteration, ~ draw_stratified_samples(meta_df, n_per_condition = samples_per_group)),
    
# Apply Limma to each subsample: fits a linear model per iteration to assess DEG stability
    limma_results = map(sampled_metadata, ~ {
      sub_meta <- .x
      sub_expr <- expr_matrix[, sub_meta$sample_id]
      
# Build design matrix for linear modelling: encodes group membership and covariates (sex, age, race) for Limma
      design_sub <- model.matrix(~ condition + age + sex + 0, data = sub_meta)
      colnames(design_sub) <- make.names(colnames(design_sub))
      
      # Fit linear model directly without block correlation factors or array weights
      fit_sub <- lmFit(sub_expr, design = design_sub)
      
# Define contrasts of interest: specify which group means to subtract (e.g. Treatment − Control) to test specific hypotheses
      cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(
        Trauma_Early = conditionTrauma_Early_Hours - conditionControl_Early_Hours,
        Trauma_D1    = conditionTrauma_Day_1  - conditionControl_Early_Hours,
        Trauma_D3    = conditionTrauma_Day_3  - conditionControl_Early_Hours,
        Trauma_D7    = conditionTrauma_Day_7  - conditionControl_Early_Hours,
        levels = design_sub
      )
      
      # Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2_sub <- contrasts.fit(fit_sub, cont.matrix)
      # robust = TRUE as original setup, trend = FALSE since trend was deactivated
      fit2_sub <- eBayes(fit2_sub, robust = TRUE, trend = FALSE)
      
      res_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2_sub), function(i) {
        # Extract DEGs for this contrast using topTreat
        df_res <- topTreat(fit2_sub, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE)
        df_res$symbol <- rownames(df_res)
        df_res$comparison <- colnames(fit2_sub)[i]
        rownames(df_res) <- NULL
        return(df_res)
      })
      
# Row-bind all contrast results into a single data frame: combines list of per-contrast results into a tidy DEG table
      do.call(rbind, res_list)
    })
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 4. POST-SIMULATION COMPILATION & SIGNIFICANCE SUMMARIES
# ==============================================================================
trauma_human_subsampled_degs <- df_global_runs %>%
  select(iteration, limma_results) %>%
# Unnest the list-column of Limma results into a flat data frame: one row per gene × comparison × iteration
  unnest(limma_results) %>%
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
    clean_names() %>%
    #Calculate errors by iteration
  mutate(
    se_iteration = abs(log_fc / t),
    sd_iteration = se_iteration / sqrt(0.4) # N = 5
  ) %>% 
  group_by(comparison, symbol) %>%
  summarise(
    p_value = median(p_value),
    adj_p_val = median(adj_p_val),
    mean_l2fc = median(log_fc),
    sd_sampling_stability = sd(log_fc),
    se = median(se_iteration),
    sd = median(sd_iteration),
    ci_lower = median(ci_l),
    ci_upper = median(ci_r),
    t = median(t),
    b = median(b),
    ave_expr = median(ave_expr),
    pct_iterations_significant = mean(adj_p_val <= 0.05) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rename(human_symbol = symbol, condition = comparison) %>%
# Tag rows as Human: required for downstream faceting when combining Mouse and Human results
  mutate(organism = "Human")

# Save Downsampled DEGs Object
trauma_human_subsampled_degs %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_human_dge_subsampled_degs.rds"))

# Print Robust Differential Expression Summary Count
trauma_human_subsampled_degs %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
  summarise(n_robust_degs = n()) %>%
  print()

```

```{r}

###### DEGs

all_degs_human_burn = readRDS(here("tables", "burn_human_dge_subsampled_degs.rds")) %>%
```

## Mouse
### Download dataset

Download the Duchenne mouse dataset (GSE1025) from GEO. Extract metadata from the ExpressionSet, save it as a CSV, then extract and save the raw expression matrix.

```{r eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, cache = TRUE}
# Download the GEO ExpressionSet
filename = "GSE1025"
# Download GEO ExpressionSet using GEOquery package: retrieves both expression data and phenotype metadata
GSE1025 <- getGEO("GSE1025", GSEMatrix = TRUE) 
# Unlist the GEO download result: extract the ExpressionSet object from the list wrapper
eset <- GSE1025[[1]]

# Clean and save metadata
duchenne_metadata = eset %>% 
  pData() %>% 
# Reorder columns: place comparison/condition column first for readability
  dplyr::select( 
    geo_sample = "geo_accession", 
    subject_id = "title",
    # sex = "gender:ch1", 
    # treatment = "treatment:ch1", 
    tissue = "source_name_ch1",
    # timepoint = "timepoint:ch1",
    platform_id,
    participant_id = subject_id,
    # animal_replicate = "animal replicate:ch1",
    # strain = "strain/background:ch1"
    ) %>% 
        mutate(
          tissue = "Muscle",
          temp_col = str_to_lower(subject_id),
          treatment = case_when(
            str_detect(subject_id, "control|Control") ~ "Control",
            str_detect(subject_id, "mdx") ~ "DMD",
            T ~ NA
          )
        ) %>%
          extract(
            col = temp_col,
            into = c("timepoint", "group", "replicate"),
            regex = "leg (\\d+) day ([a-z]+) rep (\\d+)",
            convert = TRUE
          ) %>%
          mutate(
            treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "Control"),
            condition = paste(treatment, timepoint, sep = "_")
          ) %>% 
  select(!(group))

#Save
saveRDS(duchenne_metadata, file = here("tables", "duchenne_mouse_metadata.rds"))

# Extract and save expression matrix
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
eset <- exprs(eset)

#Save
eset %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "duchenne_mouse_exprs.rds"))

```

### Annotate genes

Map Agilent probe IDs to human gene symbols using Ensembl BioMart and the FIT.mouse2man orthology lookup table.

```{r}
# Set up Ensembl BioMart for mouse
ensembl_mart <- useMart("ensembl")
# Select the mouse genome (mmusculus_gene_ensembl) as the annotation dataset in BioMart
ensembl_mart <- useDataset("mmusculus_gene_ensembl", mart = ensembl_mart)

# Get probe IDs from the expression matrix
gene_id <- duchenne_exprs %>% rownames()

# List available attributes
listAttributes(ensembl_mart)

# Affymetrix Murine Genome U74A Version 2 Array

# Retrieve annotations for all probes
# Query BioMart for gene annotations (Ensembl → HGNC/MGI symbols)
annot <- getBM(
  attributes = c("affy_mg_u74av2", #Agilent microarray data (design ID 028005, retrieved from GEO)
                 "ensembl_gene_id",
                 "entrezgene_id",
                 "mgi_symbol",
                 "description"),
  filters = "affy_mg_u74av2",
  values = gene_id,
  mart = ensembl_mart)

# Load mouse-to-human orthology lookup table
library(FIT.mouse2man)

HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez = FIT.mouse2man::HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(mouse_entrez = mouse_ortholog)

# Summarise expression per probe, collapse to one row per gene
### Filter probes with highest median expression
mouse_log2summary = duchenne_exprs %>% #20,845 probes
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe") %>% 
# Reshape expression data from wide (columns = samples) to long (rows = probe × sample) format for tidyverse workflows
  pivot_longer(cols = -probe,
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "expression") %>% 
# Group by probe ID to collapse multiple probe-to-gene mappings later
  group_by(probe) %>% 
# Compute per-probe summary statistics (mean, median) across all samples to select the most representative probe
  summarise(mean = mean(expression,na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(expression, na.rm = T)) %>%  
  # Join BioMart annotation to expression data
inner_join(annot %>% 
              rename(probe = affy_mg_u74av2), 
            by = "probe") %>%  #24.009 rows
  # Collapse multiple probes per Ensembl ID (keep highest median)
  group_by(ensembl_gene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(-ensembl_gene_id) %>% 
# Remove duplicate rows: eliminates redundant probe-to-gene mappings (one probe may match multiple transcript clusters)
  distinct() %>% 
  
  # Collapse multiple Ensembl IDs per Entrez ID
  group_by(entrezgene_id) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1) %>%  #21.863 probes/entrez_ids
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(mouse_entrez = entrezgene_id) %>% 
  
  # Join human orthologs, collapse to one row per HGNC symbol
  inner_join(HS_MM_Symbol_Entrez, by = c("mouse_entrez", "mgi_symbol")) %>% 
# Group by human gene symbol: after orthology mapping, collapse mouse genes that map to the same human gene
  group_by(hgnc_symbol) %>% 
  # Keep probe with highest median expression per gene
  slice_max(median, n = 1)  %>% #14.396
  ungroup()

# Remove HGNC symbols that map to multiple MGI symbols
hgnc_symbol_dupes = mouse_log2summary %>% 
# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
  get_dupes(hgnc_symbol)

mouse_log2summary = mouse_log2summary %>% 
# Remove genes with ambiguous human symbol mappings: retains only one-to-one mouse-to-human orthologs
  filter(!hgnc_symbol %in% c(hgnc_symbol_dupes$hgnc_symbol %>% unique())) 

# Build filtered expression matrix with human gene symbols
mouse_log2_filtered_probes = duchenne_exprs %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column("probe") %>% 
# Join expression data with annotation by probe ID: adds gene symbols to raw probe-level measurements
  inner_join(mouse_log2summary, by = "probe") %>%   #214,396
  select(human_symbol = hgnc_symbol,
         probe_id = probe,
         human_entrez,
         mouse_entrez,
         c(duchenne_metadata$geo_sample))
#14395mouse_log2_filtered_probes
mouse_log2_filtered_probes %>% dim()

mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol = mouse_log2_filtered_probes 

# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% get_dupes(human_symbol)

mouse_exprs_log2fc_sample = mouse_exprs_log2fc_sample %>% 
  inner_join(mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
               select(human_symbol, probe_id),
             by = join_by(probe_id))

mouse_exprs_log2fc_sample %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "duchenne_mouse_log2fc_sample_clean_long.rds"))

#Save 
mouse_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "duchenne_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
```

### Differential gene expression

Build an ExpressionSet from the filtered gene-symbol expression matrix with quantile normalization.

```{r}
# Create ExpressionSet
# Load data
mouse_duchenne_log2_hgnc_symbol = readRDS(here("tables", "duchenne_mouse_exprs_hgnc_symbol.rds"))
mouse_duchenne_metadata = readRDS(here("tables", "duchenne_mouse_metadata.rds")) 

# Build expression matrix
duchenne_exprs_matrix = mouse_duchenne_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  select(human_symbol, c(mouse_duchenne_metadata$geo_sample)) %>% 
  column_to_rownames("human_symbol") %>% 
  as.matrix()

# Quantile normalization
duchenne_exprs_matrix_normalized <- normalizeBetweenArrays(duchenne_exprs_matrix, 
                                                                    method = "quantile")

# Diagnostics
dim(duchenne_exprs_matrix_normalized) #7367   36

# Create new ExpressionSet with normalized data
eset_filtered <- ExpressionSet(
  assayData = duchenne_exprs_matrix_normalized,
  phenoData = AnnotatedDataFrame(mouse_duchenne_metadata %>%
                                   mutate(timepoint = as.character(timepoint) %>% as.factor())))

#Save
eset_filtered %>% 
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "duchenne_mouse_eset.rds"))

```


#### Limma

Fit a linear model with array weights, duplicate correlation, and empirical Bayes moderation to identify differentially expressed genes at each timepoint vs day 0.

```{r}
# Create design matrix
eset_filtered = readRDS(file = here("tables", "duchenne_mouse_eset.rds"))

# Filter low-expressed genes (log2 > 6 in at least 5 samples)
# Extract raw expression matrix from the ExpressionSet: probes in rows, samples in columns
genes_to_keep <- exprs(eset_filtered) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ . > 6)) %>% 
  rowSums() %>% 
  { . >= 5 }

eset_filtered <- eset_filtered[genes_to_keep, ]

# Build design matrix for Limma with condition and covariates
design <- model.matrix(~ condition + 0, eset_filtered)
# Ensure syntactically valid column names: replaces spaces/special characters with dots for model.matrix compatibility
colnames(design) <- make.names(colnames(design))

# Array weights
# Calculate sample quality weights
aw <- arrayWeights(eset_filtered, design)
# Barplot of array weights: visual diagnostic to identify low-quality arrays (bars near zero indicate problematic samples)
barplot(aw, 
        names.arg = eset_filtered$condition,
        main = "Sample Weights Diagnostic", 
        ylab = "Weight", 
        las = 2,
        cex.names = 0.7,
        col = "skyblue")

# Fit linear model
# Fit linear model with array weights and duplicate correlation
fit <- lmFit(eset_filtered, 
             design, 
             weights = aw
             ) 

# Define contrasts
colnames(design) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  arrange(.)

# Define contrasts of interest (each timepoint vs baseline)
cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(conditionDMD_7  - conditionControl_7 ,
                             conditionDMD_14  - conditionControl_14 ,
                             conditionDMD_23  - conditionControl_23 ,
                             conditionDMD_28  - conditionControl_28 ,
                             conditionDMD_56  - conditionControl_56 ,
                             conditionDMD_112  - conditionControl_112 ,
                             levels=design)

# Apply contrasts to the fitted model
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont.matrix)

# Empirical Bayes moderation
# Apply empirical Bayes moderation to shrink variances
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2, trend = T, robust = T)

# Diagnostic plot: scatterplot of log2 residual variance vs average expression (should show no strong trend after moderation)
plotSA(fit2, main = "Sigma vs Abundance (Weights Applied)")

# Extract DEGs for every contrast
results_list <- lapply(1:ncol(fit2), function(i) {
  
# Extract differentially expressed genes using the treat method (tests whether log2FC exceeds a minimum threshold, not just non-zero)
  topTreat(fit2, coef = i, adjust = "fdr", p.value = 1, number = Inf, confint = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(comparison = colnames(fit2)[i]) %>% 
    rownames_to_column("symbol")
    
})

# Combine all results
all_contrasts_degs <- bind_rows(results_list)

# Clean and organise DEG table
all_degs_mouse = all_contrasts_degs %>% 
  select(comparison, everything()) %>% 
  mutate(condition = case_when(comparison == "conditionDMD_7 - conditionControl_7"	~ "DMD_Day7",
                                comparison == "conditionDMD_14 - conditionControl_14"	~ "DMD_Day14",
                               comparison == "conditionDMD_23 - conditionControl_23"	~ "DMD_Day23",
                               comparison == "conditionDMD_28 - conditionControl_28"	~ "DMD_Day28",
                               comparison == "conditionDMD_56 - conditionControl_56"	~ "DMD_Day56",
                               comparison == "conditionDMD_112 - conditionControl_112"	~ "DMD_Day112",
                                T~comparison),
         timepoint = str_remove(condition, "DMD_"),
         timepoint = str_replace(timepoint, "Day", "Day "),
         organism = "Mouse",
         treatment = "DMD",
         pathogen = "DMD",
         se = abs(logFC / t),
         #N = 3
         sd = se / sqrt(3)) %>% 
  select(condition, everything()) %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(condition, human_symbol = symbol, 
         mean_l2fc = log_fc, ci_lower = ci_l, ci_upper = ci_r, ave_expr,  everything())

# Count the number of differentially expressed genes (adj.p ≤ 0.05) per comparison
all_degs_mouse %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>%
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>%
  summarise(n_degs = n())


         
	
#Save
all_degs_mouse %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "duchenne_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))


```

### Engerix B
Load the Engerix B mouse dataset from saved RDS files.

```{r}
# Load data
all_degs_human_mouse = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds")) 
all_degs_mouse = readRDS(file = here("tables", "influenza_fluad_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

#Input
input2FIT = mouse_engerixb_log2_hgnc_symbol %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
# Join BioMart gene annotation to expression data by probe ID: adds gene symbol, Entrez ID, and description
  inner_join(annot %>% select(probe_id = agilent_sureprint_g3_ge_8x60k, 
                              MM.Entrez = entrezgene_id),
             by = "probe_id") %>% 
  select(participant_id, timepoint, MM.Entrez, EffectSize = log2fc) %>% 
  group_by(timepoint, MM.Entrez) %>% 
  summarise(mean_log2fc = mean(EffectSize, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  drop_na() %>% 
  mutate(row = MM.Entrez,
         pathogen = "Hepatitis B",
         condition = paste0(pathogen, "_D", timepoint)) %>% 
  select(row, condition, EffectSize = mean_log2fc, MM.Entrez) %>% 
  ungroup()

### Loop for every time point -----
# Generate csv for every condition
all_conditions <- unique(input2FIT$condition)
purrr::walk(all_conditions, function(cond) {
  
  delete_dupes <- input2FIT %>%
    filter(condition == cond) %>%
# Identify duplicated gene symbols: marks genes that map to multiple Entrez IDs or probes for removal
    get_dupes(row) %>%
    pull(row)
  
  filtered_df <- input2FIT %>%
    filter(condition == cond, !row %in% delete_dupes) %>%
    select(-condition) %>% 
# Move identifier column to row names: required format for ExpressionSet and Limma (matrix must have rownames)
    column_to_rownames("row") %>% 
    select(MM.Entrez, EffectSize)
  
  file_name <- paste0(cond, "_FIT_mouse.csv")
  file_path <- here("tables", file_name)
  
# Save metadata to CSV: preserves clean phenotype table for reuse without re-processing
  write_csv(filtered_df, file_path)
})

# FIT loop
fit_results_combined <- map2_dfr(all_conditions, all_conditions, function(cond, cond_name) {
  
  file_path <- here("tables", paste0(cond, "_FIT_mouse.csv"))
  
  fit_output <- FIT.mouse2man::FIT(MouseFile = file_path, DataType = "rnaseq")

  fit_output_tbl <- as_tibble(fit_output) %>%
    mutate(condition = cond_name)
  
  return(fit_output_tbl)
})
# Play notification sound: alerts that a long-running chunk has finished execution
beep()

#Print
fit_results_combined

#Save
fit_results_combined %>% saveRDS(here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_mouse_fit_prediction_alltimes.rds"))

#Pivot longer
fit_engerixb_results = fit_results_combined %>% 
# Standardise column names to snake_case using janitor::clean_names for consistent tidyverse syntax
  clean_names() %>%  
  pivot_longer(cols = c(mouse_effect_size, fit_prediction),
               names_to = "measure", 
               values_to = "value") %>% 
  mutate(pathogen = "Hepatitis B",
         vaccine = "Engerix B", 
         treatment = vaccine,
         timepoint = str_remove(condition, "Hepatitis B_D")) %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(pathogen,treatment,  timepoint, everything()) %>% 
  arrange(mouse_symbol) %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(pathogen, timepoint, everything())

#Save
fit_engerixb_results %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_fit_prediction_results_alltimes.rds"))

#Visualize distribution
fit_engerixb_results %>% 
# Create ggplot object: maps data to aesthetic (x = expression value)
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = value,
      fill = timepoint,
      color = timepoint) +
# Create faceted plot: split data into sub-panels by condition or organism for side-by-side comparison
  facet_wrap(~measure, ncol = 1) +
# Plot histogram: visualises the distribution of expression values for quality control
  geom_histogram() +
# Apply project-specific ggplot theme: consistent fonts, gridlines, and legend styling across all figures
  theme_vaxgo()
```

## Metadata
Merge all analysis results into a comprehensive dataset.

```{r}
#Merge results =====================
#Metadata
#S. aurues
human_mouse_metadata_saureus = readRDS(file = here("tables", "saureus_infection_human_mouse_metadata.rds")) %>% 
  select(geo_sample, participant_id, organism, timepoint, time_unit, pathogen, treatment, age, sex, ethnicity, strain, tissue, tissue_infection, batch = batch_experimental) %>% 
  mutate(pathogen = "S. aureus",
         tissue = "Blood",
         timepoint = as.numeric(timepoint),
         age = as.character(age)) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint = if_else(timepoint == 1, 24, timepoint),
         time_unit = "Hour") 

human_mouse_metadata_ecoli = readRDS(here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_mouse_metadata.rds")) %>% 
  filter(host_strain == "C57BL/6J" | organism == "Human",
         !batch %in% c("1", "2")) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint = as.numeric(timepoint), 
         time_unit = "Hour", 
         pathogen = "E. coli", 
         tissue = "Blood", tissue_infection = site_infection, 
         age = str_remove(age, "0.50-0.66"),
         organism = if_else(organism == "Mus musculus", "Mouse", organism)) %>% 
  select(geo_sample, participant_id = subject_id, organism, timepoint, time_unit, pathogen, treatment = status, age, sex, ethnicity, strain = host_strain,
         tissue, tissue_infection, batch) %>% 
  arrange(organism, timepoint)

human_mouse_engerix_metadata = readRDS(file = here("tables", "hepatitisb_engerixb_human_mouse_metadata.rds")) %>% 
  mutate(pathogen = "HepB",
         vaccine = "Engerix B",
       treatment = "Engerix B", 
       type = "VLP",
       timepoint = as.numeric(timepoint),
       age = as.character(age)) %>% 
  select(geo_sample, participant_id, organism, timepoint, time_unit, pathogen, vaccine, type, treatment, age, sex, ethnicity = race, strain, tissue)

fluad_human_mouse_metadata = readRDS(here("tables", "fluad_human_mouse_metadata.rds"))  %>% 
  mutate(time_unit = "Day", timepoint = as.numeric(timepoint), age = as.character(age)) %>% 
  select(geo_sample, participant_id, organism, timepoint, time_unit, pathogen, vaccine, type, treatment, age, sex, ethnicity, strain, tissue)

#Burn and Trauma
mouse_metadata_burn_trauma = read_csv(file = here("tables", "trauma_burn_mouse_metadata.csv")) %>% 
  filter(!str_detect(treatment, "LPS")) %>% 
  separate(timepoint, into = c("timepoint", "time_unit")) %>% 
  separate(treatment, into = c("pathogen", "treatment")) %>% 
  mutate(tissue = "Leukocytes",
         organism = "Mouse",
         treatment = if_else(is.na(treatment), pathogen, treatment),
         timepoint = as.numeric(timepoint)) %>% 
  select(geo_sample, participant_id, organism, timepoint, time_unit, pathogen, treatment, sex, strain, tissue)
  
#Burn
human_burn_metadata = read_csv(file = here("tables", "burn_human_metadata.csv")) %>% 
  rename(timepoint_original = timepoint,
         timepoint = timepoints_new) %>% 
  mutate(pathogen = "Burn", 
         organism = "Human",
         subject_id = if_else(subject_id == "Control", paste0(subject_id, "_", geo_sample), subject_id),
         timepoint = str_replace(timepoint, "_", " "),
         time_unit = if_else(str_detect(timepoint, "Day"), "Day", "Hour"),
         timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "Day "),
         timepoint = if_else(treatment == "Control", "0", timepoint)) %>% 
  select(geo_sample, participant_id = subject_id, organism, timepoint_original, timepoint, time_unit, pathogen, treatment, age, sex, tissue)

outliers = readRDS(file = here("tables", "trauma_human_metadata_outliers.rds"))

#Trauma
human_trauma_metadata = read_csv(file = here("tables", "trauma_human_metadata.csv")) %>% 
  rename(timepoint_original = timepoint,
         timepoint = timepoints_new) %>% 
  mutate(pathogen = "Trauma", 
         organism = "Human",
         subject_id = if_else(subject_id == "Control", paste0(subject_id, "_", geo_sample), subject_id),
         timepoint = str_replace(timepoint, "_", " "),
         time_unit = if_else(str_detect(timepoint, "Day"), "Day", "Hour"),
         timepoint = str_remove(timepoint, "Day "),
         timepoint = if_else(treatment == "Control", "0", timepoint)) %>% 
  select(geo_sample, participant_id = subject_id, organism, timepoint_original, timepoint, time_unit, pathogen, treatment, age, sex, tissue) %>% 
  #Remove outliers
  filter(!participant_id %in% c(outliers))
  

#Unite datasets
all_human_mouse_metadata = bind_rows(
  human_mouse_metadata_saureus %>% 
    mutate(timepoint = as.character(timepoint),
           age = as.numeric(age)),
  human_mouse_metadata_ecoli %>% 
    mutate(timepoint = as.character(timepoint),
           age = as.numeric(age)),
  human_mouse_engerix_metadata %>% 
    mutate(timepoint = as.character(timepoint),
           age = as.numeric(age)),
  fluad_human_mouse_metadata %>% 
    mutate(timepoint = as.character(timepoint),
           age = as.numeric(age)),
  mouse_metadata_burn_trauma %>% 
    mutate(timepoint = as.character(timepoint)),
  human_burn_metadata,
  human_trauma_metadata
) %>% 
  # Annotate timepoints
  mutate(timepoint = case_when(pathogen %in% c("Burn", "Trauma") & timepoint %in% c("2", "2h", "Early Hours") ~ "Early hours",
                               time_unit == "Day" ~ paste0("Day ", timepoint),
                               time_unit == "Hour" & timepoint != "Early hours" ~ paste0(timepoint, "h"),
                               T~timepoint),
         timepoint = fct_relevel(timepoint, "Early hours", "2h", "4h", "6h", "12h", "24h", 
                                           "Day 1", "Day 2", "Day 3", "Day 4", "Day 5", "Day 7", "Day 14", "Day 28"),
         timepoint_comparison = if_else(pathogen %in% c("Escherichia coli", "Staphylococcus aureus"),
                                        paste0(timepoint, "-", "24h"), 
                                        paste0(timepoint, "-", timepoint)) %>% 
                                str_replace(., "Early hours-Early hours", "2h-Early"),
         pathogen = case_when(pathogen == "Staphylococcus aureus" ~ "S. aureus",
                              pathogen == "Escherichia coli" ~ "E. coli",
                              pathogen == "Hepatitis B" ~ "HepB",
                              T ~ pathogen))
  

all_human_mouse_metadata %>% 
  dplyr::count(pathogen, treatment, organism, timepoint)

all_human_mouse_metadata %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "all_human_mouse_metadata.rds"))
```

```{r}
         vaccine = "Engerix B",
         timepoint = as.character(timepoint))

#S.aureus

  mutate(pathogen = "Staphylococcus aureus", treatment = "Infection")

#E coli
all_degs_human_mouse_ecoli = readRDS(here("tables", "ecoli_infection_human_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds")) %>% 
  mutate(pathogen = "Escherichia coli", treatment = "Infection")

#Burn

#Burn

all_degs_human_mouse = bind_rows(all_degs_human_mouse_saureus, 
                                 all_degs_human_mouse_ecoli,

                                 all_degs_human_mouse_engerixb,
                                 all_degs_human_mouse_burn, 
                                 all_degs_human_mouse_trauma
                                 ) %>% 
# Select all columns: ensures clean column order with key identifier first
  select(organism, pathogen, treatment, timepoint, condition, human_symbol, everything()) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint = if_else(pathogen == "Staphylococcus aureus" & timepoint == "1", "24", timepoint)) %>% 
  #Annotate timepoints
  mutate(timepoint = case_when(pathogen %in% c("Burn", "Trauma") & timepoint %in% c("2h", "Early hours")~"Early hours", 
                               pathogen %in% c("Influenza", "Hepatitis B") ~ paste0("Day ", timepoint),
                               pathogen %in% c("Escherichia coli", "Staphylococcus aureus") ~ paste0(timepoint, "h"),
                               T ~timepoint),
         timepoint = if_else(pathogen %in% c("Burn", "Trauma") & timepoint %in% c("2h", "Early hours"), "Early hours", timepoint),
        timepoint = fct_relevel(timepoint, "Early hours", "2h", "4h", "6h", "12h", "24h", 
                                           "Day 1", "Day 2", "Day 3", "Day 4", "Day 5", "Day 7", "Day 14", "Day 28")) %>% 
   mutate(pathogen = case_when(pathogen == "Staphylococcus aureus" ~ "S. aureus",
                              pathogen == "Escherichia coli" ~ "E. coli",
                              pathogen == "Hepatitis B" ~ "HepB",
                              T ~ pathogen))

#Check

all_degs_human_mouse %>%
```

Duplicate Infection timepoints
```{r}
#========================
#Duplicate to match Infection in human (24h) with different timepoints in mouse (2h, 4h, 6h, 12h, 24h) #========================

all_degs_human_mouse =
  readRDS(here("tables", "all_human_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

all_degs_human_mouse_matched = 
  bind_rows(
  #Maintain all
  all_degs_human_mouse,
    
  #Duplicate Human infection timepoints with mouse
  all_degs_human_mouse %>% 
  filter(organism == "Human",
         treatment == "Infection") %>% 
  inner_join(all_degs_human_mouse %>% 
               filter(organism == "Mouse",
                      treatment == "Infection") %>% 
               select(pathogen, timepoint) %>%
               distinct(),
             by = "pathogen") %>% 
    mutate(timepoint_comparison = paste0(timepoint.y, "-", timepoint.x)) %>% 
    rename(timepoint = timepoint.y) %>% select(-timepoint.x) 
  ) %>% 
  distinct() 

all_degs_human_mouse_matched %>% 
  filter(adj_p_val <= 0.05) %>% 
  dplyr::count(timepoint_comparison, treatment, pathogen, organism) 

all_degs_human_mouse_matched %>% 
# Save R object to disk in native RDS format: preserves data types and structure for fast loading
  saveRDS(here("tables", "all_human_mouse_dge_limma_degs_matched.rds"))
```
